title: The Bell That Must Come Down

nodes.brief: Opening: the reader is a bell-ringer's apprentice of Orisonhold, the monastery-city above the cloud line; the Great Bell Orison has cracked, and the Prioress hands over its bronze Clapper to be carried down thirteen stair-towns to the foundry at Lowgate before the ice-wind season closes the passes in twenty days.

exits.label: Lift the bronze tongue immediately and set forth

exits.intent: Ask the Prioress what she is not saying
exits.label: Demand of the Prioress what she keeps hidden

nodes.title: The Fractured Bell
nodes.page:
High above the swirling cloud line, Orisonhold clings to its mountain face like a barnacle on a ship's timber, enduring the bitter nip of thin air. In the damp nave of the upper monastery, the Great Bell Orison sits silent with a jagged fracture splitting its metallic lip from crown to sound-bow. The Prioress stands before you in her woollen habit, lined fingers gripping an iron key, and tells you that the ice-wind season will lock the mountain passes in twenty days. She commands you, as bell-ringer's apprentice, to carry the broken bronze down through the thirteen stair-towns to the foundry at Lowgate before the frost seals the world.

The cold wind whistles through the high clerestory windows, carrying the sharp scent of old tallow and frozen stone, reminding you that time is short.

nodes.brief: The reader takes the Clapper straight from the Prioress's hands; describe it (a bronze tongue as long as a forearm, heavy as a child, faintly humming) and the padded cradle, and what it is for (recasting the Great Bell at Lowgate).

exits.intent: Go to pack for the descent
exits.label: Leave the cloister and pack for the descent

nodes.title: Bearing the Bronze
nodes.page: You take the bronze tongue from the Prioress's outstretched hands and feel its strange deep warmth against your palms. It is as long as your forearm and dense as a sleeping child, and even held still it sends a faint shiver straight up into your teeth. You slide it carefully into the padded leather cradle strapped across your shoulders, adjusting the hempen buckles until the dead-weight balances evenly against your spine. This scarred fragment of Orison must reach the foundry at Lowgate to be melted and recast into a true voice for the monastery before the winter storm closes the upper trails.

nodes.brief: The reader questions the Prioress; she admits that nobody has come back up from Lowgate in a year, that the Cable Court has been buying the ropeways, and that no bell below has rung true since the master founder left. Include the description of the Clapper (a bronze tongue as long as a forearm, faintly humming) and its purpose.

exits.intent: Go to pack for the descent
exits.label: Turn away from the altar and pack for the descent

nodes.title: Questions in the Gloom
nodes.page: You hesitate before the Prioress, fixing your eyes upon her weathered face, and ask what dangers truly wait for you along the hanging stair-towns. She presses her thin lips together before admitting in a low murmur that nobody has climbed back up from Lowgate in over a full year, that the greedy Cable Court has been buying up the ropeways, and that no bell below has rung true since the master founder departed. Despite these dark warnings, she transfers the bronze tongue into your hands; it measures as long as your forearm, weighs about as much as a child, and rests cool against your chest. It must be carried down to the foundry to be recast before the mountain passes freeze solid.

nodes.brief: Packing at dawn at the cloister gate; the novices and old ringers see the reader off; the cradle on their back, a water skin, and the ninety steps down ahead.

exits.label: Step out and tread the first stair

nodes.title: Dawn at the Gate
nodes.page: Dawn breaks over the cloister gate in a pale streak of saffron light while the older ringers and sleepy novices gather to see you off into the biting frost. You hitch the padded cradle on your shoulders and check that the bronze tongue is lashed tight beside your spare water skin and dried rye biscuits. Ninety sheer stone steps stretch down from the threshold into the churning grey mist, marking the beginning of the long, perilous road to the lowlands. The watchers offer quiet nods and silent prayers, their breath pluming white in the freezing air as you prepare to cross the threshold.

nodes.brief: Arrival in Orisonhold and the Ninety Steps: the cliff-monastery, its bell-towers and mule yards; outfitting, kin and rivals; the reader takes the Clapper and chooses a companion and a rope; the first stairs down. The reader enters with several ways forward.

exits.label: Follow the wide main stair downward
Cut across the steep lower ledges

exits.intent: Ask the way of a stranger
exits.label: Ask the way of an old stranger
Take the hidden carriers' path

nodes.title: The Ninety Steps
nodes.page: You stand at the threshold of Orisonhold where the sheer limestone cliff drops away into an endless sea of tumbling clouds and screaming gulls. The monastery's stone bell-towers pierce the grey sky above, while the mule yards bustle with anxious drovers shouting hoarse instructions across the frozen cobbles. Your shoulders ache already under the cradled weight of the bronze tongue, and you must choose how to begin the long descent through the clifftops. Kin and rivals eye your burden from the shelter of the butter-lamp alcoves, each with their own advice on which path to trust when the mountain wind turns sour.

nodes.brief: Mandatory scene at the Mule Yard: the reader decides whether to take Biscuit, a stubborn mule who knows the stairs, or to go alone and light

exits.intent: Take Biscuit the mule to carry the pack
exits.label: Take Biscuit the mule to carry the pack

exits.intent: Go down on foot, alone and light
exits.label: Go down on foot, alone and light

nodes.title: The Departure Choice
nodes.page: Standing within the bustling courtyard of the mule yard, you face the central dilemma of your descent toward Lowgate. The bronze Clapper rests heavily in its frame, a demanding load that will test every joint and sinew on the thousand-meter drop. You can accept the company of Biscuit, a famously stubborn grey mule who knows every icy turn of the stairs but requires constant cajoling, or you can shoulder the entire burden yourself and take the narrow foot-path alone in the freezing mist.

nodes.brief: Mandatory scene at the Rope Store: the reader decides whether to sign for a Guild rope (strong, with the Guild's protection and obligations) or carry their own worn rope

exits.intent: Sign for a Ropewrights' Guild rope
exits.label: Sign for a Ropewrights' Guild rope
Trust your own old rope

nodes.title: The Rope Store
nodes.page: The smell of cold tar and beaten flax fills the low-beamed timber warehouse where Master Orem weighs every coil on rusted scales. You face a hard choice for the descent ahead. You can swear the Guild oath and bind your waist with their branded hemp, gaining the protection of the cable-makers along the vertical drop, or you can rely solely on your own frayed and trusted line, keeping your independence at the cost of safety.

nodes.brief: Leaving Orisonhold and the Ninety Steps for The Rope Markets: close this part of the journey.

exits.label: Push onward into the noisy bazaars

nodes.title: Leaving The Ninety Steps
nodes.page:
Leaving Orisonhold and the Ninety Steps for The Rope Markets, you tighten the straps across your chest and lean forward into the biting wind that sweeps up the cliff. The stone stairs grow narrower here, replaced by suspended wooden galleries and swaying rope bridges that bridge the yawning chasms between the upper monastery and the bustling trade tiers below. Every breath burns your throat with the crisp clean edge of high altitude air, and the Clapper keeps a soft beat against your spine.

The chaotic din of the markets rises through the mist, promising trade, hazard, and the next stretch of your long descent.

nodes.brief: In the frost-rimed belfry of Orisonhold, you hoist the bronze Clapper into its harness while Orison's fractured lip weeps cold grease onto your knuckles.

exits.label: Step out onto the wind-whipped stone balcony.
Slip past the buttery for a stolen rye crust.
Clear the frozen rime from your boot-soles by the salt-bins.

nodes.title: The Bronze Tongue
nodes.page: In the frost-rimed belfry of Orisonhold, you hoist the bronze Clapper into its harness while Orison's fractured lip weeps cold grease onto your knuckles. The metal tongue sits against your spine, as big as a sleeping child and smelling of old rain. Outside, the high mountain wind rattles the slate roofs and spits dry sleet across the stone sill.

nodes.brief: Beneath the echoing bronze ribs of Orison, you swab copper dust from your woollen sleeves before shouldering the heavy metal tongue for its long descent.

exits.label: Pause by the salt-bins to clear your boots
Dodge the swinging buckets in the choir-loft
Rest your spine against the warm chimney

nodes.title: Copper Dust
nodes.page: Beneath the echoing bronze ribs of Orison, you swab copper dust from your woollen sleeves before shouldering the heavy metal tongue for its long descent. The cold air bites at your cheeks, carrying the sharp tang of mountain lichen and woodsmoke from the warming braziers near the lower cloisters. Around you, novices scurry through the shadows with tallow buckets and iron scrapers, intent on their morning chores before the great frost sets in for the day. You check the leather buckles of your cradle one last time, listening to the faint, continuous hum emanating from the bronze against your back.

nodes.brief: By the monastery's butter-lamp alcove, you check the hempen straps of your carrying cradle while the dawn wind rattles the frozen iron wind-vanes above.

exits.label: Cross the quiet library garth
Splash freezing water by the cisterns
Tighten your belt in the dormitory

nodes.title: The Butter-Lamp Alcove
nodes.page: By the monastery's butter-lamp alcove, you check the hempen straps of your carrying cradle while the dawn wind rattles the frozen iron wind-vanes above. The flickering yellow flames cast long, dancing shadows across the whitewashed stone walls, smelling faintly of rendered mutton fat and dried rosemary. Your muscles tighten with anticipation as you feel the dead-weight of the Clapper shifting slightly against your shoulder-blades with every breath you take. Several paths lie open before you, leading either through the quiet library garth or past the deep stone cisterns where the mountain water runs black and cold.

nodes.brief: Within the dim sacristy, you trade your greasy apprentice smock for a stout dyer's jacket while the cathedral bells toll a low, muffled warning for the frost.

exits.label: Tighten your belt among the sleeping pallets
Step out into the freezing outer gatehouse
Warm your fingers by the brazier pit

nodes.title: The Sacristy Threshold
nodes.page: Within the dim sacristy, you trade your greasy apprentice smock for a stout dyer's jacket while the cathedral bells toll a low, muffled warning for the frost. The heavy wool keeps out the worst of the draft, but the iron Clapper in its harness remains as cold as a river stone against your spine. Through the narrow door, you can see the white vapour of fellow apprentices breathing into their cupped hands as they gather near the outer gatehouse. The time for preparation is over, and the mountain demands an immediate answer from anyone bold enough to carry its broken voice downward.

nodes.brief: Staggering onto the frost-slicked balcony, you feel the Clapper's bronze dead-weight shift against your shoulder-blades as the cloud-sea boils below the limestone sills.

exits.label: Enter the damp gloom of the rope-loft
Seek out Mistress Garrow in the buttery

nodes.title: The Balcony Edge
nodes.page: Staggering onto the frost-slicked balcony, you feel the Clapper's bronze dead-weight shift against your shoulder-blades as the cloud-sea boils below the limestone sills. The wind catches at the hem of your coat, howling an ancient mountain tune that threatens to pull you off balance if you do not plant your boots firmly. Down in the courtyard, the rope-loft door swings back and forth on rusted iron hinges, while across the corridor, Mistress Garrow prepares her morning rations for the travelers. Every breath tastes of iron and rime, urging you to choose your next step with absolute care.

nodes.brief: Passing the high buttery, you snatch a crust of rye bread from a wicker tray while old Brother Thomas mutters a prayer for the valley road.

exits.label: Inspect the tarred cordage in the rope-loft
Follow the cart ruts along the curtain wall

nodes.title: The High Buttery Threshold
nodes.page: Passing the high buttery, you snatch a crust of rye bread from a wicker tray while old Brother Thomas mutters a short prayer for the valley road. The coarse crumb sticks in your dry throat, tasting faintly of caraway and cellar dust. Outside the narrow lancet window, the mountain mist coils against the leaded glass like white wool.

nodes.brief: Near the salt-bins, you pause to scrape rime from your boot-soles while the iron Clapper hums a dull, shivering note against your spine.

exits.label: Follow the cart ruts along the curtain wall
Face the bailiff by the winch-tower

nodes.title: Beside the Salt Bins
nodes.page: Near the salt-bins, you pause to scrape rime from your boot-soles while the iron Clapper hums a dull, shivering note against your spine. The white grains crunch under your heels, dry and bitter-smelling in the freezing draft that sweeps up from the lower gorges. You shift the padded cradle, trying to find a balance before the long descent begins.

nodes.brief: Ducking under the low arch of the choir-loft, you dodge a swinging tallow-bucket while the novice-master shouts last-minute cautions about the wind-slips on the stair.

exits.label: Accept the dried plums and press onward
Brace against the glacier gust and stride ahead
Thread past the sheep pens and the crooked stick

nodes.title: Choir-Loft Exit
nodes.page: Sweeping under the low timber of the choir-loft, you dodge a swinging tallow-bucket as the novice-master bellows final warnings about sudden wind-slips on the upper stair. The bronze tongue in its padded cradle knocks against your spine, keeping time with the pounding of your heart. Ahead lie the stone thresholds leading down the mountain face, and you must decide how to begin your descent.

nodes.brief: In the south cloister walk, you press your back against the warm stone chimney to ease the shoulder strap before tackling the vertical drop.

exits.label: Head past the sheep-dip pens and the shepherd
Receive the pewter charm of St. Jude for safety
Sidestep the rolling pine logs in the charcoal yard

nodes.title: South Cloister Rest
nodes.page: Pressing your back against the warm stone of the cloister chimney, you ease the biting canvas shoulder strap before tackling the vertical drop. The air smells of old lime mortar and woodsmoke drifting from the refectory. Around you, the monastery walls seem to contract, urging you outward into the freezing light of the high tiers.

nodes.brief: Crossing the library garth, you watch jackdaws wheeling through the grey rime while the bronze tongue in your cradle taps a steady, rhythmic tattoo against your ribs.

exits.label: Lean hard against the glacier gale in the courtyard
Pass the sheep pens toward the lower stone path
Pocket the pewter charm by the frozen fountain

nodes.title: Crossing the Library Garth
nodes.page: Crossing the library garth, you watch jackdaws wheeling through the grey rime while the bronze tongue in your cradle taps a steady, rhythmic tattoo against your ribs. The frozen turf snaps crisply beneath your boots with every stride. Frost feathers cling to the copper sundial in the centre of the lawn, pointing silently toward the west.

nodes.brief: Pausing by the rain-cisterns, you splash freezing water over your wrists to clear the workshop sleep from your eyes before the descent begins.

exits.label: Dodge the rolling timber in the charcoal yard
Adjust the canvas rain-hood over your precious cradle
Skirt the steaming heap of slaking stone by the lime-kiln

nodes.title: Cistern Awakening
nodes.page: Splashing freezing cistern water over your wrists, you scrub away the last traces of workshop sleep before the long descent begins. Frost crusts the edges of the stone basin, and the distant clatter of mule gear echoes off the cliff face. You hitch the bronze clapper on your back until it settles between your shoulder blades.

nodes.brief: Under the stone vaulting of the Great Dormitory, you tighten your leather waist-belt while fellow apprentices murmur quiet bets on whether you will reach Lowgate intact.

exits.label: Skirt the steaming lime-kiln and the white dust
Walk past the screeching hawk at the cliff-mews

nodes.title: Dormitory Murmurs
nodes.page: Tightening your leather waist-belt beneath the stone vaulting of the Great Dormitory, you listen to fellow apprentices murmuring quiet wagers on whether you will reach Lowgate intact. The air is thick with the scent of wool grease and old straw pallets. Every eye in the dim hall watches to see how you shoulder the burden of the broken Orison.

nodes.brief: Standing on the threshold of the outer gatehouse, you watch the white vapour of your breath dissolve into the high mountain air before stepping onto the stones.

exits.label: Pass the steaming heap of slaking stone
Glance at the hooded mountain hawk in the mews
Brush the dry snow from the gate-saint's stone beard

nodes.title: Outer Threshold
nodes.page: Watching the white vapour of your breath dissolve into the high mountain air, you stand upon the threshold of the outer gatehouse before committing to the stone steps. The wind carries a sharp hint of pine resin and coming snow from the upper peaks. Your boots find purchase on the frozen flags as you take the final measure of the monastery walls behind you.

nodes.brief: Beside the brazier-pit, you warm your stiffened fingers over glowing charcoal while the master bell-founder watches you with a critical, squinting eye.

exits.label: Brush the drift of dry snow from the gate-saint

nodes.title: Brazier Warmth
nodes.page: Warming your stiffened fingers over the glowing charcoal of the brazier-pit, you catch the master bell-founder watching you with a critical, squinting eye. The bitter mountain draft curls around the stone pillars, carrying the metallic tang of hot slag and quenching oil. No words are spoken, for the weight on your shoulders tells the master all he needs to know about your readiness.

nodes.brief: Entering the damp gloom of the rope-loft, you smell tarred hemp and mutton tallow while Master Hobb dangles a hank of three-ply cordage for your inspection.

exits.label: Step out onto the stone platform of the Ninety Steps
Dodge the sliding slate at the butter-stores corner

nodes.title: Rope-Loft Gloom
nodes.page: Inhaling the thick aroma of tarred hemp and mutton tallow, you step into the damp gloom of the rope-loft as Master Hobb dangles a hank of three-ply cordage for your inspection. The low ceiling creaks under coiled cables stacked overhead, and distant wind screaming through the mountain gorges fills the shadowy corners.

nodes.brief: In the buttery corridor, Mistress Garrow shoves a greasy tallow-skin into your coat-pocket with strict orders to grease your boot-seams before the middle stairs.

exits.label: Descend the stone steps
Dodge the sliding roof-slate
Tighten your pack breast-harness

nodes.title: The Greasy Tallow-Skin
nodes.page:
Mistress Garrow shoves a greasy tallow-skin into your coat-pocket with strict orders to grease your boot-seams before the middle stairs. The buttery corridor smells heavily of soured milk and damp flagstones, a stale refuge against the howling drafts outside. You finger the stoppered leather flask, wondering if the grease will hold back the slush of the lower runs or merely attract the mountain grit.

Weighing your next move, you consider the icy drop awaiting you beyond the walls.

nodes.brief: Beside the north curtain wall, you watch iron-shod cart wheels crack the frozen ruts while a teamster curses his stumbling mare on the slope.

exits.label: Step out onto the platform
Catch your breath near the mast

nodes.title: Frozen Ruts and Carts
nodes.page:
Iron-shod cart wheels crack the frozen ruts beside the north curtain wall while a teamster curses his stumbling mare on the slope. The beast's breath plumes white against the dark grey granite of Orisonhold, and the weight of your burden pulls sharply at your shoulders. You brace the bronze Clapper in its padded cradle and match your stance to the shudder of the mountain wind.

The cart groans forward, clearing a narrow path for your descent.

nodes.brief: Under the shadow of the winch-tower, a Cable Court bailiff blocks your path to demand a toll-token for the bronze you carry down to the valley.

exits.label: Sidestep the falling roof-slate
Secure the heavy leather straps
Test your grip on the ice

nodes.title: The Cable Court Toll
nodes.page:
Under the shadow of the winch-tower, a Cable Court bailiff blocks your path to demand a toll-token for the bronze you carry down to the valley. His brass-trimmed badge catches the pale mountain glare, and his hand rests casually upon a heavy ledger. You shift your stance, feel the metal tap faintly against your spine, and weigh a sharp reply against compliance.

The wind whistles through the iron pulleys overhead, urging you to decide.

nodes.brief: At the junction of the upper lych-gate, a terrace miller thrusts a bag of dried plums into your pouch, begging news of barley prices in Lowgate.

exits.label: Walk toward the cider-press
Drink the warm herb-wine
Pass the iron-plated postern

nodes.title: Plums and Barley Prices
nodes.page:
A terrace miller thrusts a bag of dried plums into your pouch at the junction of the upper lych-gate, begging news of barley prices in Lowgate. Her fingers are calloused from years of tending high-altitude wind-crops, and her eyes betray the quiet hunger of the terraces. You nod noncommittally, tucking the sweet fruit close to your ribs while the bitter air bites your cheeks.

The path splits before you into shadow and frost.

nodes.brief: In the open courtyard, a gust of wind off the glacier nearly lifts you from your boots, forcing you to lean your heavy frame into the rock-face.

exits.label: Move past the old cider-press
Accept the lay brother's cup

nodes.title: The Glacier Gust
nodes.page:
A sudden gust off the glacier nearly lifts you from your boots in the open courtyard, and you plant your frame against the rock-face. As the pressure shifts, the bronze Clapper deepens its note against your spine and answers the vast emptiness of the precipice below. You wait out the squall with your gloved hands clawed into the limestone crevices.

The gale subsides just enough for you to pick a route.

nodes.brief: Passing the sheep-dip pens, you smell wet fleece and dung while an old shepherd waves a crooked hazel stick toward the grey stairs below.

exits.label: Head past the black lantern
Inspect the frozen drainage sluice
Turn back to the bell-loft

nodes.title: Sheep-Dip and Crooked Wood
nodes.page:
Wet fleece and dung fill the air as you pass the sheep-dip pens, where an old shepherd waves a crooked hazel stick toward the grey stairs below. The animals crowd against the wooden hurdles, steaming in the morning chill while their bells clatter a dull accompaniment to your thoughts. You glance down the winding stone track, measuring the distance to the first cloud-bank.

The shepherd turns back to his flock without a word more.

nodes.brief: By the frozen fountain, a nervous novice presses a pewter charm of St. Jude into your palm to ward off the rock-slides on the Ninety Steps.

exits.label: Find the goat-path shortcut
Follow the iced drainage grating
Pull your muffler higher up
Turn back to the bell-loft

nodes.title: Pewter Charm on Stone
nodes.page:
A nervous novice presses a pewter charm of St. Jude into your palm by the frozen fountain to ward off the rock-slides on the Ninety Steps. The metal is bitterly cold against your skin, stamped with the crude image of a fisherman and a heavy oar. You slip the trinket into your mitten, offering a brief, silent nod to the boy before looking down the dizzying drop.

The fountain ice cracks with a sharp, pistol-like report.

nodes.brief: In the charcoal-burner's yard, soot-stained lads roll pine logs through the slush while you sidestep a rolling roundwood with the heavy Clapper swaying.

exits.label: Walk past the iron postern
Check the frozen drainage sluice

nodes.title: Charcoal-Burner's Yard
nodes.page:
Soot-stained lads roll pine logs through the slush in the charcoal-burner's yard while you sidestep a rolling roundwood and the Clapper sways on your back. The sweet, acrid scent of charred wood cuts through the biting mountain air, clinging to your woollen tunic. You keep your balance on the slick mud, eyes fixed on the narrow exit between the stacked timber cribs.

The lads shout a rough warning as another log breaks loose.

nodes.brief: Under the timber pentice of the buttery stores, you adjust the canvas rain-hood over your cradle to shield the bronze tongue from dripping icicles.

exits.label: Hide behind the salt-store wall
Inspect the frayed mooring-ring

nodes.title: Canvas and Icicles
nodes.page:
You adjust the canvas rain-hood over your cradle under the timber pentice of the buttery stores to shield the bronze tongue from dripping icicles. Water droplets strike the heavy cloth with dull ticks like a clock running down, while the metal within answers with a faint, sympathetic tremor. You secure the drawstrings with numb fingers, checking the lashings one last time.

The path ahead drops sharply into the grey haze.

nodes.brief: Beside the lime-kiln, white dust coats your boots as you skirt a steaming heap of slaking stone while the mountain air bites your ears.

exits.label: Watch the kitten on the sled
Examine the high mule-track ring

nodes.title: Lime-Kiln Dust
nodes.page:
White lime dust coats your boots as you skirt a steaming heap of slaking stone beside the kiln, while the mountain air bites your ears. The heat from the pit radiates against your freezing side, a brief and deceptive comfort before the long cold descent. You cough once against the alkaline haze, wiping your spectacles with a frosted sleeve.

The trail continues past the smoking enclosure into the wind.

nodes.brief: At the head of the cliff-mews, a caged mountain hawk screeches as you pass, its hood fluttering against the leather strap in the grey wind.

exits.label: Follow the high mule-track junction
Step past the fish-hurdles toward the stairs

nodes.title: The Hawk Mews
nodes.page: At the head of the cliff-mews, a caged mountain hawk screeches as you pass, its hood fluttering against the leather strap in the grey wind. You adjust your grip on the carrying frame while the bronze Clapper answers against your shoulder blades, vibrating through your coat in the thin air. The mountain gale smells of old snow and wet feathers, sweeping down from the jagged peaks above Orisonhold to test your balance on the narrow flagstones.

nodes.brief: In the alcove of the gate-saint, you brush a drift of dry snow from the stone saint's beard while the bronze Clapper hums softly against your shoulder.

exits.label: Inspect the granite mooring-ring ahead
Head toward the timber drying racks

nodes.title: The Gate-Saint
nodes.page: In the alcove of the gate-saint, you brush a drift of dry snow from the stone saint's beard while the bronze Clapper hums softly against your shoulder. The carved granite face of the protector stares blankly out over the cloud line, indifferent to the freezing draft funneling through the stone arches. You hitch the harness padding aside to ease the dead load pressing against your spine, then pick your route down.

nodes.brief: Stepping out onto the stone platform of the Ninety Steps, you peer down into the swirling mist where the first stair-flight vanishes into white nothingness.

exits.label: Descend the frozen granite gradient
Touch the abbot's niche for luck

nodes.title: The Ninety Steps
nodes.page: Stepping out onto the stone platform of the Ninety Steps, you peer down into the swirling mist where the first stair-flight vanishes into white nothingness. The mountain wind howls off the glacier face and tries to tip you as you brace the bronze tongue in its padded cradle. Below you, the staircase drops away into the abyss of cloud and rock, demanding total concentration with every boot-heel placement.

nodes.brief: At the corner of the butter-stores, you dodge a sliding avalanche of roof-slate while your boots skid briefly on the black ice of the landing.

exits.label: Take the frozen iron hand-rail down

nodes.title: The Butter-Stores
nodes.page: At the corner of the butter-stores, you dodge a sliding avalanche of roof-slate while your boots skid briefly on the black ice of the landing. The bitter cold bites sharply at your fingers as you catch yourself against the rough-hewn stone wall, keeping the Clapper balanced behind your neck. A second rattle of falling tiles reminds you that lingering here is as dangerous as the descent itself.

nodes.brief: Beside the wind-whistle mast, brass weather-gauges spin wildly in the draft while you catch your breath against the jagged limestone parapet.

exits.label: Grip the frozen iron hand-rail
Catch your balance near the third landing

nodes.title: The Weather-Gauges
nodes.page: Beside the wind-whistle mast, brass weather-gauges spin wildly in the draft while you catch your breath against the jagged limestone parapet. The metallic shriek of the spinning instruments meets the deep tone of the Clapper against your back. Together they make an odd chord in the high-altitude air. You tighten your grip on the carrying straps and scan the precipitous drop for a safe footing.

nodes.brief: In the lee of the buttery gable, you tighten the breast-harness of your pack as the bronze Clapper gives a heavy, dead lurch against your spine.

exits.label: Slide carefully along the damp cliff-face
Brush the mossy stone of the abbot's niche

nodes.title: The Buttery Gable
nodes.page: Under the buttery gable you tighten the breast-harness of your pack, and the bronze Clapper gives a dead lurch against your spine. The wooden wall offers a brief shelter from the biting gusts sweeping across the upper courtyards of Orisonhold. You prepare yourself for the exposed stretch of stairs waiting just beyond the timber corner.

nodes.brief: Near the old cider-press, frozen apple pulp clings to the cobblestones while you test the grip of your iron-nailed heels on the steep slope.

exits.label: Pass the mossy stone of the first abbot
Pad the lower rim with extra felt
Keep your eyes fixed on the stone riband

nodes.title: The Old Cider-Press
nodes.page: Near the old cider-press, frozen apple pulp clings to the cobblestones while you test the grip of your iron-nailed heels on the steep slope. The air smells faintly of fermented peel and mountain frost, sharp enough to make your eyes water as you adjust the weight of the bronze tongue on your back. Choosing your path carefully among the frozen debris, you look for the clearest way down the upper terraces.

nodes.brief: Under the carved lintel of the porter's lodge, an old lay brother hands you a horn cup of bitter herb-wine to steady your nerves for the stairs.

exits.label: Add extra felt padding to the rim
Walk toward the narrow stone riband

nodes.title: The Porter's Lodge
nodes.page: Under the carved lintel of the porter's lodge, an old lay brother hands you a horn cup of bitter herb-wine to steady your nerves for the stairs. The warm spirit burns pleasantly in your chest, cutting through the mountain chill as you secure the canvas rain-hood over the Clapper's cradle. With a brief nod of farewell to the silent porter, you step out toward the edge of the abyss.

nodes.brief: By the iron-plated postern, a frost-blackened lantern swings in its bracket, casting long, jittery shadows across the slippery limestone flagstones.

exits.label: Recover your balance near the third landing
Pause to check the lower rim padding

nodes.title: The Postern Gate
nodes.page: By the iron-plated postern, a frost-blackened lantern swings in its bracket, casting long, jittery shadows across the slippery limestone flagstones. Metal creaks in the rising wind and keeps time with the low note of the bronze Clapper resting against your coat. You pull your wool scarf tighter around your throat and steady your footing on the rimed stone.

nodes.brief: At the head of the goat-path shortcut, you kick away a pile of wind-blown twigs to find the frozen edge of the stone-cut track.

exits.label: Touch the mossy stone of the abbot's niche
Fix your gaze on the narrow stone riband

nodes.title: The Goat-Path
nodes.page: At the head of the goat-path shortcut, you kick away a pile of wind-blown twigs to find the frozen edge of the stone-cut track. The narrow path winds steeply down between jagged outcrops of grey rock, offering a quicker but far more treacherous descent than the main stair-flights. You lean forward into the slope, letting the heavy Clapper's weight settle squarely over your center of gravity.

nodes.brief: Beside the drainage sluice, yellow ice coats the iron grating while water gurgles sluggishly through the dark masonry under your boots.

exits.label: Descend toward the lower mule yard
Cut across toward the stone chimneys

nodes.title: The Sluice Gate
nodes.page: Beside the drainage sluice, yellow ice coats the iron grating while water gurgles sluggishly through the dark masonry under your boots. The bronze Clapper shifts in its padded cradle, cold metal pressing into your shoulder blades against the bite of the mountain air. You test the grip of your left heel on the rimed stone, deciding whether to press directly toward the lower courts or loop back around the outer wall.

nodes.brief: In the shelter of the salt-store wall, you pull your woollen muffler higher across your nose to keep out the biting needle-wind off the glacier.

exits.label: Face the downdraft on the upper ledge
Head down toward the steaming mule yard

nodes.title: The Salt-Store Shelter
nodes.page: In the shelter of the salt-store wall, you pull your woollen muffler higher across your nose to keep out the biting needle-wind off the glacier. Grains of fine frost drift across the packed snow, stinging your exposed cheeks as you adjust the heavy straps of your carrying frame. The weight is balanced, but the descent ahead promises steeper pitches and deeper shadows where the cliff-face curves away into the grey vapor.

nodes.brief: Near the broken mounting-block, a stray orange kitten watches you from a sled-runner with unblinking yellow eyes through the drifting rime.

exits.label: Walk toward the distant stone chimneys
Step down to the lower terrace landing

nodes.title: The Broken Block
nodes.page: Near the broken mounting-block, a stray orange kitten watches you from a sled-runner with unblinking yellow eyes through the drifting rime. You hitch the Clapper on your back and feel its familiar low knock against your spine as the animal blinks slowly against the cold. The path forks ahead between the shuttered grain-store and the steep, frost-rimed descent toward the terrace level.

nodes.brief: At the junction of the high mule-track, you pause to inspect a frayed mooring-ring set deep into the granite face by the old road-makers.

exits.label: Follow the narrow shelf into the wind
Make for the haze of the mule yard

nodes.title: The Frayed Ring
nodes.page: At the junction of the high mule-track, you pause to inspect a frayed mooring-ring set deep into the granite face by the old road-makers. Long-frozen strands of hemp curl outward from the iron eye, grey with age and brittle under your leather-gloved thumb. You glance down the winding track where the cloud layer hides the lower steps, weighing whether to brave the open shelf or seek shelter near the upper wall.

nodes.brief: By the timber drying racks, empty fish-hurdles rattle in the draft while you shoulder the Clapper and step firmly onto the head of the stair.

exits.label: Brace against the sharp downdraft
Drop down to the terrace landing
Turn back toward the cloisters

nodes.title: The Timber Racks
nodes.page: By the timber drying racks, empty fish-hurdles rattle in the draft while you shoulder the Clapper and step firmly onto the head of the stair. The world below drops away into a thick floor of white cloud, broken only by the jagged tips of the lower chimney-stacks and the dark thread of the cable-ways. You can push onward into the descent, turn back toward the warmth of the cloisters, or seek the lower terrace gates.

nodes.brief: Descending the initial granite gradient, you grip the frozen iron hand-rail as your boots strike the first of the Ninety Steps with a hollow ring.

exits.label: Approach the heavy oak mule yard doors
Wait in the freezing stable draft

nodes.title: The Ninety Steps
nodes.page: Descending the initial granite gradient, you grip the frozen iron hand-rail as your boots strike the first of each of the Ninety Steps with a hollow ring. The bronze Clapper taps rhythmically against your pack-frame, keeping a stubborn time against the whistle of the draft. Below you, the stone steps vanish into the milky grey of the cloud-deck, leaving only the cold iron and your own breath for company.

nodes.brief: Slipping on a patch of black frost near the third landing, you catch your balance against the damp cliff-face with a sharp intake of breath.

exits.label: Head directly for the high mule yard
Step toward the stable entrance draft

nodes.title: The Third Landing
nodes.page: Slipping on a patch of black frost near the third landing, you catch your balance against the damp cliff-face with a sharp intake of breath. The bronze tongue shifts in its cradle and nearly throws you off balance unless you plant your feet at once. You catch your breath, wipe your palm on your woollen trousers, and look toward the paths diverging through the mist.

nodes.brief: Passing a niche carved with the image of the first abbot, you touch the mossy stone for luck before plunging deeper into the mountain shadow.

exits.label: Peer through the mule yard wicket-gate
Rest your load by the mounting-block

nodes.title: The Abbot's Niche
nodes.page: Passing a niche carved with the image of the first abbot, you touch the mossy stone for luck before plunging deeper into the mountain shadow. The stone saint's weathered features are choked with rime, his carved blessing worn down by centuries of driving sleet and frozen spray. You settle the Clapper on your spine and face the next steep stretch of the descent.

nodes.brief: Hearing the iron Clapper resonate against your carrying frame, you pause to pad the lower rim with an extra fold of greasy wool.

exits.label: Watch the grooms through the wicket
Rest the bronze against the stone block

nodes.title: The Extra Fold
nodes.page: Hearing the iron Clapper resonate against your carrying frame, you pause to pad the lower rim with an extra fold of greasy wool. The muffled thud satisfies you and kills the bronze chatter that has lived in your teeth since you left the bell-tower. With the load secured against the jarring stone, you scan the mist for the familiar low buildings of the staging post.

nodes.brief: Stepping around a heap of wind-shattered pine boughs, you keep your eyes fixed on the narrow riband of stone winding down toward the mule yard.

exits.label: Weigh the merits of the stable entrance

nodes.title: The Pine Boughs
nodes.page: Stepping around a heap of wind-shattered pine boughs, you keep your eyes fixed on the narrow riband of stone winding down toward the mule yard. The sharp scent of resin cuts momentarily through the freezing air, reminding you of the warmer valleys far below the cloud line. You check the lashings of your pack before taking the next curving flight of steps.

nodes.brief: A sudden downdraft from the upper cirque tears at your collar, almost spinning you around on the narrow, sheer-drop tread of the stair.

exits.label: Duck into the cleft of stone

nodes.title: The Upper Cirque
nodes.page: Frigid gales barrel down from the upper cirque, catching the hem of your coat and threatening to spin you clean off the narrow, sheer-drop tread of the mountain stair. The bronze Clapper hums softly against your spine, vibrating with every shiver of your frame as you lock your boots into the frozen ruts. Frost rims your eyelashes, and below your dangling heels, the cloud sea churns in a pale, silent abyss.

nodes.brief: Catching sight of the mule yard's stone chimneys through the grey vapor, you lengthen your stride as the weight of the bronze tongue burns your shoulders.

exits.label: Sneak past the outer grooming stalls
Approach the main timber loading dock
Take the sheltered servants' side alley

nodes.title: Smoke Over the Yard
nodes.page:
Gray vapor parts just enough to reveal the stout stone chimneys of the mule yard, drawing a fresh wave of exhaustion through your aching muscles as the weight of the bronze tongue burns your shoulders. Puffs of steam rise from the stables below, carrying the sharp scent of wet straw, old dung, and wood smoke over the cliff edge. You adjust the grease-soaked padding of your carrying frame, listening to the muffled clatter of hooves on cobbles through the fog.

Three distinct paths beckon from this snowy threshold, each leading deeper into the complex before the long descent truly begins.

nodes.brief: Bracing your knees against the downward plunge, you reach the lower terrace landing where the stable-gates loom large through the drifting mountain fog.

exits.label: Knock heavily on the main oak portal
Inspect the side latch near the fodder shed

nodes.title: The Lower Landing
nodes.page: Knees braced against the steep downward plunge, you reach the lower terrace landing where the stable-gates loom large through the drifting mountain fog. Frost crusted on the massive iron bolts glitters in the dim light filtering through the cloud layer. You can hear the low, rhythmic thrum of the Great Bell's memory still vibrating faintly through the mountain rock beneath your soles, urging you onward toward the descent. A choice of approach hangs before you in the damp air.

nodes.brief: Standing before the heavy oak doors of the high mule yard, you listen to the rhythmic stamping of iron-shod hooves on frozen cobbles within.

exits.label: Push forward into the stable yard

nodes.title: The High Mule Yard
nodes.page: Oak doors of the high mule yard open on rhythmic work as iron-shod hooves stamp frozen cobbles inside the enclosure. The dry scent of barley chaff and animal sweat hangs thick in the drafty space, offering a brief shelter from the biting external wind. Inside, stable-hands move between shadowy stalls with lanterns held high, checking girths and smoothing blankets. You stand with your heavy burden, weighing the best way to announce your arrival to the yard-master.

nodes.brief: Peering through the wicket-gate of the mule yard, you watch grooms breathlessly brush crusted snow from the flanks of shivering pack-beasts.

exits.label: Step through and announce your errand

nodes.title: Wicket Gate Watch
nodes.page: Wicket-gate in the weathered timber wall frames grooms who breathlessly brush crusted snow and rime from the flanks of shivering pack-beasts. The air smells of wet wool and burning peat, warm enough to sting your frozen cheeks as you peer into the bustling enclosure. A few drivers toss sharp words back and forth while securing heavy leather packs to wooden frames. You clutch the straps of your own burden, wondering if help or hindrance waits beyond the gate.

nodes.brief: Waiting in the freezing draft outside the stable entrance, you weigh the merits of taking a stubborn mule against the lonely peril of the foot-stairs.

exits.label: Enter the stable to find a beast

nodes.title: The Freezing Draft
nodes.page: Freezing draft sweeps across the threshold of the stable entrance, biting straight through your woollen tunic while you weigh the merits of taking a stubborn mule against the lonely peril of the foot-stairs. Downward travel on foot promises speed and absolute self-reliance, but the iron tongue grows heavier with every hundred heartbeats. Beside you, the distant clang of iron horseshoes on stone reminds you of the alternative waiting inside the warm, crowded pens.

nodes.brief: Rest the bronze Clapper against the mounting-block of the mule yard while stable-master Jago whistles through his teeth to call the beasts from the stalls.

exits.label: Call out to Jago across the yard

nodes.title: Mounting Block Respite
nodes.page: Resting the bronze Clapper against the stone mounting-block of the mule yard, you let your aching shoulders relax for a precious moment while stable-master Jago whistles through his teeth to call the beasts from the stalls. The metal knocks against the cold rock, answering the distant mountain winds with a low mournful note. Jago squints at your carrying frame through the haze of peat smoke, wiping grease from his calloused palms.

nodes.brief: In the frosty shadow of the mule yard's stone wall, you adjust the bronze clapper's padded straps while Biscuit plants his stubborn grey hooves against the icy cobbles.

exits.label: Tug the halter past the watering trough
Secure a loose buckle beneath the timber porch
Lead the reluctant animal toward the upper gate

nodes.title: The Stubborn Halt
nodes.page: Frosty shadow of the mule yard's stone wall stretches across the cobbles as you adjust the bronze clapper's padded straps while Biscuit plants his stubborn grey hooves against the icy stones. The mule lowers his head, ears pinned flat against a skull as hard as temple granite, refusing to budge an inch toward the open gate. Old Garrow chuckles from the doorway, tossing you a length of braided hemp to coax the beast forward into the wind.

nodes.brief: Leaving the stable door behind, you step onto the high ridge alone with your burden, feeling the wind test the heavy iron tongue against your shoulder blades.

exits.label: Follow the cliff-edge toward the steps
Pause to test the footing on the ice
Adjust your grip on the carrying frame

nodes.title: The Solo Ridge
nodes.page: The stable door swings shut behind you. You leave the warmth of the pens for the high ridge, alone with your burden, as the wind tests the iron tongue against your shoulder blades. Without a beast to slow your pace or demand your attention, the mountain feels vast, silent, and dangerously steep. Every step requires absolute concentration as the stone path narrows into a mere riband carved into the dark cliff face.

nodes.brief: Beside the watering trough, old Garrow watches you tug at Biscuit's stubborn halter, warning that the mule will bolt if the cliff gales turn sour before the ninety steps.

exits.label: Pull the stubborn beast forward
Wait for the gale to pass
Trade a crust for better footing

nodes.title: The Watering Trough
nodes.page: Beside the stone watering trough, old Garrow watches you tug at Biscuit's stubborn halter, warning that the mule will bolt if the cliff gales turn sour before the ninety steps. The animal plants all four grey hooves firmly in the slush, ears pinned back against the mountain cold, while the bronze clapper pulses a slow beat against your shoulder blades. You adjust the heavy straps and weigh your options in the biting air.

nodes.brief: Under the timber porch of the granary, you pause to secure a loose buckle on the clapper's cradle while Biscuit sniffs a sack of damp barley with absolute disdain.

exits.label: Step out onto the frozen path
Check the harness once more
Lead the animal past the stack

nodes.title: The Granary Porch
nodes.page: Under the timber porch of the granary, you pause to secure a loose buckle on the clapper's cradle while Biscuit sniffs a sack of damp barley with absolute disdain. The mountain wind whistles through the vertical slats above, carrying the sharp scent of old straw and melting ice from the upper roofs. You pat the mule's grey neck, feeling the iron tongue shift slightly in its felt lining as you prepare for the descent.

nodes.brief: Past the smithy's smoking drain, you lead the reluctant animal toward the upper gate, where the frozen ruts threaten to jar the humming bronze against your spine.

exits.label: Push through the narrow gateway
Pause by the warm iron runoff

nodes.title: The Smithy's Drain
nodes.page: Past the smithy's smoking drain, you lead the reluctant animal toward the upper gate, where frozen ruts threaten to jar the bronze tongue against your spine. Sparks from the coal-trough drift upward into the grey air, dying out long before they reach the high stone eaves of Orisonhold. Biscuit tosses his head, snorting a cloud of white vapor into the freezing wind as the first flight of stairs looms ahead.

nodes.brief: a scene in Orisonhold and the Ninety Steps: the cliff-monastery, its bell-towers and mule yards; outfitting, kin and rivals; the reader takes the Clapper and chooses a companion and a rope; the first stairs down

exits.label: Navigate past the dangling tallow racks
Check the bronze for new cracks
Haul the mule away from the edge

nodes.title: The Tallow-Chandler's Lane
nodes.page: Ice crunches beneath your boots in the narrow alley behind the tallow-chandler's workshop, where long yellow candles hang frozen in their wire racks. Biscuit stumbles against a stray cask and rattles the bronze tongue until it sounds a deep, mournful note against your shoulder blades. You grip the lead rope tighter, feeling the chill seep through your wool mittens as the vertical world drops away before you.

nodes.brief: a scene in Orisonhold and the Ninety Steps: the cliff-monastery, its bell-towers and mule yards; outfitting, kin and rivals; the reader takes the Clapper and chooses a companion and a rope; the first stairs down

exits.label: Drag the animal toward the steps
Sweep the soot from your harness
Speak softly to calm the mule

nodes.title: The Charcoal Burners' Yard
nodes.page: Black dust coats your boots as you haul on the lead rope to keep Biscuit from rolling in a pile of spent charcoal near the lower kilns. The air tastes of sulfur and ancient pine smoke, stinging your eyes against the bright glare of the snow-fields above the cloud line. You hitch the padded cradle higher on your shoulders and catch a faint knock from the metal tongue.

nodes.brief: a scene in Orisonhold and the Ninety Steps: the cliff-monastery, its bell-towers and mule yards; outfitting, kin and rivals; the reader takes the Clapper and chooses a companion and a rope; the first stairs down

exits.label: Present the stamped brass tally
Yank the lead rope away firmly

nodes.title: The Lower Yard Gate
nodes.page: By the iron-studded gates of the lower yard, the duty porter inspects your travel tally while Biscuit tries to nibble the moss off a damp stone pier. The mountain air is thin and clear, tasting of clean ice and distant stone-dust from the stair-towns hanging down the cliff. You shift your weight to ease the ache in your back, keeping a firm hand on the leather halter.

nodes.brief: In the cramped harness shed, Miller Thrum offers a handful of salted oats to coax the beast forward, demanding a copper toll just to clear the grain-chute path.

exits.label: Pay the toll and press on
Turn back to the upper yard
Take the reckless way down

nodes.title: The Harness Shed
nodes.page: In the cramped harness shed, Miller Thrum offers a handful of salted oats to coax the beast forward, demanding a copper toll just to clear the grain-chute path. Biscuit pricks his ears at the rattle of grain, though his stubborn stance remains unbroken against the frost-heaved flagstones. You dig into your pocket for the coin, watching the miller's scarred fingers tap impatiently on the wooden shelf.

nodes.brief: Beneath the hanging eaves of the salt-store, you wrestle with Biscuit's stubborn refusal to cross a patch of black ice, risking a tumble toward the outer abyss.

exits.label: Wrest the beast across the ice
Seek a safer detour inland

nodes.title: The Salt-Store Eaves
nodes.page: Beneath the hanging eaves of the salt-store, you wrestle with Biscuit's stubborn refusal to cross a patch of black ice, risking a tumble toward the outer abyss. The mule braces his legs like carved granite, eyes wide as he stares at the dizzy drop where the cloud line swallows the lower stairs. You lean your shoulder into the animal's flank, trying to find traction on the frozen glaze.

nodes.brief: By the lower hay-loft ladder, stable-hand Meara hands you a spare leather girth, muttering that the mule smells the coming blizzard in the deep gorge below.

exits.label: Secure the extra leather girth
Ask about the blizzard warnings

nodes.title: The Hay-Loft Ladder
nodes.page: By the lower hay-loft ladder, stable-hand Meara hands you a spare leather girth, muttering that the mule smells the coming blizzard in the deep gorge below. The hemp smells of summer fields long gone, sharply at odds with the bitter wind sweeping up from the first stair-town. You loop the extra strap around the clapper's cradle, thanking her with a quick nod before turning back to the descent.

nodes.brief: Near the frost-rimed sheep pens, you pause to catch your breath against the biting updraft, checking whether the heavy bronze tongue has shifted in its felt cradle.

exits.label: Check the felt padding closely
Urge the mule past the pens
Rest your shoulders against a post

nodes.title: The Sheep Pens
nodes.page: Near the frost-rimed sheep pens you pause against the updraft to catch your breath and check whether the bronze tongue has shifted in its felt cradle. The woolly backs of the penned rams crowd against the wooden hurdles, steaming in the frigid air while Biscuit blows a long, whistling sigh through his nostrils. You tighten the chest strap, and the familiar knock of metal against felt answers the cold.

nodes.brief: At the stone turn by the cider press, you coax the animal past a discarded wagon axle, wondering if traveling unburdened by four legs would have spared your aching ribs.

exits.label: Pull the mule toward the sheltered wind-break
Tug the stubborn animal past the rock buttress

nodes.title: The Cider Press Turn
nodes.page: By the old stone press, cold cider vinegar and bruised apple pulp fill your nose. You yank the lead-rope, hauling Biscuit past a jagged iron axle left half-buried in frozen mud. The mule snorts a cloud of white mist and plants his hooves on the paving stones while the bronze tongue knocks softly between your shoulder blades. You rub your aching ribs, wondering briefly if traveling unburdened by four legs and a bad temper would have spared you this misery.

nodes.brief: In the sheltered lee of the drying kiln, you adjust your shoulder pads against the biting straps, listening to the iron clapper hum a low, warning note against your back.

exits.label: Leave a copper coin at the three sisters shrine
Lean your weight into the harness across the gale

nodes.title: The Drying Kiln Lee
nodes.page: Pine smoke drifts from the drying kiln, wrapping you in a pungent, warm shroud against the mountain wind. You lean back against a dry timber wall, adjusting the wool-padded shoulder straps that bite into your collarbones. Behind you, the iron clapper pulses deep, knocking a low warning that runs straight through your ribs. The path ahead dips sharply into the grey shadow of the cliffs, where the wind howls without mercy across open stone.

nodes.brief: Beside the timber-stack near the lower trough, a novice monk offers a cup of lukewarm chicory, urging you to move before the midday ice begins to loosen from the eaves.

exits.label: Pull the mule past the narrow stone buttress
Step carefully beside the frozen monastery drain

nodes.title: The Lower Trough Timber-Stack
nodes.page: Splinters of resinous pine crunch under your boots beside the communal watering trough. A novice monk thrusts a clay mug of lukewarm chicory into your hand, urging you to swallow fast before the midday sun loosens the giant icicles hanging from the roof eaves. You hand back the empty cup with a nod, feeling Orison's tongue drag you slightly forward as Biscuit tosses his shaggy head in protest.

nodes.brief: Through the narrow alley of the tanners' quarter, you drag the recalcitrant beast away from a pile of salted hides that make the animal roll its eyes in terror.

exits.label: Meet the fog-warden climbing with winter pears
Adjust your aching shoulder cushioning in the shadow

nodes.title: The Tanners' Quarter Alley
nodes.page: Stiff salted hides line the narrow alley walls. The alkaline tang hits hard enough that Biscuit rolls his wild eyes in absolute terror. You plant your boots in the slush and haul on the lead rope until the balking beast comes away from the towering stack of goat pelts. The iron clapper shifts in its felt cradle and lands against your back with a dull thud. Every wasted moment brings the ice-wind closer.

nodes.brief: At the intersection of the tallow-chandler's lane, you dodge a cartload of tallow barrels while Biscuit plants his feet firmly on the greasy stones.

exits.label: Pick your way past the frozen drainage cascade
Shift the heavy bronze tongue in its cradle

nodes.title: The Tallow-Chandler's Lane
nodes.page: Scented tallow and rendered fat coat the steep cobblestones, turning the lane into a treacherous slide of yellow grease. You dodge a handcart piled high with leaking barrels just as Biscuit locks his knees and refuses to take another step downward. The iron tongue knocks a rhythmic note against your spine, matching the frantic beat of your pulse in the thin air.

nodes.brief: Under the carved lintel of the cooperage, you tighten the breast-band on your own leather harness, feeling the raw pinch of the straps through your woollen tunic.

exits.label: Check the horizon by the rusted iron crane
Guide the nervous animal along the high ledge

nodes.title: The Cooperage Lintel
nodes.page: Shavings of sweet oak crunch underfoot beneath the heavy timber lintel of the cooperage. You pause to yank the leather breast-band tighter across your chest, wincing as the raw hemp-and-leather straps bite straight through your thick woollen tunic. Biscuit stamps his iron-shod hoof against the flagstones, eager to bolt down the mountain before the weather closes in for good.

nodes.brief: Beside the frozen drainage culvert, you wrestle the stubborn grey mule away from a crumbling parapet that overlooks the terrifying drop of the first cliff tier.

exits.label: Check the gathering storm clouds by the crane
Seek shelter across the threshold of the lower grotto
Lead the nervous beast along the cantilevered ledge

nodes.title: The Drainage Culvert Drop
nodes.page: Slush and black ice choke the stone drainage culvert, spilling freezing water across the descending path. You throw your full weight against the lead rope, wrestling the grey mule away from a crumbling parapet that drops straight down into the dizzying abyss of the first cliff tier. Against your back the bronze clapper knocks a warning that answers the terrifying depth of the drop below.

nodes.brief: In the open courtyard of the charcoal burners, black dust coats your boots as you haul on the lead rope to keep the animal from bolting toward the stables.

exits.label: Lead the nervous animal along the high ledge

nodes.title: The Charcoal Burners' Yard
nodes.page: Soot and black coal-dust stain the melting snow grey as you cross the open yard of the charcoal burners. A gust of wind catches the charcoal grit, stinging your eyes and sending Biscuit lunging sideways toward the safety of the upper stables. You dig your heels into the slush, hauling the stubborn animal back onto the downward track with both hands.

nodes.brief: Near the dry-stone retaining wall, an old shepherd warns you that the descending stairs are slick with sheep grease and melting rime from the upper snowfields.

exits.label: Check your leather bindings by the ancient marker post
Join the shivering monks around the rock-cut brazier
Turn back toward the security of the stable door

nodes.title: The Dry-Stone Retaining Wall
nodes.page: Weathered grey stones form a low retaining wall that keeps the mountain from sliding down upon the monastery path. An old shepherd leans against the masonry, his face lined like parchment, warning you that the descending stairs are slick with sheep grease and melting rime from the upper snowfields. The iron clapper presses a low chord against your spine while you weigh your next step.

nodes.brief: Beneath the grey slate roof of the provision store, you check the lashings of the bronze tongue one last time before committing to the steep stone descent.

exits.label: Rest by the brazier in the rock-cut shelter

nodes.title: The Provision Store Slate Roof
nodes.page: Drips of cold meltwater fall rhythmically from the grey slate eaves onto your woolen hood. You check the thick hemp lashings binding the bronze tongue into its felt cradle one last time so the metal will not shift during the plunge. The mountain air tastes of ozone and old ice, daring you to take the first real step down into the winding stair-towns.

nodes.brief: By the iron-studded gates of the lower yard, the duty porter inspects your travel tally while Biscuit tries to chew the sleeve of your heavy winter coat.

exits.label: Pull the stubborn mule toward the goat troughs
Step out onto the dizzying expanse of the upper stairs

nodes.title: The Iron-Studged Gates
nodes.page: At the iron-studded gates of the lower yard the duty porter checks your travel tally, and Biscuit works at the sleeve of your winter coat with damp teeth. You yank the woolen fabric from the beast's damp teeth with a muttered warning and hitch the bronze clapper on your aching back while cold mountain wind rattles the gate-post lanterns. The porter stamps the wax tally with an iron seal, grunts a brief farewell, then points toward the frozen descent that stretches into the grey mist below.

nodes.brief: At the yawning mouth of the ninety steps, you brace yourself against the freezing downdraft, knowing that every stone brings you closer to the roaring foundry fires.

exits.label: Seek refuge with the shivering monks by the brazier
Follow the steep straightaway down into the white haze
Turn back toward the mule yard's frosty shadow

nodes.title: The Ninety Steps
nodes.page: At the yawning mouth of the ninety steps, you brace yourself against the freezing downdraft, knowing that every stone brings you closer to the roaring foundry fires. The bronze tongue upon your spine sends a faint shiver through your padded harness in the chill altitude. Biscuit shifts uneasily on the icy flags behind you, his iron shoes clicking against the frost-rimed rock as you weigh your path down the vertical world.

nodes.brief: On the broad stone landing above the first flight, you pause to let a train of descending wool-porters pass, their heavy baskets scraping loudly against the damp cliff face.

exits.label: Inspect the spliced cable hanging by the guild kiosk
Step across to the rope merchant's stacked hemp coils

nodes.title: The Descending Porters
nodes.page: On the broad stone landing above the first flight, you pause to let a train of descending wool-porters pass, their heavy baskets scraping loudly against the damp cliff face. The laborers shuffle past with bowed heads and steam rising from their wool caps, smelling of lanolin, wet fleece, and long exertion in the high thin air. You press yourself flat against the cold retaining wall to keep the massive clapper cradle from catching on their woven hampers, waiting until the last basket vanishes around the granite bend.

nodes.brief: Beside the iron ring set into the cliff, you untangle the lead rope from a frozen root while the humming bronze vibrates uncomfortably against your aching spine.

exits.label: Examine the stacked hemp coils by the cellar platform

nodes.title: The Frozen Root
nodes.page: Beside the iron ring set into the cliff, you untangle the lead rope from a frozen root while the humming bronze vibrates uncomfortably against your aching spine. The ice encrusting the iron is thick and blue as winter glass, requiring a sharp tug and a scraped knuckle to free the hemp line. Biscuit stamps a hoof against the packed snow, eager to leave the high ledge behind as the first pale light catches the jagged peaks above Orisonhold.

nodes.brief: Under the stone arch of the wind-break, you wipe rime from your eyelashes and struggle to pull the recalcitrant mule away from the precipice edge.

exits.label: Approach the stacked hemp coils by the rope cellar
Inspect the heavy spliced cable at the guild kiosk

nodes.title: The Wind-Break Arch
nodes.page: Under the stone arch of the wind-break, you wipe rime from your eyelashes and struggle to pull the recalcitrant mule away from the precipice edge. The wind howls through the narrow granite opening like a trapped spirit, tearing at your woolen cloak and sending loose pebbles clattering down the immense drop into the clouds below. You dig your heels into the frozen dirt, wrapping the leather halter twice around your mittened hand until the stubborn beast finally turns its grey head toward the path.

nodes.brief: Near the shrine of the three sisters, you leave a copper coin in the weathered crack of the masonry to buy safe passage down the icy tiers.

exits.label: Examine the heavy spliced cable hanging at the kiosk
Approach the frayed hemp bundles on the combing benches

nodes.title: The Shrine of Sisters
nodes.page: Near the shrine of the three sisters, you leave a copper coin in the weathered crack of the masonry to buy safe passage down the icy tiers. The small stone alcove is crusted with old ice, and the carved faces of the ancient patronesses stare out with blank, wind-scoured eyes toward the endless stairs. You offer a silent, breath-fogged prayer for firm footing and warm hearths below, patting the leather harness straps before stepping back onto the slick mountain path.

nodes.brief: In the narrow gap between the buttress and the sheer rock, Biscuit braces his legs against the stone steps, refusing to budge until you share a crust of rye.

exits.label: Head toward the stacked coils of hemp outside the cellar
Inspect the tar-scented grey twine in the cordage yard

nodes.title: The Buttress Gap
nodes.page: In the narrow gap between the buttress and the sheer rock, Biscuit braces his legs against the stone steps, refusing to budge until you share a crust of rye. You pull a dry heel of bread from your coat pocket, break off a grey morsel, and press it into the soft muzzle while the bronze clapper knocks against your shoulder blades. The mule chews slowly, his warm breath pluming in the bitter air, until the stubborn fit passes and the path ahead opens up.

nodes.brief: Across the open shelf where the gales howl unchecked, you lean your weight into the harness, keeping the heavy iron clapper balanced against the biting wind.

exits.label: Check the tar-scented grey twine in the cordage yard
Inspect the frayed hemp bundles near the combing benches
Proceed to the guild ledger desk by the iron scales

nodes.title: The Open Shelf
nodes.page: Across the open shelf where the gales howl unchecked, you lean into the harness and keep the iron clapper braced against the biting wind. The world falls away on your left into a vast, white sea of clouds, while the sheer granite wall presses close and unyielding on your right. Every step requires a deliberate calculation against the gusts that threaten to lift you from the stone, your fingers freezing stiff inside their woolen gloves.

nodes.brief: Beside the frozen cascade of the monastery drain, icicles clink like glass dropped upon stone as the beast's iron-shod hooves ring out on the frozen steps.

exits.label: Examine the heavy spliced cable at the guild kiosk
Inspect the tar-scented grey twine in the cordage yard
Approach the frayed hemp bundles on the combing benches

nodes.title: The Frozen Cascade
nodes.page: Beside the frozen cascade of the monastery drain, icicles clink like glass dropped upon stone as the beast's iron-shod hooves ring out on the frozen steps. The water has frozen into a ribbed sheet of blue-white crystal that covers the lower masonry like a discarded skin. You pick your way carefully across the slick incline, leaning into the weight of the bronze clapper to keep your footing from sliding out beneath you.

nodes.brief: At the turn of the carved stair-rail, you meet a fog-warden climbing upward with a basket of winter pears, her warning whistle held tight between her chapped lips.

exits.label: Approach the frayed hemp bundles on the combing benches
Proceed to the guild ledger desk by the iron scales

nodes.title: The Fog-Warden's Turn
nodes.page: At the turn of the carved stair-rail, you meet a fog-warden climbing upward with a basket of winter pears, her warning whistle held tight between her chapped lips. She pauses to nod a greeting, her weathered face lined by decades of high-altitude gales and mountain sun, smelling faintly of woodsmoke and sweet frozen fruit. You trade a brief word about the storm-damaged passes above before she climbs on into the whitening mists.

nodes.brief: In the damp shadow of the overhang, you readjust the shoulder cushioning where the iron weight has begun to bruise your collarbone through the coarse wool.

exits.label: Inspect the salted winch in the cordage yard
Follow the draughty corridor toward the rope storehouse

nodes.title: The Damped Overhang
nodes.page:
In the damp shadow of the overhang, you readjust the shoulder cushioning where the iron weight has begun to bruise your collarbone through the coarse wool. The bronze clapper hums against your spine like a trapped insect, its low vibration sinking deep into your bones as the mountain wind whistles through the rock-crevices. You shift your weight from one frozen boot to the other, testing the grip of the packed gravel beneath your heels.

Ahead, the path splits toward the lower yards: salted winches of the cordage makers one way, draughty corridors where tow-lines wait in the gloom the other.

nodes.brief: By the rusted iron crane used to hoist provisions, you check the weather-eye on the horizon, where purple clouds gather above the distant stair-towns.

exits.label: Head inside for the thick three-strand tow-line
Seek out the iron weighing scale near the ledger desk

nodes.title: The Rusted Crane
nodes.page: By the rusted iron crane used to hoist provisions, you check the weather-eye on the horizon, where purple clouds gather above the distant stair-towns. Frost nips at your knuckles as you secure the leather straps binding the heavy bronze tongue to your padded frame. Below you, the stone steps vanish into a swirling curtain of white mist, hiding the drop into the abyss.

nodes.brief: Across the threshold of the lower grotto, you pause to catch your breath while water drips rhythmically from the green-stained limestone roof onto your hood.

exits.label: Approach the hemp-combing benches where apprentices work
Step into the draughty corridor of the rope storehouse
Walk toward the iron weighing scale by the ledger desk

nodes.title: The Lower Grotto
nodes.page:
Across the threshold of the lower grotto, you pause to catch your breath while water drips rhythmically from the green-stained limestone roof onto your hood. The air here smells of damp moss and old stone, thick with the moisture of melting snow from the high ledges. A stray draft carries the faint, sweet scent of burning juniper from the monks' cells far above.

Three distinct paths branch out from the dripping cave mouth, leading toward the hemp-combing benches, the shadowy rope corridors, or the bustling ledger desks.

nodes.brief: On the dizzying cantilevered ledge above the deep fissure, you guide the nervous animal step by careful step over the frost-whitened timber planks.

exits.label: Step into the drafty rope storehouse
Approach the guild master by the scales
Inspect the stiff fibers in the rope-loft

nodes.title: The Cantilevered Ledge
nodes.page: Frost whitens the loose pine timbers of the cantilevered ledge, where the mountain wind funnels upward from the deep blue fissure with a low, whistling howl. Biscuit sets each iron-shod hoof with stubborn care, ears flicking back when the planks groan beneath the bronze Clapper in its padded frame. Below the open rail, the cloud sea shifts and rolls, swallowing the lower stairs entirely while the sheer stone wall of Orisonhold rises gray and indifferent at your shoulder. Every breath tastes of thin, high-altitude air and old pine resin, demanding absolute focus on the next flat nail-head in the grain.

nodes.brief: Beside the ancient marker post carved with the runes of the first bell-masters, you check your leather bindings to ensure the clapper cannot slip loose.

exits.label: Inspect the thick tow-lines in the draughty corridor
Weigh your backup rope against the fibers in the loft
Stop by the heavy oak wicket of the cable court office

nodes.title: The Ancient Marker
nodes.page:
Beside the ancient marker post carved with the runes of the first bell-masters, you check your leather bindings to ensure the clapper cannot slip loose. The old stone is cold and slick with rime, bearing centuries of moss and weathering from the mountain gales. A small tin cup hangs from an iron peg on the post, left for travelers to collect meltwater.

You pull your woolen cloak tighter against the biting draft and weigh your options regarding the equipment ahead.

nodes.brief: In the hollow bowl of the rock-cut shelter, a group of shivering monks huddles around a small brazier, offering you a brief nod of encouragement.

exits.label: Approach the iron weighing scale by the ledger desk
Seek shelter under the arched rafters of the rope-loft
Visit the heavy oak wicket of the cable court office

nodes.title: The Rock-Cut Shelter
nodes.page:
In the hollow bowl of the rock-cut shelter, a group of shivering monks huddles around a small brazier, offering you a brief nod of encouragement. The scent of woodsmoke mixes pleasantly with the sharp tang of high-altitude ozone. Outside the stony alcove, the vertical world plunges downward in a series of gray, ice-rimed steps.

The monks return to their silent prayers as you shoulder the metal tongue once more and eye the branching routes that lead deeper into the mountain's throat.

nodes.brief: Near the broken stone trough where mountain goats sometimes gather, you haul sharply on the halter to keep the mule from chasing a loose stone over the edge.

exits.label: Head toward the iron weighing scale near the ledger desk
Approach the heavy oak wicket of the cable court office

nodes.title: The Broken Trough
nodes.page:
Near the broken stone trough where mountain goats sometimes gather, you haul sharply on the halter to keep the mule from chasing a loose stone over the edge. The animal snorts a cloud of white vapor into the frigid air, its ears flicking back and forth at the howling of the wind. Shards of ice crunch beneath your heavy boots as you regain your footing.

The path narrows sharply here, forcing a decision between the bureaucratic hub of the ledger desks and the toll-lords waiting beyond.

nodes.brief: At the threshold of the long, steep straightaway, you look down at the dizzying perspective of the stairs receding into the grey valley fog below.

exits.label: Seek the iron weighing scale near the ledger desk
Inspect the stiff new fibers up in the rope-loft
Stop at the heavy oak wicket of the cable court office

nodes.title: The Steep Straightaway
nodes.page:
At the threshold of the long, steep straightaway, you look down at the dizzying perspective of the stairs receding into the grey valley fog below. The sheer drop-off makes your stomach lurch, reminding you that a single misstep would send both you and the sacred bell-metal tumbling into the clouds. The metal clapper taps a steady, relentless rhythm against your shoulder blades.

You grip the canvas straps tighter and evaluate the three paths opening before you into the gloom.

nodes.brief: On the wide platform outside the rope merchant's cellar, you confront stacked coils of hemp while the clerk taps an ink-stained finger on the rough wooden counter.

exits.label: Sign the guild ledger on the frosty threshold

nodes.title: The Merchant's Cellar
nodes.page:
On the wide platform outside the rope merchant's cellar, you confront stacked coils of hemp while the clerk taps an ink-stained finger on the rough wooden counter. The pungent aroma of pine tar and treated cordage hangs thick in the freezing air, masking the usual scent of mountain snow. Ledger books lie open, fluttering slightly in the drafty passage.

The clerk watches you with a practiced, calculating eye, waiting for you to commit to the guild's terms before the journey continues downward.

nodes.brief: Under the flickering tallow lamp of the guild kiosk, Master Weaver Korda dangles a heavy spliced cable, praising its braided strength against the worst mountain squalls.

exits.label: Bind your journey with the cold iron nib

nodes.title: The Guild Kiosk
nodes.page:
Under the flickering tallow lamp of the guild kiosk, Master Weaver Korda dangles a heavy spliced cable, praising its braided strength against the worst mountain squalls. The master's weathered face is etched with lines from decades of staring into blinding snow and whipping wind. A small charcoal brazier sputters in the corner, offering little warmth against the creeping frost.

You nod slowly as the spliced line is held out toward you, ready to bind your journey to the weaver's craft.

nodes.brief: Beside the salted winch in the cordage yard, you inspect a coil of grey twine that smells of tar and sea-salt, wondering if its price includes an unwritten oath.

exits.label: Buy the salted grey twine
Leave the strange coil behind
Inspect the inner strands closer

nodes.title: The Tarred Coil
nodes.page: Bespoke grease and sea-salt cling to the grey twine coiled beside the salted winch in the cordage yard, heavy with the reek of deep-sea rigging. Your fingers test the stiff twist, wondering if the cheap price hides a silent trap or a binding oath written in the trade-lore of the cliff. The cold wind bites through your woollen tunic as you weigh the risk of taking a line that demands more than simple silver.

nodes.brief: Near the hemp-combing benches, an apprentice pushes a bundle of frayed hemp toward you, whispering that the guild's cheapest line has a dangerous habit of snapping under frost.

exits.label: Take the cheap frayed bundle
Refuse the risky bargain line

nodes.title: The Frayed Bundle
nodes.page: Pungent hemp dust rises from the combing benches where an apprentice shuffles a loose, cheap bundle toward your boots, murmuring warnings about frostbite and sudden snapping under tension. The guild's bargain line looks deceptive, pale and loosely spun against the mountain chill, yet your purse grows painfully light with every step through Orisonhold. You consider whether a frayed lifeline is better than none at all when the descent begins in earnest.
