Boot scrape and the bronze pulse against your back are what remain. Every handhold on the slick stone feels uncertain and treacherous in the sudden gloom.

nodes.brief: You balance precariously on a single fir pole bridging two swaying market huts while below you the cloud sea boils upward.

exits.label: Duck beneath the web of singing overhead cables
Jump clear as a panicked pack-mule charges the path

nodes.title: The Fir Pole Bridge
nodes.page: You balance precariously on a single fir pole bridging two swaying market huts while below you the cloud sea boils upward. The pole flexes alarmingly with your every step, testing your sense of balance to its absolute limit. Mist wraps coldly around your ankles, hiding the dizzying drop into the gorge from your direct view. You keep your eyes fixed firmly on the splintered threshold on the far side, breathing in the scent of wet pine and old rope.

nodes.brief: You scramble across a dripping timber gantry where apprentice Brann frantically knots a snapping guide-rope against the gale.

exits.label: Haul yourself onto the final stone anchor-platform

nodes.title: The Dripping Gantry
nodes.page: You scramble across a dripping timber gantry where apprentice Brann frantically knots a snapping guide-rope against the gale. Freezing water drips from the salted canvas awnings above in one long stream that soaks through your wool collar. Brann shouts a brief warning over the rising din of the wind, his hands moving with practiced speed through intricate loops and hitches. You plant your feet on the wet beams and keep the bronze cradle balanced between your shoulder blades.

nodes.brief: A towering stack of tarred rope blocks the junction, forcing you to crawl through a narrow greasy drainage chute to proceed.

exits.label: Haul yourself onto the final stone anchor-platform
Leave the rope markets behind and face the cliff-drop

nodes.title: The Greasy Drainage Chute
nodes.page: A towering stack of tarred rope blocks the junction, forcing you to crawl through a narrow greasy drainage chute to proceed. The rough stone walls press close on either side, smelling strongly of old tallow and mountain mud. Your canvas pack scrapes noisily against the low timber ceiling, making every inch of forward movement a struggle. Faint chimes from distant valley towers drift up through the gloom, reminding you of the long miles still remaining before Lowgate.

nodes.brief: Toll-collector Morva steps from a canvas watch-tent, her eyes fixed entirely on the heavy bronze shape shifting beneath your canvas cover.

exits.label: Climb toward the final anchor-platform
Bribe the guard for reluctant passage
Slip away into the sheer cliff-drop

nodes.title: The Toll-Collector's Eye
nodes.page:
From a canvas watch-tent Toll-collector Morva steps out, eyes locked on the bronze shape shifting beneath your canvas cover. Cold air rasps your throat as you hitch the metal tongue on your spine, waiting for her demand. A ledger flaps in her mittened hand against the rising mountain gale while the neighboring winch-drums clatter in rhythm.

"The road below is sealed to temple freight without a bond-seal," she says, tapping her brass stamp against her palm.

nodes.brief: You dodge a hurtling hand-truck loaded with split pine billets as it careens down the sloped central tramway toward the gorge.

exits.label: Scramble up to the stone anchor-platform
Bargain with the winch-man for an easier drop

nodes.title: The Sloping Tramway
nodes.page:
You dodge a hurtling hand-truck loaded with split pine billets as it careens down the sloped central tramway toward the gorge. Splintered wood and frozen mud scatter across your boots until you throw your shoulder against a rope-strung post to keep the bronze clapper from striking the iron rail. Across the tram-channel, winch-boys shout warnings through cupped hands as another empty crate carrier hurtles upward into the mist.

The path narrows dramatically past the timber brakes, leaving you with only two ways to advance through the clamor of the market stalls.

nodes.brief: An old rope-braider named Drenn presses a greasy protective leather pad into your bruised hands to ease the weight of the cradle.

exits.label: Make for the final anchor-platform above
Seek out the weary winch-man's gate
Leave the market behind for the open cliff

nodes.title: The Braider's Gift
nodes.page:
An old rope-braider named Drenn presses a greasy protective leather pad into your bruised hands to soften how the cradle sits. His fingers are stiff and scarred from decades of twisting hemp and steel-wire cables in the mountain wind. "You will need that before the lower switchbacks chew your shoulders to bone," he mutters, nodding toward the dense maze of hanging bazaars that stretch across the abyss.

The scent of pine tar and sheep grease hangs thick in the freezing air, and you must choose your next step away from his stall before the market wardens take notice of your cargo.

nodes.brief: The suspension chains groan audibly as a heavily laden ore basket slams into the winch-station platform just ten paces ahead.

exits.label: Climb toward the final anchor-platform
Step out onto the open cliff-drop
Take the reckless way across the gap

nodes.title: The Ore Basket
nodes.page:
The suspension chains groan audibly as a heavily laden ore basket slams into the winch-station platform just ten paces ahead. Iron wheels screech against frozen oak beams, sending a shower of gray sparks into the swirling valley fog. You brace your legs against the shockwave while the bronze clapper knocks a deep note against your spine.

The path ahead bifurcates around a rusted pulley-engine, offering a standard climb or a desperate, leaping shortcut across the open chasm.

nodes.brief: Because Biscuit knows every hidden footing on these icy ledges, the stubborn mule picks a safe path past a crumbling timber arch.

exits.label: Face the sheer drop beyond the market
Pause beside the frozen water trough
Dodge the lookout's warning horn in the mist

priv.why: Biscuit the mule is with the reader and knows the ledges and the ropeway stalls

nodes.title: The Sure-Footed Mule
nodes.page:
Because Biscuit knows every hidden footing on these icy ledges, the stubborn mule picks a safe path past a crumbling timber arch. The faithful animal dips its head against the stinging spindrift, its small hooves finding purchase on frosted stone where a human would slip. You follow close behind, keeping one hand on the beast's warm flank and the other steadying the heavy bronze tongue in its padded wooden frame.

The chaotic stalls begin to thin out here, replaced by the distant, rhythmic clicking of the valley windmills and the watchful presence of the toll-lords.

nodes.brief: You press yourself flat against an alcove wall as three armed bailiffs from the Cable Court march past with drawn measuring rods.

exits.label: Seek out the weary winch-man for passage
Head outward toward the sheer cliff-drop
Rest briefly by the frozen water trough

nodes.title: The Measuring Rods
nodes.page:
You press yourself flat against an alcove wall as three armed bailiffs from the Cable Court march past with drawn measuring rods. Iron-shod boots ring on the frost-covered wooden slats, and their gray cloaks smell of damp wool and tax-office tallow. They are checking the width of every hanging freight-frame to ensure no unapproved temple metal slips past their tolls.

Their bootfalls fade into the whistling wind while you sort the remaining ways through the dense rope-markets.

nodes.brief: A frayed guide-line whips through the air with a sound like a cracking whip, grazing your canvas pack before snapping into the fog.

exits.label: Push onward to the frozen water trough
Answer the lookout's horn in the mist

nodes.title: The Whipping Line
nodes.page:
A frayed guide-line whips through the air with a sound like a cracking whip, grazing your canvas pack before snapping into the fog. The sudden lash leaves a white powder trace across your shoulder where the hemp fibers tore against your canvas cover. Around you, market traders dive behind salt-barrels and timber stacks while the broken cable thrashes blindly against the scaffolding.

With the immediate danger passing into the gray abyss, you must decide whether to push forward toward the terrace bells or seek shelter from the falling ice.

nodes.brief: You cross an open mesh platform where the frozen wind howls up from the deep valley, icing the bronze clapper inside your frame.

exits.label: Heed the lookout's warning horn in the mist
Slip through the winch-houses past inspectors
Follow the fog-warden toward the stone stairs

nodes.title: The Open Mesh
nodes.page:
You cross an open mesh platform where the frozen wind howls up from the deep valley, icing the bronze clapper inside your frame. The metal beneath your boots is nothing more than twisted wire netting, through which you can see thousands of feet of sheer gray air and nothing else. Every breath burns your lungs with sharp, thin frost as you lean your weight forward to keep your balance against the gale.

On the far side of the mesh, three distinct routes branch off into the swirling fog and timber scaffolding.

nodes.brief: Weaver Coren tries to trade a coil of waxed rigging line for your temple-cast bronze, claiming the metal is cursed by the frost.

exits.label: Evade the inspectors between the winch-houses
Follow the fog-warden down the stone stairs

nodes.title: The Cursed Metal
nodes.page:
Weaver Coren tries to trade a coil of waxed rigging line for your temple-cast bronze, claiming the metal is cursed by the frost. His eyes are bloodshot from the mountain glare, and his fingers twitch nervously toward a sharp bone knife tucked in his belt. "That tongue will drag you to the bottom of the gorge before you see Lowgate," he spits, gesturing to the swinging rope bridges around you.

You tighten your grip on the cradle straps and ignore his superstitious bargaining, looking for a way out of his cluttered stall.

nodes.brief: A group of shivering market children watch your heavy burden with wide eyes from the safety of a stacked-pulpwood lean-to.

exits.label: Slip past the inspectors between the winch-houses
Step onto the frost-heaved limestone trail

nodes.title: The Watching Children
nodes.page:
A group of shivering market children watch your heavy burden with wide eyes from the safety of a stacked-pulpwood lean-to. Their cheeks are chapped raw by the ice-wind, and they clutch bits of dried apple in mittened fists while whispering among themselves about the ringing metal on your back. You offer them a brief, tired nod as you adjust the sliding leather straps of your frame.

The ground shifts beneath your boots as you leave their shelter, offering two distinct routes away from the crowded stalls.

nodes.brief: You slide down a short, greased loading plank to bypass a crushed section of the upper bazaar walkway where scaffolding has collapsed.

exits.label: Scramble toward the windy gap
Follow the lower timber catwalk
Step out onto the limestone ledge

nodes.title: The Greased Plank
nodes.page: Slick timber offers a sudden, perilous shortcut where the upper walkway has buckled under rime frost. You slide down a short greased loading plank, heels spitting white chips of pine, the bronze clapper knocking against your spine. The drop deposits you sharply onto a narrow ledge overlooking the churning gray abyss of the lower gorge.

nodes.brief: A toll-master's clerk drops a heavy iron gate across the bridge, demanding an exorbitant inspection fee before you can take another step.

exits.label: Pay the steep toll in coin
Duck beneath the iron barrier

nodes.title: The Iron Gate
nodes.page: Iron bars slam down across the swaying bridge with a dull, echoing clang that rattles through your teeth. A toll-master's clerk plants his boots on the threshold, demanding an exorbitant inspection fee in copper before you can take another step with the temple metal. Behind you, the creak of tensioned hemp reminds you that every moment spent bargaining brings the ice-wind closer.

nodes.brief: You duck beneath a web of singing overhead cables that vibrate with the mournful hum of the mountain wind.

exits.label: Slip past the humming winch-rig
Step onto the frost-heaved limestone
Head toward the bronze warning gong
Turn back toward the inner market

nodes.title: The Singing Cables
nodes.page: Overhead webs of thick rigging vibrate with a mournful, singing resonance that mimics the mountain wind through stone flutes. You duck low beneath the shivering iron wires, feeling the metallic tang of frozen grease prickle the back of your throat. Every taut strand seems alive, humming warnings about the treacherous descents waiting beyond the market stalls.

nodes.brief: A panicked pack-mule breaks free from its tether and charges down the narrow plankway, forcing you to leap onto a stacked crate of twine.

exits.label: Drop down past the winch-house
Follow the fog-warden's brass staff

nodes.title: The Bolting Pack-Mule
nodes.page: Panic erupts as a tethered pack-mule snaps its hempen tie and charges straight down the narrow plankway toward your laden frame. You leap instinctively to the side, scrambling atop a towering stack of fragrant pine twine just as the frantic beast clatters past. Dust and loose straw settle over your boots while the muffled shouts of merchants fade into the whistling wind.

nodes.brief: You haul your aching frame onto the final stone anchor-platform of the rope markets as the last tethered huts fade into white fog.

exits.label: Descend the long stone stair-flight
Shoulder your burden toward the haze
Face the cold draft from the terraces

nodes.title: The Final Anchor
nodes.page: Aching muscles protest as you haul your frame onto the final stone anchor-platform of the rope markets. The last tethered huts and swaying platforms fade rapidly into a thick blanket of white fog, cutting off the upper tier from the world below. Your boots find solid, unyielding masonry at last, offering a brief respite from the dizzying swing of the cables.

nodes.brief: A weary winch-man named Brin unlatches a heavy security chain, granting you reluctant passage toward the descending stone stairs.

exits.label: Descend the long stone stairs
Follow the draft toward the terraces

nodes.title: The Unlatched Gate
nodes.page: Heavy iron links rattle against the winch-post as Brin drags the security chain aside with a calloused hand, grunting against the morning frost. The bronze clapper shifts on your back, its cold metal humming a dull note through your woolen tunic. A gap opens between the swaying hemp booths of the upper market and the sheer stone descent carved into the mountain flank. Behind you, the pulleys of the Ropewrights' Guild whine in the thin air, while ahead the steps drop away into the pale mist of the gorge.

nodes.brief: The rope markets fall silent behind you as you shoulder the heavy bronze clapper and face the sheer cliff-drop leading downward.

exits.label: Head down the stone flight
Keep walking into the gray haze

nodes.title: Leaving the Market
nodes.page: The low roar of the rope bazaars fades into the whistling mountain wind as you adjust the padded cradle carrying the heavy bronze tongue of Orison. Frost coats your eyebrows, and every breath plumes white against the gray granite of the cliff wall. Below your boots, the world breaks into sheer drops and hanging tiers where the stair-towns cling like swallow nests. The air smells intensely of hemp grease and old snow, clean and bitter in your lungs.

nodes.brief: You pause by a frozen water trough to catch your breath while the distant windmills of the terrace tier click against the cold sky.

exits.label: Step firmly onto the stairs
Walk toward the upper market haze

nodes.title: The Frozen Trough
nodes.page: Ice rims the edges of the stone watering trough, trapping dry barley straw blown from the tiers above. You lean against the frozen rim and let the bronze clapper rest a moment while your shoulders quit their ache. In the distance, the wooden wings of the Terrace Millers' windmills turn in jerky rhythms against the pale sky, clicking like dry bones. The air smells of cold stone and distant woodsmoke.

nodes.brief: A Cable Court lookout blows a warning horn into the mist, signaling that your debt-laden passage from the market has been logged.

exits.label: Walk down the stone steps
Take the upper market path
Follow the draft to the terrace edge
Turn back toward the iron turnstile

nodes.title: The Lookout's Horn
nodes.page: A flat, mournful blast from the Cable Court horn rolls over the swinging stalls, setting the hemp cables vibrating beneath your boots. A lookout leans over a timber rail in the mist, marking your passage in a grease-stained tally book with a blunt piece of chalk. The bronze clapper hums in response to the brass horn, a sympathetic vibration that rattles straight through your spine. You stand at the crossroads of the market shelf, where several paths carve their way into the white abyss.

nodes.brief: You slip through a narrow gap between two winch-houses just as a team of inspectors emerges to check travelers for unpaid tolls.

exits.label: Step onto the stone stairs
Follow the draft downward

nodes.title: The Narrow Gap
nodes.page: Rough timbers scrape against your shoulders as you squeeze through the tight alley between two creaking winch-houses, leaving the main bazaar behind. Shouts echo from the inspectors' station where officials are checking travelers for unpaid toll-badges, but the shadows here are deep and blue. The bronze clapper stays muffled against your padded wool, silent for once as you crouch near the edge of the cliff.

nodes.brief: The ground beneath your boots turns from splintered pine planks to slick, frost-heaved limestone as you leave the suspended bazaars.

exits.label: Follow the steep downward steps
Take the narrow ledge by the hemp coils

nodes.title: Limestone Ridge Transition
nodes.page: Slick limestone replaces splintered pine beneath your boots as the suspended bazaars fade into the mountain shadow. Frost crusts the gray stone, catching the pale mountain light and making every footfall a small calculation of balance and friction. The bronze clapper knocks a low answering beat against your spine, more present now that the noise of the market has died away into thin air. Two paths diverge before you: one plunging straight down a flight of worn steps toward the mist, and another winding along a narrow ledge where the rope-makers left coils of discarded hemp.

nodes.brief: A lone fog-warden standing by a bronze warning gong points his brass-tipped staff toward the stone stairs descending into the gray mist.

exits.label: Descend the stairs into the gray mist

nodes.title: The Fog-Warden's Post
nodes.page:
A lone fog-warden stands still beside a bronze warning gong, his brass-tipped staff planted firm in the frozen silt. He gestures mutely with three scarred fingers toward the stone stairs plunging into the thickening gray mist below, offering no words of comfort against the biting wind. The metal of his staff catches a dull glint from the overcast sky as he strikes the gong once, sending a hollow, resonant pulse through the rock to warn climbers of shifting rime.

You hitch the padded cradle on your shoulders as the clapper's low note answers the gong's fading tone.

nodes.brief: You step firmly onto the head of the long stone stair-flight, leaving the swinging rope bazaars swaying high above in the freezing clouds.

exits.label: Press on down the stone flight

nodes.title: Head of the Stone Flight
nodes.page:
Stepping firmly onto the head of the long stone stair-flight, you leave the swinging rope bazaars swaying high above in the freezing clouds. The mountain air grows noticeably crisper here, stripped of the scent of boiling tallow and cheap barley wine that clung to the market stalls. Each step is deeply hollowed by centuries of pilgrim boots and mule hooves, slick with a thin skin of black ice that demands your full attention.

The massive bronze tongue on your back shifts its weight, reminding you of the long miles still remaining to Lowgate.

nodes.brief: The great hemp cables of the upper market recede into the gray haze as you shoulder your heavy burden toward the terrace tiers.

exits.label: Press on toward the terrace tiers

nodes.title: Toward the Terrace Tiers
nodes.page:
Great hemp cables of the upper market recede into the gray haze as you shoulder the cradle toward the terrace tiers. The chaotic clatter of winches and shouting traders gives way to the rhythmic, distant groan of giant wooden windmills turning somewhere below the cloud line. Loose shale rattles beneath your boots with every stride, threatening to send small cascades of stone over the precipice edge into the empty gulf.

You keep your center of gravity low, leaning into the mountain face as the path narrows.

nodes.brief: A cold draft rushes up from the barley terraces below, smelling of damp earth, woodsmoke, and the distant turning of giant wooden sails.

exits.label: Press on against the cold draft

nodes.title: Draft from the Barley Terraces
nodes.page:
Cold draft rushes up from the barley terraces below, smelling of damp earth, woodsmoke, and the distant turning of giant wooden sails. The wind here has an unobstructed sweep across the cliff face, testing your balance and tugging hard at the heavy cradle strapped to your back. Scraps of old straw and frozen stubble cling to the stone lips of the path, marking the boundary where the bustling markets yield to the lonely agricultural ledges.

You grip the shoulder straps tighter, bracing against the sudden gusts.

nodes.brief: You leave the frantic noise of the rope-sellers behind, your boots finding a steady rhythm on the ancient stone steps leading down.

exits.label: Press on along the ancient steps

nodes.title: Leaving the Rope-Sellers Behind
nodes.page:
You leave the frantic noise of the rope-sellers behind as your boots take the ancient stone steps down into the shadow of the mountain. The sheer rock face rises steeply to your right, weeping tiny crystal tears of meltwater that instantly freeze into glassy beads on the gray surface. Below, the world drops away in dizzying tiers of gray mist and jagged slate, broken only by the distant geometry of the high agricultural works.

You hitch the clapper firm and keep your eyes on the path.

nodes.brief: Enticed by a high-stakes dice game on a swaying rope-platform, you wager your sacred guild transit pass and lose it over the abyss to cheating card-sharks.
nodes.title: The Flayed Pass
nodes.page: Silver coins spin under the cold grease-lamps of the swaying platform, and the flash of a marked deck draws your tired eyes from the heavy bronze bulk on your back. You stake your guild transit pass against a roll of foreign copper, trusting the quick shuffle of a dealer whose smile is too sharp for the high air. The paper flutters from his thumb, catches the sudden mountain updraft, and spirals down into the white wool of the clouds below without a sound. Without the green wax of the guild, the toll-keepers bar the stairs at the middle gate, leaving you to winter in the drafty shacks of the rope-markets as an outlawed drifter. Biscuit shifts his weight against the frozen rail, huffing a cloud of warm breath into the dusk while the mountain slowly closes its gates around you.

nodes.brief: You attempt to leap an icy gap in the swinging market bridges while carrying the heavy bronze clapper, and plunge into the mist.
nodes.title: The Frozen Slip
nodes.page:
Ice crusts the narrow gap between the swinging market bridges. Your boots slip as a sudden gust catches the bronze clapper on your back. The weight pulls you backward off balance, tearing the shoulder straps from your fingers with a sharp snap of hemp. You tumble out into the open gray air, watching the swinging stalls and the tiny figures of the rope-sellers recede upward into the mist.

There is only the rushing wind in your ears and the cold, bright freedom of the long fall.

nodes.brief: Arrival in The Windmill Terraces: stepped barley terraces in thin air, windmill-keepers whose harvest bell is silent, hard bargains, wind-calls that carry between mills. The reader enters with several ways forward.

exits.label: Follow the main stair
Cut across the lower ledges

exits.intent: Ask the way of a stranger
exits.label: Ask the way of a stranger
Take the old carriers' path

nodes.title: The Windmill Terraces
nodes.page:
Stepped barley terraces cling desperately to the sheer mountain face in the thin, freezing air, where silent harvest bells hang motionless from carved wooden frames. Windmill-keepers eye you with hard, hungry stares from shuttered doorways, guarding their meager grain stores while low wind-calls echo mournfully between the creaking towers. The path splits here into several distinct routes, each offering its own hazard and bargaining opportunity among the turning sails.

The heavy bronze clapper shifts against your tired spine as you weigh your next step.

nodes.brief: Mandatory scene at the Rumour Mill: two rival rumours about the Lowgate foundry; the reader decides which to believe, and it will colour how they act

exits.intent: Believe the foundry still stands and is hiring
exits.label: Believe the foundry still stands and is hiring

exits.intent: Believe the foundry flooded and went cold
exits.label: Believe the foundry flooded and went cold

nodes.title: Whispers in the Flour-Dust
nodes.page:
Two contradictory tales drift across the grease-stained tables of the milling-house like mountain mist. One group of millers insists the Lowgate forge remains fully manned and desperate for apprentices, while another swears the entire lower district went under water when the river-wall breached last night. The bronze tongue rests against your back as the afternoon wind edges toward bitter.

Your choice here shapes every hard bargain and closed door you will face as you descend the remaining stone steps toward the valley floor.

nodes.brief: Mandatory scene at the Miller's Lesson: a Terrace Miller offers to teach their wind-calls in a night, at the cost of a day

exits.intent: Stay a night and learn the wind-calls
exits.label: Stay a night and learn the wind-calls
Press on without the lesson

nodes.title: The Miller's Bargain
nodes.page:
On the eighth barley tier, an old miller blocks the narrow stair with a wooden measuring-rod, offering to teach the secret grammar of gale-notes in a single night. The instruction promises safe passage through the treacherous wind-funnels ahead, but trading the hours means losing a full day against the fast-approaching ice-season. The bronze clapper knocks against your spine, impatient with every moment spent still on the frozen slate.

Biscuit lowers his head to nuzzle a patch of crusted snow, indifferent to the hard choice hanging in the thin mountain air.

nodes.brief: Leaving The Windmill Terraces for The Glacier Ladders: close this part of the journey.

exits.label: Go on into the moving ice

nodes.title: Leaving The Terraces
nodes.page: Leaving The Windmill Terraces behind, you slip past the final barrier and commit your weight to the hanging paths that cross the upper reaches of the glacier. The air grows sharper and thinner as the stone stairways give way to swaying iron and hemp bridges suspended over bottomless blue crevasses. Every breath scrapes your lungs, but the bronze clapper's low knock reminds you that the foundry at Lowgate waits far below in the valley mist.

nodes.brief: On the high stone shelf of Tenth Tier, you step between two shuttered windmills while the heavy bronze clapper shifts against your tired spine.

exits.label: Duck beneath a spinning canvas sweep
Stop and speak with old Mara
Brace against the sudden eddy

nodes.title: Tenth Tier Shuttered Mills
nodes.page: High stone shelves of the Tenth Tier give little cover as you pick your way between two shuttered windmills, the bronze clapper shifting against your tired spine. Overhead the canvas sweeps groan in the rising gale, slap wet against wooden spars, and millers you cannot see work the brakes inside. Frost glitters on the iron axle-pins, and the scent of crushed barley and frozen grease hangs thick in the drafty corridor between the buildings.

nodes.brief: Frost rims the axle of the uppermost mill-wheel where Miller Garrow demands a toll before you cross his turning blades.

exits.label: Pay the toll with a heavy coin
Duck beneath the turning wheel's sweep
Bargain with the stubborn miller for passage

nodes.title: Toll at the Wheel
nodes.page:
Frost rims the axle of the uppermost mill-wheel where Miller Garrow demands a toll before you cross his turning blades. The bronze clapper presses into your spine as you shift on the frozen stone and watch a blur of canvas sweep dangerously close to your ear.

Garrow taps an iron coin-tray with a calloused thumb, his eyes narrowed against the biting mountain wind that shrieks across the terraced fields.

nodes.brief: Biscuit digs her stubborn hooves into the grey grit of the barley path as a sudden gust of mountain wind rattles the flour-sacks.

exits.label: Pull the mule past the gusty gap
Wait out the gale in the lee of the wall

exits.privWhy: the reader owes nobody and can bargain freely
exits.label: Slip through the secret drainage past the post

nodes.title: The Stubborn Mule
nodes.page:
Biscuit digs his stubborn hooves into the grey grit of the barley path as a sudden gust of mountain wind rattles the flour-sacks piled high against the stone wall. While you tug gently on the beast's leather halter, the bronze clapper taps a low note against your tired shoulders.

Across the narrow terrace, a row of silent harvest bells sways slightly in the draft, their iron tongues muffled by thick bands of grease and wool.

nodes.brief: A rusted iron wind-pipe hums against your ear on the cliff edge, carrying sharp snatches of argument from the miller's courtyard below.

exits.label: Follow the pipe down to the courtyard
Climb the stone parapet to avoid the noise
Press onward along the narrow cliff ledge

nodes.title: Voices on the Wind
nodes.page:
A rusted iron wind-pipe presses cold against your ear on the cliff edge and carries sharp snatches of argument from the miller's courtyard below through the freezing air. You press your shoulder against the damp stone, listening to the bitter dispute over barley prices and broken axle-trees while the weight of the clapper pulls you downward.

The cold metal vibrates with every rising shriek of the gale, singing a thin, metallic tune that matches the rhythm of your own racing pulse.

nodes.brief: You duck beneath a spinning canvas sweep that groans against the gale, risking a broken rib to save seconds on the downward track.

exits.label: Shout insults back at the angry miller
Crawl beneath the low stone trestle
Step onto the vibrating timber gallery

nodes.title: Ducking the Canvas
nodes.page:
You duck beneath a spinning canvas sweep that groans against the gale, risking a broken rib to save seconds on the downward track. The coarse fabric grazes your woolen cap with a sharp snap, kicking up a flurry of ice crystals that sting your cheeks.

Behind you, the huge wooden arms of the mill continue their rhythmic pounding against the sky like the wings of a trapped giant.

nodes.brief: Old Mara blocks the stone door of her grain-store with a flour scoop, refusing passage unless you recite the proper miller's blessing.

exits.label: Crawl beneath the low stone trestle
Distract the children clustering near Biscuit
Take the steep ice-glazed stone steps downward

nodes.title: The Grain-Store Door
nodes.page:
Old Mara blocks the stone door of her grain-store with a flour scoop, refusing passage unless you recite the proper miller's blessing. White dust clings to her eyebrows and eyelashes, making her look like a creature carved from compacted winter sleet.

The bronze clapper rests heavy and cold against your back as you search your memory for the ancient words taught in the high monastery.

nodes.brief: A sudden eddy catches the bronze clapper on your back, threatening to tip you backward off the narrow terrace wall into the gray mist.

exits.label: Shoo away the hungry terrace children
Step onto the vibrating timber gallery

nodes.title: The Narrow Wall
nodes.page:
A sudden eddy catches the bronze clapper on your back, threatening to tip you backward off the narrow terrace wall into the gray mist. You throw your weight forward against the cold stone, fingers digging into the frozen mortar between the slate blocks.

Below your dangling boots, nothing exists except a bottomless ocean of clouds churned white by the mountain wind.

nodes.brief: You shelter in the drafty lee of a barley hopper where a shivering apprentice offers you a crust of hard rye bread for a copper.

exits.label: Descend the steep ice-glazed stone steps
Dodge the flying wooden shutter overhead
Confront Miller Caden at the lower gate

nodes.title: Hard Rye Bread
nodes.page:
You shelter in the drafty lee of a barley hopper where a shivering apprentice offers you a crust of hard rye bread for a copper. The boy's fingers are blue with cold as he clutches a wooden oil-lamp that flickers wildly in the drafts whistling through the timber planks.

The smell of damp grain and stale yeast fills your lungs, offering a momentary refuge from the biting gale outside.

nodes.brief: The rope-bridge across the miller's irrigation trench sags dangerously under your weight while freezing meltwater spits from the rocks above.

exits.label: Pay the exorbitant inspection fee at the gate

exits.privWhy: the reader swore the knot-oath and is known by the ropewrights for it
exits.label: Use the private winch-house stairs with your knot-oath

nodes.title: The Irrigation Trench
nodes.page:
The rope-bridge across the miller's irrigation trench sags dangerously under your weight while freezing meltwater spits from the rocks above. Each hemp strand groans in protest as the icy spray turns the wooden slats slick as river glass.

You keep your center of gravity low and balance the bronze tongue against the violent sway of the bridge.

nodes.brief: Two bickering millers haul sacks of gray grain across your path, neither willing to yield an inch of the slippery limestone ledge.

exits.privWhy: the reader swore the knot-oath and is known by the ropewrights for it
exits.label: Unlock the private winch-house stairs proudly
Take the steep ice-glazed stone steps downward

nodes.title: Blocked Path
nodes.page:
Two bickering millers haul sacks of gray grain across your path, neither willing to yield an inch of the slippery limestone ledge. Their angry shouts echo off the stone walls while Biscuit rolls his eyes and snorts plumes of white vapor into the freezing air.

The heavy clapper shifts uneasily in its leather cradle, reminding you of the ticking time before the high passes freeze shut.

nodes.brief: You squeeze through a narrow cleft between two stone grain-bins where the smell of stale yeast and wet wool hangs thick in the air.

exits.label: Venture into the damp mountain fog
Help the frantic miller wedge the brake-beam
Pause in the shadow of the silent windmill

nodes.title: The Narrow Cleft
nodes.page:
You squeeze through a narrow cleft between two stone grain-bins where the smell of stale yeast and wet wool hangs thick in the air. The rough granite walls scrape against the leather straps of your burden, testing the stitches that hold the clapper's cradle together.

Emerging on the far side, you find yourself knee-deep in a drift of dry chaff driven here by the relentless gale.

nodes.brief: Because you owe nothing to any guild, a friendly miller waves you past his toll-post through a secret drainage chute that cuts the descent in half.

exits.label: Slip down the dark limestone drainage chute
Leap to assist the struggling miller at the brake-beam
Balance carefully across the trembling irrigation plank

priv.why: the reader owes nobody and can bargain freely

nodes.title: The Secret Chute
nodes.page:
Recognizing the simple brass ring on your collar that marks you as bound to no greedy guild, the old miller spits into the chaff and jerks his thumb toward a narrow, grease-blackened chute carved straight through the limestone. This steep drainage slide bypasses the lower toll-gates entirely, cutting your descent through the barley terraces cleanly in half.

You adjust the padded bronze clapper on your back and weigh the damp chill of the stone tunnel against the open path ahead.

nodes.brief: A small pack-mule has slipped its tether near the cliff edge, and its frantic kicking threatens to send your own beast tumbling into the abyss.

exits.label: Seize the panicked pack-mule by its swinging halter
Duck into the shelter of the silent, skeletal windmill

nodes.title: The Tangled Tether
nodes.page:
A frantic pack-mule has slipped its woven halter near the crumbling rim of the terrace, kicking out wildly with iron-shod hooves as its load shifts over the grey emptiness. Every violent thrash threatens to tangle its lead rope with Biscuit's harness, dragging your own stubborn beast toward the sheer drop.

You brace your boots against the frost-rimmed soil, reaching out a hand to grab the thrashing animal's bridle before the whole ledge gives way.

nodes.brief: You steady your breathing against the biting frost as the great canvas sails of Mill Ten shriek overhead in a sudden squall.

exits.label: Skirt the edge of the chasm along the vibrating plank
Duck your head and charge directly into the swirling mist

nodes.title: The Screaming Canvas
nodes.page:
Great canvas sails of Mill Ten shriek overhead like trapped gales, tearing at their wooden yardarms as a sudden squall sweeps across the high barley terraces. You press your shoulder against the cold stone wall and slow your breath while the bronze clapper on your back answers the roaring wind.

Ice-grit stings your cheeks as you weigh whether to push forward into the blinding white flurry or seek temporary shelter inside the churning mill.

nodes.brief: Miller Hobb leans from an upper window to hurl insults at your heavy burden, claiming the bronze clapper brings bad luck to his grinding stones.

exits.label: Scramble down the shifting grey shale of the scree-slope
Accept the warm barley-water and trade news with Jago

nodes.title: Miller Hobb's Curse
nodes.page:
Miller Hobb leans his greasy shoulders out from an upper stone casement, screaming jagged curses down at the heavy bronze clapper strapped across your spine. He insists that carrying the tongue of a broken sacred bell brings foul weather and blighted grain to every grinding stone in the district.

You ignore his spittle-flecked warnings, tightening the leather shoulder straps as the bronze hums softly against your jacket, shivering with cold and ancient memory.

nodes.brief: You crawl beneath a low stone trestle supporting the main drive-shaft while greasy machine-oil drips onto your padded shoulder harness.

exits.label: Pick your way down the unstable shale slope
Stop for a steaming mug of barley-water with Jago

nodes.title: Beneath the Drive-Shaft
nodes.page:
Thick machine-oil drips in slow plops onto your padded shoulder harness as you crawl on hands and knees beneath the low stone trestle that holds the main drive-shaft. The massive wooden axle groans above your head, turning with a rhythmic, bone-deep thump that rattles your teeth in your gums.

You squeeze through the grease-stained gap, keeping your profile low to avoid the turning iron bolts of the giant overhead cogs.

nodes.brief: A group of hungry terrace children cluster around Biscuit, trying to pry loose the leather straps holding your precious metal cargo.

exits.label: Trade stories and news with Miller Jago by the kiln
Squeeze past the straining winch and the wet grain sacks
Turn back toward the upper heights against the rising wind

nodes.title: The Terrace Children
nodes.page:
A cluster of hungry, soot-smudged terrace children swarms around Biscuit, tugging eagerly at the leather straps that secure your precious metal cargo with sticky fingers and wide eyes. Their small voices rise in a piping chorus of demands for crusts of bread or bright bits of scrap bronze.

You shoo them gently away with a dry word, checking the buckles of the clapper's cradle to ensure no small hands have worked them loose.

nodes.brief: You step onto the vibrating timber gallery of Mill Twelve just as the massive granite millstones grind to a sudden, shrieking halt.

exits.label: Squeeze past the straining winch and the wet grain sacks
Fight against the fierce crosswind twisting your shoulder straps
Turn back uphill toward the frosty axle of the upper wheel

nodes.title: The Millstone Grinds to a Halt
nodes.page:
Timbers shake beneath your boots on the open gallery of Mill Twelve just as the granite millstones grind to a sudden shrieking halt with a smell of scorched beechwood. The miller curses loudly from the shadowy interior, kicking at a jammed wooden cog while the drive-belt slacks and thrashes.

You pause against the railing, bracing the bronze clapper as the mountain wind whistles through the empty grain chutes.

nodes.brief: A steep flight of ice-glazed stone steps cuts downward through the barley fields, forcing you to unclip Biscuit and lead her by hand.

exits.label: Navigate the labyrinth of low stone storage sheds

exits.privWhy: the reader carries a Ropewrights' Guild rope and is waved through guild places
exits.label: Show your guild-woven rope to pass the terrace guards

nodes.title: The Ice-Glazed Stair
nodes.page:
A precipitous flight of stone steps cuts straight down through the frozen barley fields, glazed thick with blue ice from a burst irrigation pipe. The steepness leaves no room for error, forcing you to unclip Biscuit's lead and guide him down step by careful step by hand.

Your hobnails scratch for purchase on the slippery limestone while the bronze tongue slides and digs at your padded shoulders.

nodes.brief: You dodge a flying wooden shutter torn loose by the gale, watching it spin end-over-end into the white clouds far below.

exits.label: Squeeze past the straining winch and the wet grain sacks
Navigate the labyrinth of low stone storage sheds

exits.privWhy: the reader carries a Ropewrights' Guild rope and is waved through guild places
exits.label: Show your guild-woven rope to pass the terrace guards
Turn back along the cliff edge toward the humming wind-pipe

nodes.title: Flying Timber
nodes.page:
A massive wooden shutter tears loose from its iron hinges in the howling gale, spinning end-over-end past your face and vanishing into the white abyss of clouds far below. You flatten yourself against the rough stone wall of the mill-house, feeling the back-draft pull at the heavy metal cradle on your spine.

The thin mountain air burns your lungs as you wait for the gust to break before making your next move down the cliff.

nodes.brief: Miller Caden blocks the lower terrace gate with a stout ash pole, demanding an exorbitant inspection fee for your heavy bronze cargo.

exits.label: Wait out the stubborn sheep blocking the narrow stone stair
Catch your balance on the timber railing near the flour-chutes
Listen to Miller Voss mutter warnings through his spy-glass
Turn back against the wind along the upper barley path

nodes.title: Miller Caden's Toll
nodes.page:
Miller Caden plants his stout ash pole firmly across the lower terrace gate, barring the path with a scowl and demanding an exorbitant inspection fee for your heavy bronze cargo. His fingers drum impatiently on the polished wood while he eyes the precious metal on your back with greedy calculation.

You stand your ground in the thin air, considering whether to pay his steep price or look for a way around his gate.

nodes.brief: Because you wear the rope-wrights' knot-oath proudly, the gate-keeper unlocks the private winch-house stairs and lets you descend unhindered.

exits.label: Descend the private winch-house stairs carefully

priv.why: the reader swore the knot-oath and is known by the ropewrights for it

nodes.title: The Knotted Gate
nodes.page:
Because you wear the rope-wrights' knot-oath proudly pinned to your woollen collar, the old gate-keeper recognizes the binding loop at a glance and unlocks the private winch-house stairs without a single grumble about tolls or cargo weights. You slip past the heavy iron latch, leaving the main terrace track behind as you descend into the shadowed stone stairwell where the air smells of hemp, tallow, and cold mountain grease.

The bronze clapper shifts in its padded cradle on your back and knocks faintly against your spine as you test the first frost-slick step.

nodes.brief: A damp shroud of mountain fog rolls over the terraces, reducing visibility to a single arm's length and muffling the great wind-pipes.

exits.label: Peer through the cracked spy-glass ahead
Hurry past the silent, empty windmills
Brace against the flurry of wet snow

nodes.title: Shrouded Terraces
nodes.page:
A damp shroud of mountain fog rolls suddenly over the barley terraces, reducing visibility to a single arm's length and muffling the great wooden wind-pipes until they sound like distant, groaning giants. The familiar stone path dissolves into grey nothingness on either side of your boots, leaving you to guide your steps entirely by the rhythmic crunch of gravel and the dull, comforting weight of the bronze clapper on your back.

You pause to listen through the thick mist, trying to distinguish the whistle of a guide-rope from the treacherous drop of the outer retaining wall.

nodes.brief: You help a frantic miller wedge a jammed brake-beam into place before his runaway wheel shatters the entire stone wall.

exits.label: Slip past near the flour chutes
Hurry past the silent empty windmills

nodes.title: The Runaway Wheel
nodes.page:
You throw your shoulder against a straining wooden beam just as a frantic miller screams for help, wedging the jammed brake-shoe firmly back into place before the screaming runaway wheel can shatter the entire terrace wall into the abyss. The miller gasps his thanks, wiping flour and sweat from his forehead with a sleeve while the massive oak blades above slow their frantic rotation with a deep, shuddering groan.

The bronze clapper rattles once in its cradle from the sudden jolt, but the straps hold fast as you catch your breath against the cold stone.

nodes.brief: The path narrows to a single plank bridging a deep irrigation chasm where the roar of rushing glacial meltwater deafens your ears.

exits.label: Inspect the path through the spy-glass
Face the sudden flurry of wet snow

nodes.title: The Glacier Chasm
nodes.page:
The path narrows abruptly to a single wet pine plank bridging a deep irrigation chasm, where the deafening roar of rushing glacial meltwater shakes the very air in your lungs and sends freezing spray across your face. You grip the guide-rope with frozen fingers, balancing the heavy bronze tongue of the great bell against the violent updraft as you inch across the roaring void one careful boot-length at a time.

Below the wooden bridge, white water smashes against jagged boulders before plunging over the edge of the terrace tier.

nodes.brief: You pause in the shadow of a silent windmill whose broken timber vanes hang motionless like the ribs of a starved beast.

exits.label: Step into the flurry of wet snow
Retighten the pack-girth on Biscuit
Listen to the mournful wind-pipe ahead

nodes.title: The Skeleton Mill
nodes.page:
You pause in the shadow of a silent windmill whose broken timber vanes hang motionless like the bleached ribs of a starved beast against the grey sky. The wind has died away entirely in this rocky pocket. Only your ragged breathing and the faint persistent note of the bronze clapper against your spine remain.

The mule, Biscuit, shakes his dusty ears and stamps a hoof against the frozen dirt, eager to leave the dead machinery behind.

nodes.brief: A sharp whistle echoes from the mist above, warning all terrace folk to batten down their hatches against an incoming gale.

exits.label: Follow the mournful moan of the wind-pipe

nodes.title: The Warning Whistle
nodes.page:
A sharp, piercing whistle echoes down from the mist above, carrying the unmistakable terrace signal that warns all folk to batten down their hatches against an incoming gale. Across the barley shelves, shutters slam and heavy timber bars drop into place with hollow thuds that ripple through the mountain face like small drumbeats.

You pull your woollen hood lower over your forehead and lean hard into the mounting pressure of the cold air rushing up from the valley floor.

nodes.brief: You scramble across a scree-slope of loose shale that gives way beneath your boots, sending grey stones clattering into the void.

exits.label: Cross the threshold of the weighing-shed
Approach the tired miller by the crate

nodes.title: The Shifting Scree
nodes.page:
You scramble across a treacherous scree-slope of loose shale that gives way suddenly beneath your boots, sending a cascade of grey stones clattering out into the blinding white void of the cloud sea. Your arms pinwheel for a frantic second as you fight for balance, leaning back against the bronze clapper to keep from sliding down the steep incline.

The shale settles with a final, hollow rattle, leaving you clinging to the rock face with shaking fingers.

nodes.brief: Miller Jago offers a mug of warm barley-water in exchange for news of the storm damage up at Orisonhold's high sanctuary.

exits.label: Enter the communal weighing-shed
Speak with the weary miller near the crate

nodes.title: The Miller's Mug
nodes.page:
Miller Jago offers a steaming mug of warm barley-water across a flour-dusted counter in exchange for news of the storm damage up at Orisonhold's high sanctuary. The thick, sweet liquid burns agreeably in your frozen throat as you recount the tearing of the great roof timbers and the silent crack in the shoulder of Orison.

The old miller nods slowly, his scarred hands wrapping around his own cup while he gazes up toward the cloud-shrouded peak with quiet dread.

nodes.brief: You squeeze past a straining winch where two terrace workers struggle to hoist a sodden sack of grain from the valley floor.

exits.label: Step inside the communal weighing-shed
Approach the tired miller by the crate
Dodge the rolling barley cask near the wall

nodes.title: The Hoisting Winch
nodes.page:
You squeeze past a straining wooden winch where two terrace workers grunt in rhythm, desperately trying to hoist a sodden sack of un-milled grain up from the lower cable-way before the tension snaps. Hemp ropes groan under the immense strain, shedding frayed fibers that drift down into the misty depths like grey snow.

You tuck your elbows tight to your ribs to protect the clapper's cradle from the swinging cargo bags.

nodes.brief: A fierce crosswind catches the clapper's cradle, twisting your shoulder straps painfully as you fight to keep your footing on the ice.

exits.label: Approach the weary miller by the crate
Dodge the rolling barley cask near the wall

nodes.title: The Crosswind Ridge
nodes.page:
A fierce, erratic crosswind sweeps across the open terrace shelf, catching the heavy bronze clapper's cradle and twisting your leather shoulder straps painfully into your flesh. You plant your staff deep into the frozen mud, leaning your entire body weight sideways to fight the sudden gust before it can sweep you off the narrow path.

Biscuit braces his sturdy legs against the stone wall, blowing a cloud of frosty steam from his nostrils as the gale shriek fades into a low whistle.

nodes.brief: You navigate a labyrinth of low stone storage sheds where the pungent aroma of fermented barley mash fills the freezing air.

exits.label: Descend toward the lower terrace steps
Dodge the rolling barley cask ahead

nodes.title: Labyrinth of Fermented Mash
nodes.page:
Sharp fumes of fermenting grain sting your eyes as you wind through low stone storage sheds. Stacks of damp malt bags press close against the narrow passage, and the bronze clapper knocks a low note against your spine in the cold mountain draught.

Two dark alleyways branch away between the barrel-vaulted roofs, one leading down toward the shadowed lower shelf and the other winding past an unsecured loading dock.

nodes.brief: Because you carry a genuine guild-woven rope, the terrace guards salute your passage and point out a sheltered shortcut through the grain lofts.

exits.label: Approach the tired miller resting near crates
Step out into the muddy pack-mule courtyard
Follow the scent of woodsmoke and dried mash

priv.why: the reader carries a Ropewrights' Guild rope and is waved through guild places

nodes.title: Shortcut Through the Grain Lofts
nodes.page:
Because your shoulder strap bears a genuine guild-woven rope, the terrace guards snap a crisp salute and wave you past the heavy iron gate. They point out a dry, sheltered shortcut through the cavernous grain lofts, sparing you the bitter teeth of the open ledge.

Dust motes dance in the slanted shafts of sunlight piercing the timber rafters overhead while muffled voices echo from the storage bins below.

nodes.brief: A stubborn sheep blocks the narrow stone stair, refusing to budge until Biscuit lowers her head and nudges it aside with a huff.

exits.label: Approach the tired miller near the crates
Dodge the rolling barley cask on the left
Enter the muddy courtyard past the tethered mules

nodes.title: Blocked Stair and Stubborn Mule
nodes.page:
A thick-fleeced mountain sheep plants its hooves firmly on the narrow stone stair, stubbornly refusing to yield an inch of the path. Biscuit lowers his grey head, exhales a cloud of frosty breath, and gives the woolly obstruction a solid, patient nudge until it clatters aside.

The path ahead divides around a massive stone water-trough frozen solid with grey ice.

nodes.brief: You slip on a patch of black ice near the flour- chutes, barely catching yourself on a timber railing before dropping your cargo.

exits.label: Follow the scent of woodsmoke and dry grain
Seek the clerk checking parchment by candlelight

nodes.title: Black Ice at the Chutes
nodes.page:
Your boot heel catches on a treacherous sheet of black ice near the timber flour-chutes, pitching you sideways into a rough wooden railing. You throw out an arm just in time to save the heavy clapper from crashing against the stones, leaving your fingers aching from the jarring impact.

Across the narrow ledge, two distinct routes beckon through the swirling mist.

nodes.brief: Miller Voss peers suspiciously at the bronze clapper through a cracked spy-glass, muttering dark warnings about cursed temple metal.

exits.label: Approach the miller resting by dusty crates
Step out toward the muddy pack-mule courtyard
Head toward the scent of woodsmoke and mash

nodes.title: Suspicious Miller's Spy-Glass
nodes.page:
Miller Voss peers intently through a cracked brass spy-glass, squinting with one eye at the bronze clapper strapped to your frame. He mutters dark warnings about cursed temple metal bringing bad luck to the barley harvest, his fingers twitching nervously against his leather apron.

The stone path stretches out on either side of his wooden post, offering two distinct ways forward.

nodes.brief: You hurry past a row of silent, empty windmills whose black apertures stare out across the dizzying drop like sightless eyes.

exits.label: Dodge the loose cask near the drystone wall
Enter the muddy courtyard where mules wait
Approach the clerk by the flickering tallow candle

nodes.title: Row of Silent Windmills
nodes.page:
You hurry past a row of silent, empty windmills whose black apertures stare out across the dizzying drop like sightless eyes. Their wooden sails are lashed fast against the rising gales, leaving the terrace eerily quiet save for the rhythmic crunch of your boots on frozen gravel.

The path splits ahead, leading toward different corners of the sprawling milling district.

nodes.brief: A sudden flurry of wet snow blinds your eyes, turning the steep stone steps into a treacherous slide of slush and mud.

exits.label: Seek shelter near the smoking hearth
Squeeze past the gossiping mill-hands below

nodes.title: The Slush-Stair Descent
nodes.page:
Heavy, wet flakes swirl out of the bruised grey sky, instantly coating the steep stone steps in a treacherous grease of freezing slush and clinging mud. Every boot-heel slides perilously against the shale, and the leaden weight of the bronze clapper on your back threatens to tip your balance toward the sheer abyss.

You steady yourself against a low retaining wall of dry-stacked granite, your breath pluming white and sharp in the sudden squall. Down through the swirling whiteout, a faint glow of amber light beckons from an overhanging eave, while a narrower side-passage offers a sheltered route away from the open precipice.

nodes.brief: You pause to retighten Biscuit's pack-girth where the vibration of the great grinding stones has shaken the leather loose.

exits.label: Follow the trail smelling of woodsmoke and mash
Squeeze past the gossiping mill-hands near the arch

nodes.title: Tightening the Pack-Girth
nodes.page:
You pause against a rough stone pillar to retighten Biscuit's pack-girth, where the constant, bone-shaking vibration of the great grinding stones has worked the thick leather loose. The mule stamps a hoof patiently against the frost while you pull the knot tight with numb fingers.

The path runs on past the slow knock of the mills.

nodes.brief: The wind-pipe beside the trail emits a long, mournful moan as the pressure shifts across the terraces ahead of the storm.

exits.label: Step into the sheltered lee of the Rumour Mill

nodes.title: Mournful Wind-Pipe Moan
nodes.page:
A hollow wind-pipe mounted beside the trail emits a long, mournful moan as pressure shifts across the stone terraces ahead of the storm. The metallic moan mingles with the faint knock of the bronze clapper on your back, and the chord they make sets your teeth on edge.

The path narrows sharply as it plunges into the sheltered lee of the district's social heart.

nodes.brief: You cross the threshold of the communal weighing-shed where greasy iron scales hang suspended from a blackened cedar beam.

exits.label: Listen to Tanner whisper near the dark rafters
Catch the nervous trader's talk by the mugs

nodes.title: The Weighing-Shed
nodes.page:
Cold drafts whistle through the slatted cedar walls of the communal weighing-shed, where greasy iron scales hang suspended from a blackened overhead beam. You duck inside to escape the biting mountain drift; the bronze clapper clicks softly against its padded leather cradle as you shrug the wind from your shoulders.

Several large sacks of barley are stacked against the damp floorboards, bearing the seal of the Terrace Millers' proud guild. A ledger lies open on a trestle table near the iron weights, its ink smudged by moisture, waiting for an entry that no one has marked.

nodes.brief: A tired miller rests his calloused hands on a flour-dusted crate, watching your approach with weary, measuring eyes.

exits.label: Step closer to speak with the miller

nodes.title: The Miller's Stare
nodes.page: Flour-dusted hands rest on a scarred timber crate, and weary eyes track your progress across the terrace stones. The old miller watches the bronze tongue shift in its padded cradle on your back, sizing your errand against the thin bitter mountain air.

nodes.brief: You dodge a rolling barley cask that breaks loose from a hand-cart and smashes into the low drystone wall beside the path.

exits.label: Dodge the debris and hurry down the trail

nodes.title: The Rolling Cask
nodes.page: Splintered wood explodes against the low drystone wall as a runaway barley cask shatters inches from your boots, showering the frosty path with grain. Biscuit shifts nervously against the ropes, ears pinned back against the whistling wind, while the frantic shouting of loaders echoes from the upper tier.

nodes.brief: The stone trail flattens into a muddy courtyard where several pack-mules are tethered outside the district's central gathering hall.

exits.label: Cut across the courtyard toward the stairs
Shelter briefly by the gathering hall wall

nodes.title: The Muddy Courtyard
nodes.page: Thick gray mud cakes the soles of your boots as the stone trail widens into a drafty central courtyard where a dozen pack-mules huddle in the lee of the district hall. Wet wool and damp chaff smell sharp here, cut by the clinking of harness rings and the low grumbling of resting drivers.

nodes.brief: You wipe the freezing condensation from your forehead as the air grows thick with the smell of woodsmoke and damp chaff.

exits.label: Seek warmth beside the smoking peat kiln
Ignore the smoke and press down the slope

nodes.title: Smoke and Chaff
nodes.page: Icy moisture clings to your brow and turns to frost as the scent of burning peat and sweet damp chaff rolls over you from the terrace kilns. The bronze Clapper keeps a faint counter-rhythm against your shoulder blades, vibrating deep in the padding as the mountain wind shifts.

nodes.brief: A nervous clerk checks names off a long parchment scroll by the light of a flickering tallow candle set in a tin sconce.

exits.label: Wait patiently for the clerk to look up
Slip quietly past the distracted clerk
Ask the clerk about the rumor mill

nodes.title: The Candlelit Scroll
nodes.page: Tallow drips steadily from a flickering tin sconce as a nervous clerk drags a quill down a long, grease-spotted parchment scroll by the side of the track. He mutters dates and quotas under his breath and barely glances up when your boots crunch on the gravel.

nodes.brief: You squeeze through a press of gossiping mill-hands who have gathered near the lower archway to escape the biting draft.

exits.label: Push through the crowd into the warm interior

nodes.title: The Archway Press
nodes.page: Shoulders brush and voices rise in sharp argument as you squeeze through a dense knot of gossiping mill-hands gathered beneath the stone lower archway for shelter. The biting draft cuts through your wool tunic, but the crowd's chatter provides a brief barrier against the worst of the mountain gust.

nodes.brief: The roar of the great valley wind fades into a low hum as you step into the sheltered lee of the Rumour Mill.

exits.label: Step inside the mill to escape the wind

nodes.title: Lee of the Mill
nodes.page: The frantic roar of the great valley wind drops to a soft mutter as you step into the shadowed overhang of the Rumour Mill. Inside, the air smells of stale ale and roasted barley, offering a brief respite from the biting chill that claws at your woolen cloak.

nodes.brief: Inside the dim rafters of the Rumour Mill, old Tanner whispers that the Lowgate foundry has already run out of tin and will reject all temple bronze.

exits.label: Press on regardless of Tanner's grim warning

nodes.title: Tanner's Warning
nodes.page: Shadows stretch long across the dim rafters of the Rumour Mill, where old Tanner leans close to whisper a dark warning about the valley below. He insists the Lowgate foundry has completely run out of tin and will reject all temple bronze, so your cradle would sit stranded in the cold.

nodes.brief: By the sputtering hearth of the Rumour Mill, a scarred smith claims the foundry furnaces are roaring hotter than ever and eager for the great bell's tongue.

exits.label: Press on toward the roaring valley forge

nodes.title: The Roaring Hearth
nodes.page: Red firelight flickers across a scarred smith's face near the sputtering hearth, where he loudly claims the foundry furnaces are roaring hotter than ever. He laughs off talk of scarcity, declaring the master-smiths are fiercely eager for the great bell's tongue to feed their blazing pits.

nodes.brief: Amidst the clatter of tin mugs in the Rumour Mill, a nervous trader insists the foundry has been seized by the Cable Court to forge debt-shackles.

exits.label: Demand proof from the merchant

nodes.title: The Rumour Mill
nodes.page:
Tin mugs chatter against grease-stained tables inside the drafty milling-house, where a nervous spice-trader leans across a cask to grab your sleeve. He insists the Cable Court's bailiffs have already seized the Lowgate foundry to recast your bronze Clapper into debt-shackles instead of a true voice for Orison. The air smells of wet barley and spilt small-beer while every miller at the hearth-bench turns to watch how you take the news.



You might stay to question the trembling merchant for details, or shoulder the padded cradle and leave the warm stone walls behind before the whispers harden into a blockade.

nodes.brief: Leaning against a sack of barley in the Rumour Mill, a one-eyed packer swears the foundry master has fled south, leaving the great pits cold and empty.

exits.label: Press on down the terrace path
Turn back toward the upper stairs

nodes.title: The One-Eyed Packer
nodes.page: A one-eyed packer leans against a dusty sack of barley inside the Rumour Mill, swearing by every knot in the rope-walk that the foundry master has fled south. He taps his glass against the cask and insists the great pits are cold, empty, and choked with ash before you can even catch your breath in the thin air. Biscuit fidgets in the narrow aisle while the bronze Clapper knocks a faint note against your shoulder blades.

nodes.brief: On the sun-bleached stone of the seventh terrace, Miller Garrow complains that the foundry has secretly bartered all its tin to the Cable Court.

exits.label: Ask about the upper cable tolls
Inspect the miller's grain-hoppers
Slip past toward the lower ladder

nodes.title: The Barter of Tin
nodes.page: Miller Garrow stands on the sun-bleached stone of the seventh terrace, his flour-dusted fingers gripping a wooden ledger as he complains about the valley's trade. He mutters that the Lowgate foundry has secretly bartered all its reserve tin to the Cable Court, leaving common apprentices with nothing to work. The cold mountain wind whistles through the wooden slats of the mill, carrying the dry scent of cracked barley and old grease. Biscuit stamps a hoof against the flags, eager to leave the grumblers behind.

nodes.brief: Beneath the idle canvas sails of mill nine, miller-wife Jella whispers that the forge-masters are hoarding fresh bronze to mint private tokens.

exits.privWhy: the reader travels without the mule, light and quick, and so notices what a pack-animal would crowd out
exits.label: Slip through the narrow grain aperture
Question her about the private mints
Lead the mule down the stone ramp

nodes.title: The Mint of Private Tokens
nodes.page: Canvas sails creak overhead as miller-wife Jella leans close beneath the wooden ribs of mill nine, whispering that the forge-masters are hoarding fresh bronze to mint private tokens. She taps her temple knowingly, claiming no bell will ever be recast until the profit-takers have filled their own pockets first. Pale sunlight cuts the loft and lights the dust, and the Clapper knocks once against your travel-worn leather pack as if answering the room.

nodes.brief: Beside the stone grain-hopper, Miller Orlo accuses you of carrying forged trade-permits in your pack-straps.

exits.label: Defend your honest papers
Offer a handful of salt
Force a path past the hopper

nodes.title: The Forged Permits
nodes.page: Miller Orlo blocks the doorway beside the stone grain-hopper, squinting suspiciously at the straps of your travel-pack while accusing you of carrying forged trade-permits. His flour-whitened eyebrows draw together in a harsh frown as he demands to inspect your papers before you take another step down the mountain. Biscuit lowers stubborn ears and snorts a cloud of white breath into the freezing air between you.

nodes.brief: Across the squeaking timber footbridge, miller-girl Tressa offers stale oat-cake in exchange for news of the upper snows.

exits.label: Trade news for the oat-cake
Ignore her and cross the bridge

exits.privWhy: the reader owes nobody and can bargain freely
exits.label: Share a secret shortcut with her

nodes.title: The Stale Oat-Cake
nodes.page: Tressa stands across the squeaking timber footbridge, holding out a dry piece of stale oat-cake in exchange for any scrap of news from the upper snows. Her fingers are red from the mountain chill, and her eyes scan the dizzying drops behind you with wary curiosity. The ropes of the nearby bridge hum a low, vibrating chord in the rising wind while Biscuit noses at an empty grain sack.

nodes.brief: In the drafty shadow of the great timber winch, miller Hael demands a toll of three copper groats for crossing his flour-chute.

exits.label: Pay the three copper groats
Barter with a length of cord
Duck beneath the rattling winch

nodes.title: The Flour-Chute Toll
nodes.page: A timber winch creaks in the drafty shadow above, where miller Hael bars the way and demands a toll of three copper groats to cross his flour-chute. He crosses thick, flour-dusted arms over his chest and watches the heavy bronze Clapper in its padded cradle with sharp, assessing eyes. The wind rattles the wooden shingles overhead like loose teeth.

nodes.brief: Unburdened by baggage, you slip through a narrow wheat-bin aperture, bypassing the blocked miller gate entirely.

exits.label: Descend the hidden cedar ladder
Follow the narrow wall ledge
Drop onto the lower timber catwalk

priv.why: the reader travels without the mule, light and quick, and so notices what a pack-animal would crowd out

nodes.title: The Narrow Wheat-Bin
nodes.page: Without the mule or bulky gear, you slip through a narrow wheat-bin aperture and bypass the blocked miller gate entirely. The passage smells of dry chaff and sweet grain as you squeeze between cool cedar planks into the damp air beyond. Light filters in through cracks in the siding, showing a steep, unused ladder dropping down the cliff face.

nodes.brief: Beside the sputtering grease-lamp of the flour-store, miller Fenn warns that the wind-pipes are choked with salt-dust.

exits.label: Clear the jammed wind-pipe
Warn the neighboring millers
Hurry down the interior steps
Check the grease-lamp levels

nodes.title: The Salt-Choked Wind-Pipes
nodes.page: Miller Fenn stands beside the sputtering grease-lamp of the flour-store, warning you with frantic gestures that the wind-pipes are choked with salt-dust from the lower flats. He points a soot-stained finger toward the groaning machinery overhead where white powder drifts like winter snow. The air tastes of brine and dry husk, biting the back of your throat with every breath.

nodes.brief: On the precipitous limestone stair, miller Bessa drops a sack of barley that scatters golden grain across your boots.

exits.label: Help her gather the spilled grain
Step carefully around the golden spill
Scold the clumsy miller sharply

nodes.title: The Scattered Barley
nodes.page: Miller Bessa drops a sack of barley on the precipitous limestone stair, and golden grain scatters in a bright cascade across your travel-worn boots. She mutters an oath against the mountain gales as the golden kernels bounce over the cliff edge into the cloud sea below. Biscuit immediately lowers his head to snap up a stray mouthful before you can catch your balance.

nodes.brief: Within the echoing stone loft of mill twelve, miller Corin sharpens his scythe while demanding news from Orisonhold.

exits.label: Follow the rattled beams toward the lower floor

exits.privWhy: the reader owes nobody and can bargain freely
exits.label: Barter your unburdened credit for an iron wedge

nodes.title: The Stone Loft
nodes.page:
Dust hangs thick in the echoing stone loft of mill twelve as miller Corin whets his broad scythe against an oilstone, stopping only to eye the padded cradle on your back with sharp suspicion. He demands to know what the high monks of Orisonhold are playing at while the barley rots in the frost, his thumb testing the newly polished edge with a soft hiss. The bronze Clapper knocks against your shoulder blades like a caged hornet, answering the scrape of steel.

Step past the grinding floor and head down toward the lower mills.

Seek a favorable trade with clean ledgers and an open hand.

nodes.brief: Beside the churning wooden mill-stone, miller Marna complains that the autumn gusts bring nothing but salt-grit and freezing mist.

exits.privWhy: the reader owes nobody and can bargain freely
exits.label: Trade your unburdened credit for a spare wedge
Duck beneath the flapping canvas wind-breaks outside
Slip into the dim flour-bin to mend your gear

nodes.title: The Grinding Stone
nodes.page:
A fine spray of salt-grit blows through the open shutter, settling over the churning wooden mill-stone where miller Marna shakes her head in bitter disgust. She complains that the autumn gales bring nothing useful from the heights, only freezing mist and low-altitude damp that spoils her winter milling. Biscuit shifts his weight against the stone wall outside, blowing a long, frosty breath through his soft grey muzzle as the canvas roof billows overhead.

Choose between pressing onward into the gathering gloom or seeking shelter among the rattling gears.

nodes.brief: Under the canvas canopy of mill fourteen, miller Dane barters handfuls of parched barley for a length of hempen twine.

exits.label: Step out onto the wind-lashed canvas terrace
Hide within the dim stone flour-bin from the gale
Turn back toward the sun-bleached seventh terrace

nodes.title: The Canvas Canopy
nodes.page: Under the snapping canvas canopy of mill fourteen, miller Dane measures handfuls of parched, grey-brown barley into a wooden measure, trading them away for a stout length of hempen twine. Bitter mountain wind tugs the roof-ropes and sings a thin, whining note through the timber that answers the faint knock of the Clapper on your back.

nodes.brief: On the wind-scoured balcony of mill fifteen, miller-widow Kella offers shelter from the rising gale for a pinch of pipe-leaf.

exits.label: Crawl inside the dim stone flour-bin for shelter
Climb toward the frost-slick balcony and signal cords

nodes.title: The Wind-Scoured Balcony
nodes.page:
Miller-widow Kella leans against the wooden railing of mill fifteen's wind-scoured balcony, watching the white clouds drift far below the mountain face like a frozen sea. She offers a warm corner out of the drafting wind if you can spare a pinch of dried pipe-leaf from your travel pouch, her weathered fingers already clutching a short clay pipe. The bronze tongue in its padded cradle warms against your spine and seems to draw the thin air deep into your lungs.

Choose whether to seek refuge in the dim flour-bin or climb toward the whistling signal cords.

nodes.brief: Beside the stone drying-kiln of mill sixteen, miller Tion pokes the glowing embers with a charred pine branch.

exits.label: Seek shelter inside the dim stone flour-bin
Press past the clattering wooden hopper and noisy gears
Step out onto the frost-slick balcony near the signal line

nodes.title: The Drying Kiln
nodes.page:
Red embers glow softly beside the stone drying-kiln of mill sixteen, where miller Tion idly pokes the slumbering fire with a charred pine branch while the milling stones turn overhead. The rising heat smells pleasantly of roasted grain and woodsmoke, driving the biting mountain chill from your travel-worn fingers for a brief, welcome moment. Biscuit stamps a hoof against the flagstones outside, eager to move before the heavy gray clouds settle any lower over the crags.

Select your path among the clattering hoppers and whistling balconies ahead.

nodes.brief: Owing no debts to the terrace folk, you trade a cheerful nod for a secret shortcut through the grain-drying loft.

exits.label: Advance toward the frost-slick balcony and signal cords
Descend toward the stone grinding-floor and spilled grain

priv.why: the reader owes nobody and can bargain freely

nodes.title: The Unencumbered Path
nodes.page:
Walking with clean ledgers and an unburdened pack opens doors that remain firmly bolted against the debt-ridden and the desperate. Miller Corin nods respectfully as you pass, letting you slip through a concealed door in the grain-drying loft where the sweet scent of dry oats fills the dim, warm air. The Clapper rests easy against your spine, clear of the bitter reckonings and bitterer coin-lenders of the upper terraces.

Choose whether to climb toward the freezing balcony or descend to the grinding floor.

nodes.brief: Under the rattling wooden gears of mill seventeen, miller Jory measures out black rye into a notched wooden scoop.

exits.label: Venture out onto the frost-slick stone balcony
Search the echoing timber loft for a quiet corner

nodes.title: The Wooden Gears
nodes.page: Wooden gears grind overhead with a deafening, wooden roar as miller Jory measures out dark rye into a notched wooden scoop, his eyes darting anxiously toward the darkening sky. The air tastes of dry chaff and old iron, and every timber in the loft shivers as a fresh gust strikes the great canvas sails outside. Against your padded frame the bronze Clapper taps softly, a deep pulse under the mountain's raw height.

nodes.brief: On the frost-rimed stone platform of mill eighteen, miller-boy Bram chases a stray goat away from the flour-sacks.

exits.label: Make your way toward the stone grinding-floor
Cross the dizzying rope-bridge toward the lower cables

nodes.title: The Stray Goat
nodes.page: Miller-boy Bram runs across the frost-rimed stone platform of mill eighteen, waving a knitted cap to drive a stubborn stray goat away from an open stack of flour-sacks. The animal leaps lightly over a coil of hempen rope, its small hooves clattering sharply against the frozen flags before disappearing around the corner of the kiln. The thin, clear air burns your throat with every breath, reminding you how far Orisonhold and the great cracked bell remain above.

nodes.brief: Within the dim flour-dust haze of mill nineteen, miller Sula scours a grease-stained wooden trough with river sand.

exits.label: Grease the groaning wooden axle with mutton tallow
Step onto the dizzying rope-bridge above the abyss
Approach the drafty flour-shed and its smoking peat fire

nodes.title: The Flour-Dust Haze
nodes.page:
River sand scrapes against a grease-stained wooden trough as miller Sula vigorously scours the vessel within the dim flour-dust haze of mill nineteen, paying little heed to your arrival. The air is thick with white particles that stick to your damp eyelashes and coat your woolen cloak in a fine, ghostly powder. Biscuit shakes his head stubbornly outside, his long ears twitching at the mournful whistle of the wind through the axle-beams.

Choose between greasing the iron journals, crossing the rope-bridge, or stoking the peat fire.

nodes.brief: Beside the churning wooden sluice-gate, miller Vane repairs a broken leather drive-belt with thick waxed thread.

exits.label: Head toward the stone grinding-floor and sweeping brooms
Venture onto the dizzying rope-bridge spanning the gorge

nodes.title: The Sluice-Gate
nodes.page:
Thick waxed thread snakes through a leather punch as miller Vane repairs a broken drive-belt beside the churning wooden sluice-gate of mill twenty. Ice forms rapidly along the wooden edges where the mountain runoff spills into the troughs, glittering like scattered salt in the pale afternoon light.
