nodes.title: Behind the Presses
nodes.page:
Crouching behind a stacked crate of cider-presses, you watch a hooded Warden blow three sharp warning notes into a brass whistle while mist clings to your wool. The piercing shrill echoes off the damp stone walls and vanishes into the orchard cloud. Your muscles cramp from holding still with the bronze tongue strapped tight against your spine. Biscuit stamps a hoof softly in the gloom, impatient for open ground.

The notes fade into a tense silence across the terrace. You can wait out the search in the shadows of the press, risk the freezing mountain tracks believing the lower forge has gone cold and seeking another way, or slip past the wooden frames into the deeper orchard fog.

nodes.brief: Beneath a canopy of frost-bitten russets, you crawl under a split timber rail while the mule's soft snort is muffled by thick white fog.

nodes.title: Beneath the Russets
nodes.page: Beneath a canopy of frost-bitten russets, you crawl under a split timber rail while the mule's soft snort is muffled by thick white fog. Frozen apples crunch beneath your knees, releasing a sharp tang of fermented cider into the damp air. The bronze clapper slides on your back and tips your balance toward the muddy earth. Somewhere through the grey gloom, a heavy boot-heel grates against slate, drawing uncomfortably close to your hiding spot.

nodes.brief: Edging along a sunken drainage ditch where rotting apples ferment in the damp, you pray the bronze weight on your back remains entirely silent.

nodes.title: The Sunken Ditch
nodes.page:
Edging along a sunken drainage ditch where rotting apples ferment in the damp, you pray the bronze weight on your back remains entirely silent. The heavy fog presses down from the mountain heights, blurring the gnarled shapes of the orchard trees into towering phantoms. Cold moisture drips steadily from your woollen cap, finding a path down the back of your neck. Every movement requires absolute care to avoid disturbing the loose shale lining the trench walls.

The path ahead branches into three distinct directions, each swallowed entirely by the impenetrable mountain mist.

nodes.title: The Sleeping Watchdog
nodes.page: Tiptoeing past a sleeping watchdog tethered to a pear trunk, you hold your breath as a wet pine-needle drops against your leather collar. The animal lets out a low, rumbling sigh in its sleep, its flank rising and falling against the damp moss. The bronze clapper feels like an anchor strapped to your spine, threatening to throw you off balance if you make a single false step. The fog wraps tightly around the orchard, muting every sound except the frantic beating of your own heart.

nodes.brief: Ducking under a low trellis strung with grey lichen, you spot a discarded Warden whistle lying in the mud, offering an instant passport if you dare blow it.

nodes.title: The Discarded Whistle
nodes.page:
Ducking under a low trellis strung with grey lichen, you spot a discarded Warden whistle lying in the mud, offering an instant passport if you dare blow it. The brass instrument gleams faintly through the fog, smudged with dried mud and greenish tarnish. Picking it up means you might mimic their signals, but a false note will bring every patrol in the orchard down upon your head. The bell-tongue presses cold against your jacket with an insistent pulse.

You can pocket the whistle and risk the signals, creep along the nursery beds, duck behind empty crates, or slide down the muddy bank into the gloom.

nodes.title: The Smuggler's Hatch
nodes.page:
You spot a forgotten smuggler's hatch under a root-knotted bank and slide inside with the clapper, taking an old cellar past the whole checkpoint. The air inside smells of dry straw, spilled mash, and centuries of mountain dampness. Because you believe the low forge has gone cold and you must look elsewhere for a way to recast the bell, this hidden route offers a vital reprieve from the watchful eyes of the Fog-Wardens. Stone steps descend into absolute darkness beneath your boots.

You hitch the cradle straps, eye the dark cellar tunnel ahead, then scan the earthen walls for old handholds and damp mortar that might take a knuckle.

nodes.title: The Drainage Pipe
nodes.page: You skirt the perimeter fence, rusted iron wire shivering in the updraft, and slip into a narrow drainage pipe that leads straight down toward the lower groves. The corrugated metal scrapes against the padded cradle of the bell-tongue with a harsh metallic whisper. Frigid air rushes upward through the cylinder, carrying the unmistakable scent of woodsmoke and damp earth from the valley floor. Your shoulders ache from hunching low to fit within the cramped iron tube.

nodes.title: The Blackthorn Labyrinth
nodes.page: Navigating a labyrinth of blackthorn hedges, you dodge a swinging lantern held by a searcher whose boots squelch heavily in the wet orchard clay. The orange light sweeps across the low-hanging branches just inches above your head, painting the fog in sickly amber hues. Thorns catch at your coat sleeves, threatening to tear the wool as you squeeze sideways through the narrow gaps. Against your spine the bronze clapper sounds a warning note and shivers with the cold mountain air.

Dust motes dance in the thin slivers of grey light piercing the cracked slat walls. Outside, the muffled shouts of the Wardens fade into the rhythmic drip of moisture and the distant hum of wind through the upper cables. The heavy bronze weight feels colder by the minute, drawing the heat straight out of your back.

The cold air tastes of rotting pulp and mountain water, sharp enough to make your lungs ache with every measured breath.

Distant cables stretch across the void, humming a taut chord that drowns out the sounds of the valley below.

You can skirt the old winch station, slip along the warden's box-hedge, or flash your forged token if the toll-collectors challenge your passage.

Fog-Wardens patrol these upper lines with practiced rhythm, their silver whistles cutting through the damp air like thin wire.

You wait for a break in the whistling before deciding where to make your next move beneath the sorting tables.

Somewhere nearby, a wood-fire crackles softly in a warden's hearth, offering a fleeting reminder of warmth.

You have a clear window to slip past the sorting tables, hug the high box-hedges, or deal with the Cable Court bailiffs if your debt catches up with you.

The water inside is black and still, reflecting nothing of the grey sky above. The bronze tongue rests cold against your spine, and the miles still remaining before Lowgate's forges press on your mind.

You can risk the toll-collectors, navigate the lead fountain pipes, or turn back up the mountain toward the upper ridges.

nodes.title: The Terraced Nursery
nodes.page: Creeping along the edge of a terraced nursery bed, you step lightly over coiled grafting twine that could easily trip you into the briars. The delicate saplings brush against your sleeves like skeletal fingers, and the damp soil clings to your boots with every cautious step. Down in the valley, unseen bells toll the hour in muffled, hollow notes that fade quickly into the mist.

nodes.title: The Apple Crates
nodes.page:
Ducking behind a towering stack of empty apple crates, you watch two Fog-Wardens pass by with muffled lanterns, discussing the morning frost. The wood smells of sweet decay and stored autumn harvests, thick and cloying in the damp air. Your shoulders ache from the cradle's weight, but the silence of the fog offers a safe cloak for your passage.

You can slip past the willow baskets, follow the boundary wall into the lower groves, or dodge into an alcove if the runaway barrel threatens your path.

nodes.brief: Sliding down a slick mud slide between two terraced plots, you use your free hand to brake against mossy roots while the heavy bell-tongue pulls.

nodes.title: The Mud Slide
nodes.page:
Sliding down a slick mud slide between two terraced plots, you use your free hand to brake against mossy roots while the heavy bell-tongue pulls. The wet earth smells of rich loam and crushed leaves, cold and slick beneath your palms. Below you, the orchard paths branch out into the fog, offering several routes toward the lower valley levels.

You can seek cover behind the willow baskets, follow the boundary wall, or take the drainage ditch toward the cobblestones.

nodes.brief: Threading your way through an ancient orchard where gnarled trunks look like twisted fingers, you follow the sound of a distant rushing flume.

nodes.title: The Rushing Flume
nodes.page:
Gnarled apple trunks twist into shapes like reaching fingers as you thread your path through the ancient orchard, guided by the steady, rushing sound of a distant water flume. The bronze tongue on your back knocks a low note against your spine, matching the pulse of the mountain current nearby.

A sudden clatter shatters the muffled stillness of the fog, and you spot danger barreling down the terrace.

nodes.brief: Spotting an old frostbite scar on your knuckles, you recall a veteran carter's trick of rubbing tallow on your boot-soles to move in absolute silence.

exits.label: Duck away from the bouncing timber barrel
Check the weathered milestone for the Lowgate distance
Turn back along the mossy irrigation run

nodes.title: Tallow and Frost
nodes.page: White frost clings to the old scar across your knuckles, a lasting reminder of the bitter glacier crossing that tested your endurance weeks ago. Remembering an old carter's trick, you pause to rub rendered tallow into your boot-soles, ensuring that every step you take through the silent fog remains completely soundless. The bronze clapper sits secure in its padded cradle, its faint metal knock dulled by damp orchard air.

nodes.brief: Navigating a narrow animal track beneath low-hanging branches, you press flat against the damp earth as a heavy cart rumbles along the terrace above.

Descend the moss-slick stone stairs toward the rumble

nodes.title: The Cart Above
nodes.page: Low-hanging branches scratch the canvas of the bell-cradle as you pick along the narrow twisting animal track through the fog. A farm cart rumbles along the paved terrace directly overhead, iron-rimmed wheels grinding on frozen gravel and shaking loose droplets of cold dew. You press yourself flat against the damp earth, waiting out the passage of the unseen vehicle before you dare to move forward.

nodes.brief: Slipping past a stone storage clamp filled with winter root vegetables, you hold your breath as a door creaks open in the thick white gloom.

Follow the steep stone stairway downward in the mist

nodes.title: The Storage Clamp
nodes.page: Root vegetables stored for the winter fill the stone clamp beside you with a sharp, earthy scent that cuts through the thick white gloom. You freeze in place as a heavy timber door creaks open just yards away, casting a pale sliver of lamplight across the wet grass. Holding your breath, you keep your hand steady against the padded frame of the bronze clapper until the footsteps fade back inside.

nodes.brief: Crossing a suspended wooden plank over a roaring drainage sluice, you feel the wet timber groan beneath the heavy bronze cradle on your back.

nodes.title: The Drainage Sluice
nodes.page: Wet timber groans beneath your boots as you cross a narrow wooden plank stretched over a roaring mountain drainage sluice. Icy water churns below and throws up a fine mist that mixes with the cloud blanketing the terraces. Every step requires absolute concentration as the heavy bronze cradle on your back shifts its weight against your shoulders.

nodes.brief: Weaving through a dense plantation of dwarf quinces, you keep low as a stray dog barks against the fog somewhere near the upper fence.

nodes.title: The Quince Plantation
nodes.page:
Weaving through a dense plantation of dwarf quinces, you keep low as a stray dog barks against the fog somewhere near the upper fence. The bronze Clapper shifts heavily in its padded cradle on your back, its cold metal pressing against your shoulder blades like a sleeping weight. Dew drips from the low branches, soaking through your woollen sleeves while the damp air tastes of bruised fruit and frozen loam.

Three distinct paths beckon through the mist-shrouded orchard rows, each leading deeper down the mountain toward the looming valley floor.

nodes.brief: Clinging to a mossy retaining wall while a Cable Court tax-collector hurries past with a ledger under his arm, you blend into the grey stone.

exits.label: Take the limestone steps downward
Slip past the silent warden gate

nodes.title: The Mossy Wall
nodes.page:
Clinging to a mossy retaining wall while a Cable Court tax-collector hurries past with a ledger under his arm, you blend into the grey stone. The official mutters curses about the damp ink ruining his tallies, his boots squelching loudly in the mud just inches from yours. Your arms ache from bracing Orison's tongue against the damp masonry, and the bronze seems to pass its cold through the wet rock into your spine.

The collector turns a corner into the grey gloom, leaving two narrow avenues open for your descent.

nodes.brief: Navigating a muddy terrace where fallen fruit rots in thick heaps, you keep your balance by clutching dangling branch-ends with frozen fingers.

exits.label: Head for the grand stone staircase
Seek the silent toll-gate in the mist

nodes.title: The Rotten Harvest
nodes.page:
Navigating a muddy terrace where fallen fruit rots in thick heaps, you keep your balance by clutching dangling branch-ends with frozen fingers. Bruised apples and frost-bitten quinces leave a sweet fermented stench in the stagnant air. Your stomach turns as you trudge through the grey soup. Every step needs absolute care, or the bronze tongue will throw you off balance and you will skid into the thorny brambles below.

Ahead lie two distinct ways out of the treacherous orchard maze.

nodes.brief: Squeezing past a rusted iron winch station, you listen to the rhythmic creak of distant cables stretching across the hidden gulf of the valley.

exits.label: Continue along the cliffside ledge

nodes.title: The Rusted Winch
nodes.page:
Squeezing past a rusted iron winch station, you listen to the rhythmic creak of distant cables stretching across the hidden gulf of the valley. The grease on the massive steel drum smells of old tallow and cold iron, sticking faintly to your knuckles as you steady yourself against the frame. Somewhere out in the dense fog, a cable-rider's whistle trills twice, answered immediately by a faint metallic clang from an unseen platform dangling over the abyss.

The pathway narrows past the winch house, offering a single viable route into the misty expanse.

nodes.brief: Crouching beneath a canvas fruit-sorting table, you wait out a group of gossiping orchard workers who complain bitterly about the early cold snap.

nodes.title: The Sorting Table
nodes.page:
Crouching beneath a canvas fruit-sorting table, you wait out a group of gossiping orchard workers who complain bitterly about the early cold snap. Their worn leather boots shuffle against the packed dirt just above your head while they discuss the failing barley harvest and the rising tolls charged by the Cable Court. You hold your breath, careful not to let the humming bronze tongue knock against the wooden slats of the table and betray your hiding place in the gloom.

The workers finally trudge away down a side path, leaving two ways open before you.

Inside its padded cradle the bronze clapper knocks cold against your shoulder blades, even with warmth drifting from the chimney. The mist clings thick to the stone pathway, muting your footsteps as you weigh the safest route further down the mountain.

Three distinct trails diverge ahead through the dripping orchards, each offering a different way past the silent sentinel posts of the valley.

nodes.title: The Bailiff's Mistake
nodes.page:
Recognizing a Cable Court bailiff who mistakes your brass cradle for a toll-box, you flash a forged token to stride past unchecked down the stone stairs. The collector narrows his eyes behind a fog-frosted visor, his hand hovering near his ledger strap, but the dull gleam of the counterfeit seal satisfies him enough to let you through with a gruff nod. You owe these toll-lords a bitter debt, making every second spent under their gaze a tense gamble with your precious cargo.

The path drops steeply into the gray gloom, leaving the checkpoint behind as the mountain air grows thin and sharp.

nodes.title: The Fountain Pipes
nodes.page:
Stepping carefully over a maze of lead pipes feeding the valley fountains, you make sure the mule avoids the slippery brass junction-boxes. Water leaks from a rusted joint, hissing softly as it hits the cold limestone and turning the path into a slick hazard for iron-shod hooves. Biscuit tests the footing with a cautious hoof, ears flicking back and forth to catch any sign of pursuit through the thick gray fog.

Ahead, the trail splits toward the lower terraces and the growing warmth of the river gorge.

nodes.title: The Wicker Stack

Hiding behind a towering stack of willow wicker baskets, you let a patrol of whistle-guards march by before breaking into a steady trot southward. Their signal whistles trill softly in the damp air, a three-note code that fades away as the wardens vanish into the white shroud of the orchards. The bronze clapper stirs in its leather straps, a low melancholy knock that matches your breathing.

The path ahead opens into a clear lane free of watchers.

nodes.title: The Boundary Wall
nodes.page:
Trailing your hand along a damp stone wall that marks the boundary of the lower groves, you sense the air growing warmer and less choked with mist. The persistent dampness of Orisonhold begins to yield to the dry, coal-scented updrafts rising from the foundry town far below. Every stone here is slick with centuries of mountain runoff and autumn leaves, demanding absolute concentration with every step you take.

Three separate ways beckon through the thinning vapor as the descent continues.

nodes.brief: Wading through a shallow drainage ditch filled with fallen leaves, you emerge onto a wider cobblestone track leading down toward the deep gorge.

Descend the zig-zag trail to Lowgate

nodes.title: The Drainage Ditch
nodes.page:
Wading through a shallow drainage ditch filled with fallen leaves, you emerge onto a wider cobblestone track leading down toward the deep gorge. The water runs clear and cold around your boots, washing away the stubborn mountain mud that has clung to your soles since the upper gate. Biscuit shakes his shaggy head, spraying droplets into the misty air as he finds firmer ground on the paved road.

The lower valley opens its gray arms before you, offering several distinct paths toward the safety of the forge-masters.

nodes.brief: Dodging a runaway cider barrel that bounces off a terrace wall, you pull the mule into a shallow alcove just in time to avoid disaster.

nodes.title: The Runaway Barrel
nodes.page:
Dodging a runaway cider barrel that bounces off a terrace wall, you pull the mule into a shallow alcove just in time to avoid disaster. The heavy oak cask shatters against a stone marker with a thunderous crack, spilling sweet fermented pulp across the flagstones just inches from Biscuit's trailing hooves. Shouts echo from an upper orchard as unseen workers argue over the clumsy mishap, reminding you that danger comes in many forms here.

You can cross the bridge toward the safety of the smoke, or make a desperate leap across the irrigation flume to outrun the commotion.

nodes.brief: Pausing beside a milestone carved with lichen-filled runes, you verify that the path to Lowgate is finally clear of the upper warden patrols.

nodes.title: The Lichen Milestone
nodes.page:
Pausing beside a milestone carved with lichen-filled runes, you verify that the path to Lowgate is finally clear of the upper warden patrols. The ancient stone bears the chisel marks of forgotten guilds, measuring the distance in bell-beats rather than miles down the sheer cliff face. The mule exhales a long, warm sigh, lowering its muzzle to nibble at a hardy tuft of moss growing beside the plinth.

The route ahead splits into a pair of clear tracks winding through the lower fruit groves.

nodes.brief: Slipping through an unlocked orchard gate that swings silently on oiled leather hinges, you leave the misty veil of the upper valley behind.

exits.label: Cross the torrent toward the coal-smoke

nodes.title: The Leather Hinges
nodes.page:
Slipping through an unlocked orchard gate that swings silently on oiled leather hinges, you leave the misty veil of the upper valley behind. The thick canopy of pear and apple trees gives way to open scrubland where the mountain wind sweeps clean and cold across the rocks. The bronze clapper sits a touch easier against your back now that the steepest cliffs are behind you.

Two descending tracks offer passage toward the rumbling iron foundries of the gorge.

nodes.brief: Descending a steep stone stairway slick with winter moss, you hear the distant, reassuring rumble of the iron foundries echoing up from the river.

exits.label: Take the final zig-zag trail down

nodes.title: The Iron Rumble
nodes.page:
Descending a steep stone stairway slick with winter moss, you hear the distant, reassuring rumble of the iron foundries echoing up from the river. The harsh scent of sulfur and coke replaces the sweet rot of fallen orchard fruit, signaling that the end of your arduous journey is finally within reach. Every muscle in your back aches from the dead weight of the Orison's tongue, but the rhythmic hum of the bronze keeps fatigue at bay.

A single steep track remains between you and the roaring heart of Lowgate.

nodes.brief: Emerging from the dripping fruit-groves onto the great limestone staircase, you adjust the padded cradle as the cloud ceiling lifts above your head.

exits.label: Take the lower smithy path

nodes.title: The Limestone Descent
nodes.page: Damp fruit-groves give way beneath your boots to the great limestone staircase, sweeping downward in broad, weather-worn tiers. As the cloud ceiling lifts to show jagged peaks far above, you shift the padded cradle and feel the bronze tongue cool against your spine. Moisture drips from mossy stone balustrades, catching the pale afternoon light while Biscuit follows closely behind on clacking hooves. Ahead, the path bifurcates toward the bustling smithies and the main gates of the lower tier.

nodes.brief: Pausing at a stone toll-arch where the warden bells hang silent, you wipe the cold condensation from your brow and check the mule's girth-straps.

exits.label: Follow the lane toward the gates

Enter the roaring foundry warmth

nodes.title: The Silent Toll-Arch
nodes.page: Cold condensation beads on your forehead as you pause beneath a vaulted stone toll-arch where the warden bells hang completely silent in the mist. You reach back to check the mule's girth-straps, ensuring the pack remains secure before pressing onward down the winding lane. The air smells sharply of damp earth and distant woodsmoke drifting up from the valley floor.

nodes.brief: Looking back up the sheer mountain face where Orisonhold dissolves into white mist, you feel the first clear breeze of the lower gorge strike your cheeks.

exits.label: Watch the scarred smith inspect the bronze

nodes.title: The Lower Gorge Breeze
nodes.page: White mist swirls behind you as you look back up the sheer mountain face where Orisonhold dissolves into impenetrable cloud. The first clear, crisp breeze of the lower gorge strikes your cheeks, carrying the unmistakable scent of coal-smoke and rushing river water. Every step downward eases the pull on your shoulders, even as the bronze core of the Great Bell keeps pulsing in its cradle.

nodes.brief: Walking briskly down the broad paved descent toward Lowgate, you hear the muffled clank of the great foundry hammers drawing you toward the end of your quest.

exits.label: Ring the heavy brass hand-pull

Present the relic to the master founder

nodes.title: The Broad Paved Descent
nodes.page: Broad paved stones guide your rapid descent toward Lowgate, and muffled foundry hammers clank through the valley haze. The sound acts as a steady pulse, drawing you ever closer to the final destination of your grueling quest. Biscuit quickens his pace beside you, sensing the journey's end in the thickening air and the warmth radiating from the forge-master's yards.

nodes.brief: Reaching the final stone terrace above the river-fog, you pat the mule's dusty neck as the silhouette of the lower smithies looms through the haze.

exits.label: Watch the scarred smith inspect the bronze
Present the relic to the master founder

nodes.title: The River-Fog Terrace
nodes.page: Dust settles on the mule's grey neck as you reach the final stone terrace overlooking the dense, rolling river-fog below. The dark silhouette of the lower smithies looms ominously through the haze, outlined by the fiery orange glow of furnace doors swinging open in the distance. You rest a hand on the beast's dusty flank, steadying your breathing against the sharp chill of the mountain air.

nodes.brief: Striding past a row of shuttered drying-sheds, you feel the weight of the cracked bronze clapper lighten in your spirit as the descent nears its end.

exits.label: Ring the heavy brass hand-pull
Present the relic to the master founder

nodes.title: The Shuttered Drying-Sheds
nodes.page: Shuttered drying-sheds line the narrow lane, their wooden slats grey and warped from decades of mountain moisture. Your spirit lightens despite the physical exhaustion, knowing the cracked bronze clapper is finally nearing the hearths designed to mend its voice. Biscuit snorts softly into the damp air, kicking up a loose pebble that clatters against the stone wall.

nodes.brief: Crossing the old arch bridge over the white-water torrent, you smell coal-smoke and hot iron rising from the forge-master's yard below.

exits.label: Step inside the roaring foundry

nodes.title: The Arch Bridge Torrent
nodes.page: White-water churns beneath the old arch bridge and throws fine spray into the crisp air as you cross to the northern bank. Coal-smoke and the sharp tang of hot iron rise from the forge-master's yard spread out below after days of freezing isolation. The strap across your chest digs in once more as you turn toward the roaring furnaces.

nodes.brief: Standing at the head of the final zig-zag trail down to Lowgate, you take a deep breath of the clear lowland air and prepare to deliver the Orison's tongue.

exits.label: Step inside the roaring foundry

nodes.title: The Final Zig-Zag Trail
nodes.page: Clear lowland air fills your lungs as you stand at the head of the final zig-zag trail winding down into the bustling heart of Lowgate. Orison's tongue knocks soft against your back in time with the massive hammers beating below. You adjust your grip on the carrying straps and prepare to step out of the mountain shadows once and for all.

nodes.brief: Reaching the iron-studded gates of the foundry yard, you ring the heavy brass hand-pull and wait for the forge-masters to answer your desperate summons.

exits.label: Press on

nodes.title: The Iron-Studded Gates
nodes.page: Iron-studded gates rise before you at the boundary of the vast foundry yard, where coal-smoke billows into the grey sky. You grasp the brass hand-pull and let it drop. A resounding metallic clang answers off the stone walls. Inside, the muffled shouts of workmen and the steady roar of bellows signal that your summons has been heard.

nodes.brief: Dropping the padded cradle onto the threshold of the casting hall, you watch a scarred smith come forward to inspect the fractured bronze tongue.

exits.label: Press on

nodes.title: The Casting Hall Threshold
nodes.page: Stone flags rise to meet your boots as you drop the padded cradle onto the threshold of the cavernous casting hall. A tall, scarred smith steps forward from the blinding glare of the central furnace, wiping soot from his brow with a leather rag. He looks down with narrowed eyes at the fractured bronze tongue resting quietly in its harness.

nodes.brief: Unbuckling the heavy straps from your aching shoulders, you present the humming relic to the master founder just as the first heavy snowflakes begin to fall.

exits.label: Step back into the mountain chill

nodes.title: The Master Founder's Judgment
nodes.page:
You unbuckle the straps from your aching shoulders and hand the relic to the master founder just as the first snowflakes begin to fall. The old smith runs calloused fingers down the scored bronze, testing the weight of the tongue that once woke Orisonhold through mountain blizzards. Around you, apprentices stoke the coke-beds until the cavernous arch glows like a captured sunset.

There is no time to linger by the hearth, for the low pass threatens to seal entirely before dawn breaks.

nodes.brief: Stepping inside the roaring warmth of the lower foundry, you slide the great clapper onto the iron cooling floor and know that Orisonhold's voice is saved.

exits.label: Descend further into the river basin
Turn back toward the mist-shrouded orchards

nodes.title: Refuge in the Lower Foundry
nodes.page:
Stepping inside the roaring warmth of the lower foundry, you slide the great clapper onto the iron cooling floor and know that Orisonhold's voice is saved from the frost. Sparks spit against the soot-blackened rafters while furnace-men cheer your arrival and pound iron hammers in time with the faint lingering knock of the bronze. Every muscle in your back aches from the long descent through the mist, yet relief washes over you like warm spring water.

Beyond the tall double doors, however, the valley path remains open and beckons you further down the slope.

nodes.brief: Ignoring all the Warden whistle-codes, you bolt headlong through a blind orchard gap in the thickest fog, plunging straight down an unflagged cliff drainage chute and shattering the bronze Clapper against the limestone floor below.
nodes.title: The Blind Leap
nodes.page: Ignoring all the Warden whistle-codes, you bolt headlong through a blind orchard gap in the thickest fog, plunging straight down an unflagged cliff drainage chute. The loose gravel gives way instantly beneath your boots, sending you sliding into a wall of wet limestone. The heavy bronze Clapper breaks free from its rotting straps, shattering against the bedrock below with a dull, mournful shriek that echoes endlessly down the silent mountain.

nodes.brief: Trying to outrun a mounted warden patrol by leaping across a rotting irrigation flume, you slip on the wet green slime and plunge headfirst into the thorns, shattering the bronze cradle against the stones.
nodes.title: The Final Leap
nodes.page: Trying to outrun a mounted warden patrol by leaping across a rotting irrigation flume, you slip on the wet green slime and plunge headfirst into the thorns, shattering the bronze cradle against the stones. The clapper rolls free into the muddy ditch, its ancient voice lost under dripping leaves while the patrol's lanterns close in through the gray fog.

nodes.title: Arrival in Lowgate
nodes.page: Arrival in Lowgate and the Foundry brings the bustling, soot-stained life of the river-port straight into your face, complete with flooded streets, desperate forge-masters hunting for scarce tin, and old promises coming due in the shadow of roaring blast furnaces. The air tastes of sulphur and wet river silt, thick with the shouts of bargemen and the clatter of iron on stone. Every alleyway offers a different route through the maze of workshops and docks toward your final destination.

nodes.title: The Foundry Quarter
nodes.page: Blackened gables lean precariously over the narrow, soot-stained lanes of the lower foundry quarter, where the constant drip of mountain runoff mixes with the industrial residue of centuries of metalwork. The air tastes of copper and wet coal-dust; distant machinery rumbles and weary laborers shout while they haul slag to the riverbank. You stand at a critical crossroads in the heart of the district, where every previous assumption about the warmth of the welcome or the emptiness of the bins must finally face the test of reality.

nodes.title: The Furnace Door
nodes.page: Before you the iron furnace door stands like a wall of solid night, scored by generations of soot, oil, and arcane seals. Within its depths, the great furnace roars with a hunger that threatens to consume any traveler who approaches without the proper rites or tools. The air tastes of sulfur, hot scale, and the ancient promise of Orisonhold.

nodes.title: The Foundry Floor
nodes.page: Smoke hangs low beneath the blackened rafters of the Lowgate foundry, where the great brick furnace shakes the river-pavement with a deep, hungry vibration. The bronze clapper sits in its wooden cradle at your feet, and its faint familiar note cuts through the roar of the coal-fires and the shouting of the weary iron-workers. Every promise made on the stairs, every knot tied by the ropewrights, and every debt owed to the valley lords now converges on this open iron door.

nodes.title: Silt and Scraps
nodes.page:
By the silt-choked river quay, Master Vane hawks rusted scrap iron while the gray flood laps at his boots and threatens to swallow his makeshift stall. He eyes your travel-worn gear with professional suspicion, muttering about the cost of copper and the scarcity of fuel in the lower wards. The damp wind carries the stench of rotting reeds and stagnant bilge water from the moored barges.

Other travelers crowd the slippery stone quay, seeking answers or passage away from the rising tide.

nodes.title: Drips and Warnings
nodes.page:
Under the dripping eaves of the copper-smiths' alley, an old woman named Marrow sells salted eel and warnings about the rising tide to anyone willing to spare a copper coin. Freezing ropes of rainwater pour from the slate roofs, pool around her wooden crate, and soak the hems of passing laborers. The narrow passage echoes with the rhythmic clink of tiny hammers shaping kettles in the gloom.

Beyond her stall, the alley splits into darker, more treacherous lanes.

nodes.title: Locks and Barges
nodes.page:
At the sluice-gate lockhouse, a weary lock-keeper named Hobb argues with barge-haulers about tolls on the muddy current while iron chains groan under the strain of rising water. Timbers shudder as the gray river presses the wooden gates and climbs toward the lip of the stone embankments. The smell of wet hemp and horse sweat hangs thick in the damp air.

Several paths branch off from the noisy lockhouse into the misty labyrinth of the port.

nodes.title: Hemp and Gossip
nodes.page:
Near the sunken timber wharf, young apprentices trade gossip about the foundry's dwindling tin stores while hauling drenched hemp coils through the ankle-deep mire. Their laughter cuts through the monotonous roar of the weir upstream, sharp and irreverent against the gray backdrop of the industrial quarter. Heavy cargo crates are stacked haphazardly along the rotting boardwalks, leaking sawdust and grease into the puddles.

The path ahead winds deeper into the soot and steam of the workshops.

nodes.page: Past the salt-crusted crane-posts, a rope-seller named Gault curses the damp air that rots his finest hemp cables before they ever reach the mountain winches. Spools of heavy tarred cordage line the muddy track like giant sleeping serpents, glistening with moisture under the sunless sky. The distant clang of the main foundry hammer reverberates through the damp ground beneath your boots.

nodes.title: The Granary Clerk
nodes.page: Within the shadowed arch of the lower granary, a clerk named Orin weighs soggy grain bags against unpaid municipal debts, his inkhorn swinging from a greasy belt. He mutters over ledgers swollen by mountain damp while you shift the heavy bronze Clapper in its padded cradle on your back. The air here tastes of wet chaff and old ledger-glue, thick with the weight of Lowgate's ledger-books. Orin glances up from his figures, eyeing the bronze tongue that hums faintly against your shoulder blades, wondering aloud if church metal can settle the district's arrears.

nodes.title: The Cautious Ferryman
nodes.page: Because the white scar across your knuckles proves your crossing over the high glacier, a cautious ferryman grants you immediate passage across the churning lock without demanding the usual copper toll. He steadies the wet gunwale of his flat-bottomed boat with a scarred hand while the grey river boils around the wooden pilings. Against your spine the Clapper answers the freeze of the current beneath the hull with a small bronze knock. You step aboard and balance the cradle while the ferryman pushes off from the muddy bank toward the opposite wharf.

Steam rises in greasy curls into the chill air, smelling of scorched fat and woodsmoke, clinging to your woollen cloak and the padded cradle of the Clapper. Biscuit shifts his weight on the cobblestones nearby, shaking a frosty ear as the mule recognizes the familiar stench of the tanning district. Bran pauses in his scraping, wiping his greasy forearm across his brow while he stares at the heavy bronze tongue on your back.

Silver scales cling to her leather apron and the wet stones around her wooden stool, gleaming dully in the gray river light. Against your spine the massive bronze Clapper sounds a long note and startles a flock of gulls from the nearby rotting pilings. Sula looks up from her torn nets, squinting at the heavy cradle on your back and the stubborn mule standing patient at your side.

nodes.title: The Weary Drover
nodes.page: Beneath the creaking iron sign of the Drowned Ox tavern, a weary drover named Thrum tries to quiet his shivering packhorses while sleet begins to stick to their lathered flanks. Wet horsehair, cheap ale, and rotting straw spill their scent from the tavern stable doors. Biscuit stamps a hoof in greeting against the frozen mud, his breath pluming white in the freezing river air. Thrum pulls his sheepskin collar tighter around his throat, casting a sidelong glance at the heavy bronze tongue vibrating within your padded cradle.

nodes.title: The Lower Mill

The great wheel groans under the pressure of the mountain runoff, sending vibrations up through the stone foundation and into your boots. You hitch the Clapper on your back until its knock falls in step with the millworks' shudder. Corin pauses, leaning on his wooden shovel to wipe his wet face, watching you balance against the rising damp.

nodes.title: The Toll-Office

The room smells of stale ink, wet wool, and charcoal smoke venting poorly from a rusted stovepipe. The bronze Clapper taps soft against your shoulder and rattles the stack of unpaid tolls on the clerk's desk. Jora does not look up from her ink-stained papers, her hand hovering over the next manifest while she waits for your business.

nodes.title: The Charcoal Sheds
nodes.page: Near the soot-blackened charcoal sheds, a charcoal-burner named Kael loads damp sacks onto a creaking handcart, black dust smearing across his forehead and canvas tunic. Coal-dust and shattered willow twigs litter the ground and crunch under your boots as you carry the Clapper. Burnt oak smells sharp in the damp air and sticks to the wool of your cloak and the padding of the bronze cradle. Kael heaves a sack onto the cart and eyes the massive metal tongue on your back with professional curiosity.

nodes.title: The Canal Wall
nodes.page: Along the weed-choked canal wall, a mudlark named Tish washes river silt from a pocketful of copper buttons in the freezing current, her fingers blue and stiff. Bubbles rise from the dark water where old pilings rot beneath the surface, releasing a sharp smell of stagnant mud. The bronze Clapper rings a deep note that sets the floating debris in the canal trembling against the stonework. Tish drops her salvaged buttons into a leather pouch, looking up at you with wide eyes as you balance the heavy cradle.

nodes.title: The Cooperage
nodes.page: Within the dripping archway of the cooperage, a cooper named Bran hammers iron hoops onto swollen oak staves, each blow echoing sharply off the wet brick walls. The sharp scent of fresh-cut oak shavings and hot iron mixes with the cold river mist drifting in from the wharf. The Clapper on your back knocks in counterpoint to the cooper's mallet, and a faint vibration runs through the metal hoops stacked around the floor. Bran strikes another blow, pausing to wipe sweat from his neck while he glances at your heavy burden.

nodes.title: The Leaking Wharf
nodes.page: Under the leaking canvas of the vegetable wharf, a merchant named Hestia inspects bruised cabbages ruined by the flood, her fingers stained green with vegetable rot. As the icy river breeze sweeps through the rotting crates, the bronze Clapper on your back taps a damp note against your spine. Hestia mutters bitterly over a ruined crate of winter roots, tossing a water-logged head aside into the murky shallows where greasy foam bobs against the pilings. You shift the padded cradle, balancing the weight of the bell's tongue before the cold damp settles deeper into your joints.

The intense heat offers a brief mercy against the mountain chill, warming the wet leather straps of the Clapper cradle resting between your shoulder blades. Dael shoves another splintered crate into the roaring mouth of the clay oven, sparks spitting sharply onto the soot-stained cobbles. Across the lane, shadows lengthen over the dark doorways of the guildhouse, where impatient voices rise above the hiss of steam.

nodes.title: The Chain-Locker

The iron links rattle dully whenever the swollen river heaves against the wooden piers below. Fenn looks up from his slate, marks the padded bundle on your back with a clerk's eye, then returns to his dismal count. Further along the embankment, shadowy passages lead toward the grain hoist and the wet stone steps of the lower basin.

The sturdy animal picks its way with sure-footed cunning through the gloom, its ears flicking back at every sudden splash of river water. The Clapper knocks against your back in time with the beast's slow breathing as you pick through forgotten corners of the lower port. Ahead, narrow alleys branch off into the shadows of the old quarter, offering paths away from the watchful eyes of the toll-lords.

nodes.title: The Wool-Combers' Loft
nodes.page: Beneath the sagging eaves of the wool-combers' loft, an artisan named Nyx washes fleece in greasy river water, her arms red and raw from the biting cold. The soapy stench of lanolin mixes heavily with the damp odor of rotting weed drifting up from the swollen canal. Nyx wrings a soaked fleece with a sharp twist and dirty water splashes across the wooden trough. Downstream, the embankment stretches toward the net-weaver's hut and the smoking hearths of the charcoal-burners hidden in the lower ward.

nodes.title: The Candle-Dippers' Alley
nodes.page: Along the narrow alley behind the candle-dippers, an apprentice named Jory spills hot tallow onto the cobblestones, watching the pale wax harden instantly in the freezing air. Sweet rendered mutton fat smells strong between the damp brick walls, masking the sharper stench of the flooded drains. Jory scrapes at the cooling spill with a chipped slate blade, muttering curses under his breath as the wind whistles through the passage. The lane leads onward toward the smoking hearth of the charcoal workers and the towering timber rafters of the grain hoist.

nodes.title: The Timber Crane
nodes.page: Near the weed-hung crane on the timber pier, a sawyer named Loran stacks waterlogged pine planks, his muscles straining against the dead weight of the sodden timber. The river laps hungrily against the rotting pilings below, threatening to tear the remaining docks from their rusted iron anchorages. Loran pauses to wipe sweat from his brow with a brine-stiffened sleeve, staring across the grey expanse of the lower basin. Behind you, the silt-choked quay offers a clear path back toward the upper terraces where the mountain climb begins.

nodes.title: The Lower Bridge
nodes.page: Beside the crumbling stone buttress of the lower bridge, a mason named Krell chisels dry mortar into a wet crack, his mallet striking the stone with dull, rhythmic thuds. The freezing spray from the swollen river mists his thick beard, turning the droplets into tiny points of ice. Krell tests the stubborn masonry with a gloved thumb before dipping his trowel back into the bucket of gritty lime. Beyond the bridge, narrow paths wind toward a quiet stone shrine and the creaking timber cranes of the yard.

nodes.title: The Sail-Loft
nodes.page: Within the shadowy recess of the sail-loft, a seamstress named Thalia patches storm-torn canvas, her bone needle pulling stout waxed thread through stiffened folds. The vast sheets of grey cloth rustle like dry leaves in the drafty upper room, smelling of salt and fish-oil. Thalia works by the pale light of a narrow window overlooking the flooded quays, her hands moving with swift, practiced grace. Below, the coal-quay and the tanneries wait in the freezing drizzle, their lanes choked with the debris of the storm.

nodes.title: The Foundry Quarter
nodes.page: Within the flooded foundry quarter, the river laps against the blackened stone foundations of the Great Forge while forge-masters argue bitterly over dwindling supplies of tin. The air smells intensely of sulfur, wet coal-dust, and the sharp, metallic tang of molten metal cooling in iron trays. Every old promise made to the mountain city now comes due in the flickering glow of the central furnace, where the fate of the cracked bell hangs in the balance. Outside in the freezing drizzle, workers scurry between the timber yards and the smoldering smiths' alley.

nodes.title: The Salt Warehouse
nodes.page:
Behind the rusted iron gates of the salt warehouse, a guard named Bron inspects leaking sacks of gray crystals, his fingers caked with brine as he scrapes white crust from the damp floorboards. The damp air smells of ancient seas and sharp minerals that catch in your nose, and Biscuit shifts restlessly against the bronze Clapper strapped to your spine. You watch the crystals trickle through a torn seam, wondering how much weight a single split sack can lose before the tally-man notices.

Bron looks up from his messy ledger, his eyes squinting against the pale harbor light filtering through the high, barred windows. You hitch the padded cradle on your shoulders and feel the familiar faint knock of metal resting against your back. You can slip past the loading bay into the smoky alleyways or wait here until the inspection finishes.

nodes.title: The Tinker's Shack
nodes.page:
Near the smoking chimney of the tinker's shack, a mender named Garreth hammers dents out of battered copper kettles, sending sharp ringing echoes across the muddy lane. Sparks fly from the small charcoal stove, catching briefly in the cold drizzle before dying in the puddles at your feet. Biscuit lowers his head to sniff a heap of scrap metal while you hitch the bronze Clapper in its padded cradle. Garreth pauses his rhythmic pounding to wipe soot from his forehead with a greasy rag, eyeing the massive tongue of Orisonhold with professional curiosity.

The metallic clamor fades into a damp quiet as the mender turns back to a split kettle seam. You weigh your options in the chill air, knowing the foundry is close but uncertain whether to seek out the masters now or circle the lower lanes first.

nodes.title: The Boat-Builder's Shed
nodes.page:
Under the dripping thatch of the boat-builder's shed, a shipwright named Hesketh caulks seams with boiling pitch, filling the humid air with the pungent smell of pine tar and smoke. Ribs of half-built river skiffs arch overhead like the skeletal remains of mountain beasts, keeping the worst of the cold drizzle away from your shoulders. Biscuit snorts at the acrid fumes, shaking water from his shaggy ears while you ease the heavy burden of the Clapper against a sturdy timber post. Hesketh dips his iron ladle into the bubbling pot, never taking his shrewd eyes off the massive bronze tongue strapped to your back.

The thick black pitch cools rapidly in the drafty shed, hardening into glossy ribbons along the hull timbers. You consider lingering by the warm fire pit or pressing onward through the winding alleys of the lower quarters.

nodes.title: The Water-Gate Steps
nodes.page:
Beside the flooded steps of the water-gate, a watchman named Dorn blows a cold breath over his frosted brass horn, creating a low, hollow note that blends with the wash of river tides. Green algae coats the lower masonry where the high water laps persistently against the stone, smelling of silt and old iron. You and Biscuit stand balanced on the slippery ledge while the Clapper's familiar knock travels through your tired spine. Dorn lowers his horn and taps the bell against his palm, eyeing the gray waters and the various paths winding away from the basin.

The tide continues its slow, relentless climb up the mossy steps, threatening to submerge the lower landing entirely before dusk.

nodes.title: The Rag-Picker's Cellar
nodes.page:
Within the murky gloom of the rag-picker's cellar, an old woman named Martha sorts damp woolens by moonlight, her gnarled fingers deftly separating coarse mountain fleece from lowland cotton. Dust motes dance in the pale shaft of light cutting through the low cellar window, illuminating heaps of discarded textiles that muffle the sounds of the damp street above. You step carefully down the broken stone stairs, and the bronze Clapper bumps the low wooden lintel with a dull muffled thud. Martha murmurs a low greeting without lifting her head, her fingers still moving swiftly among the woolen rags.

The stale air is heavy with the scent of dried lavender and wet wool, offering a brief shelter from the biting harbor wind outside. You can press deeper into the working yards toward the iron-roofed casting shed, walk over to the roaring grand furnace, or inspect the quiet mixing floor.

nodes.brief: Along the slippery stone embankment of the lower basin, a net-weaver named Nuala mends torn hemp meshes.

exits.label: Head towards the bell-founders' guild
Check the iron-roofed casting shed
Inspect the grand furnace pit

nodes.title: The Lower Embankment
nodes.page:
Along the slippery stone embankment of the lower basin, a net-weaver named Nuala mends torn hemp meshes, her wooden shuttle flying through the gray cords with practiced speed. The cold river water laps against the mossy foundations below, carrying floating bits of marsh grass and wood chips from the upper forests. Biscuit picks his footing along the wet granite blocks while you hitch the straps that hold the Clapper to your aching back. Nuala ties a final knot and bites through the cord, watching the mist curl off the dark surface of the river.

The gray light begins to fade over the water, casting long shadows across the crowded boat docks and alleys. You weigh the fading daylight against the distance remaining to the foundry guild, the iron-roofed casting shed, or the grand furnace pit.

nodes.brief: Because you owe nobody a copper, you stride past the snarling debt-collectors outside the guildhouse with an easy conscience.

exits.label: Approach the deep grand furnace pit
Visit the weigh-master by the mixing floor

priv.why: the reader owes nobody and can bargain freely

nodes.title: The Clear Ledger
nodes.page:
Because you owe nobody a copper, you stride past the snarling debt-collectors outside the guildhouse with an easy conscience, your pockets light and your steps unhindered by promissory knots. Yellow teeth show as the lenders finger their account books, yet the ledgers hold no claim against your name or the sacred bronze you carry. Biscuit trots briskly behind you on the cobblestones, sensing the absence of pursuit and lifting his head into the crisp mountain air. You feel a rare sense of freedom in the crowded streets of Lowgate, where every other traveler is bound by tangled debts and unfulfilled oaths.

The great stone doors of the foundry stand open ahead, spilling a dull red glow and the smell of sulfur into the darkening square. You can walk straight to the deep pit of the grand furnace where the old casters work, or step toward the weigh-master's station by the mixing floor.

nodes.brief: Near the smoking hearth of the charcoal-burners' shelter, a worker named Joram roasts dry chestnuts over embers.

exits.label: Walk towards the weigh-master's scales
Follow the corridor to the clerk's office

nodes.title: The Charcoal Shelter
nodes.page:
Near the smoking hearth of the charcoal-burners' shelter, a worker named Joram roasts dry chestnuts over embers, the rich nutty smell cutting sharply through the sulfurous mountain air. Blue smoke curls lazily from the makeshift brick hearth, warming your frozen fingers as you pause to let Biscuit catch his breath. Joram holds out a warm chestnut on a blackened thumb and nods toward the padded cradle and the metal inside. Dry hardwood crackles under the pot, a warm backdrop to the distant noise of the lower foundry yards.

The glowing embers cast dancing red patterns across the soot-stained timber walls of the shelter.

nodes.brief: Beneath the leaning timber rafters of the grain hoist, a clerk named Orla counts moldy sacks of barley.

exits.label: Head towards the grand furnace pit
Walk down the soot-stained corridor

nodes.title: The Grain Hoist
nodes.page:
Beneath the leaning timber rafters of the grain hoist, a clerk named Orla counts moldy sacks of barley, her quill scratching frantically against a water-stained parchment. Dust hangs thick in the dim air, smelling of stale grain and river dampness, while outside the wind rattles the creaking wooden pulleys of the lift. You and Biscuit keep to the shadows while the bronze Clapper on your back knocks a slow note that sets the loose grain sacks shivering. Orla dips her quill into a horn inkwell and glares at a particularly soggy sack with deep irritation.

The creaking of the overhead machinery rises and falls with every gust of wind sweeping down from the mountain pass. You can leave the dusty hoist behind to visit the grand furnace pit or walk down the soot-stained corridor toward the municipal office.

nodes.brief: Beside the rusted iron winch of the coal-quay, a laborer named Skiff greases dry gears with mutton grease.

exits.label: Follow the corridor to the municipal office
Walk towards the lower foundry ventilation shaft
Turn back up the mountain path

nodes.title: The Coal-Quay Winch
nodes.page:
Beside the rusted iron winch of the coal-quay, a laborer named Skiff greases dry gears with mutton grease, the thick yellow fat slicking his calloused hands. As the crank turns, the iron drum groans and hauls another basket of wet slack up from the barge moored in the murky water below. Biscuit shakes dirty water from his hide and nearly tips a barrel of spare winch pins while you catch the bronze Clapper on your back. Skiff wipes his greasy palms on his canvas trousers and spits into the river, eyeing your mountain gear with silent appraisal.

The cold wind off the water carries the sharp taste of coal dust and salt deep into your lungs. You can follow the soot-stained corridor to the municipal office, head toward the smoking ventilation shaft of the lower foundry, or retrace your steps back up the mountain path.

nodes.brief: Within the damp stone alcove of the shrine, a pilgrim named Perrin leaves a dried mountain iris for safe travel.

exits.label: Step past the pilgrim toward the lower courtyard
Follow the narrow brick path down toward the ventilation shaft
Take the slippery stone steps toward the drainage trench

nodes.title: The Shrine Alcove
nodes.page: Damp stones weep moisture against your shoulder inside the candle-lit alcove where a pilgrim named Perrin presses a dried mountain iris into a crack in the masonry for safe travel. The delicate purple petals smell of high altitude and old snow, contrasting sharply with the thick smell of coal-smoke drifting up from the lower foundries. Biscuit shakes his harness bells outside, the light bronze clatter echoing against the wet slate. You adjust the heavy padded cradle holding the great Clapper on your back, feeling its faint, steady hum vibrate through your spine like a distant heartbeat.

nodes.brief: Along the muddy lane behind the tanneries, a hide-salter named Cadan scrapes salt from stiff ox pelts.

exits.label: Pick your way past the pelts toward the smoke-vent
Turn down the alleyway toward the flooded trench

nodes.title: The Tannery Lane
nodes.page: Along the muddy lane behind the tanneries, thick yellow salt cakes the stiff ox hides, and a hide-salter named Cadan scrapes brine crusts with a dull iron blade. Tanning liquor and wet leather leave a pungent tang, and the cold mountain wind tastes thick and salt-laden. Your boots sink deep into the slush as Biscuit tests the footing with a cautious hoof, his ears flicking at the rhythmic scraping sound. You shift the burden of the Clapper on your back, keeping the canvas dry against the swirling mist.

nodes.brief: Near the creaking wooden crane of the timber-yard, a loader named Tavis stacks soggy pine logs.

exits.label: Walk across the timber yard toward the lower courtyard
Head down the lane toward the smoking ventilation shaft

nodes.title: The Timber-Yard Crane
nodes.page: Creaking timbers groan overhead as a loader named Tavis heaves soggy pine logs into a towering stack beside the timber-yard crane. Water streams from the bark, pooling in the black mud around your boots while the heavy iron chain of the winch swings slowly in the damp draft. Biscuit lowers his head against the moisture, blowing a wet breath through his nostrils that mists in the chill air. The metal tongue in your back cradle knocks a low persistent note that seems to answer the river far below.

nodes.brief: Beside the blackened stones of the smiths' alley, an apprentice named Bram fans a dying charcoal brazier.

exits.label: Leave the flickering brazier for the courtyard ahead
Follow the alley toward the pumping station

nodes.title: The Smiths' Alley
nodes.page: Blackened stones radiate a meager, damp warmth inside the narrow alley where an apprentice named Bram frantically fans a dying charcoal brazier with a cracked leather paddle. Orange sparks rise sluggishly into the fog before dying out against the wet brick walls. Biscuit stamps on the cobblestones and rattles his pack-frames while you catch the cradle that holds the Clapper. The sharp smell of sulfur and wet coke clings to your wool coat, chilling you to the bone despite the proximity of the coals.

nodes.brief: Within the shadowed courtyard of the bell-founders' guild, a master named Morzan glares at empty tin bins.

exits.label: Approach the primary casting pit to present your metal

nodes.title: The Founders' Courtyard
nodes.page: Empty tin bins clatter slightly in the draft of the shadowed courtyard where a bell-founders' guild master named Morzan stares down into his empty ledger with a furious scowl. The surrounding workshop doors stand half-open, revealing cold hearths and silent benches where desperate artisans huddle in the gloom. Biscuit stamps a hoof against the flagstones, breaking the tense silence of the square. Before the master you stand with the Clapper strapped to your spine, bronze cool against your tired muscles.

nodes.brief: Under the leaking iron roof of the casting shed, a journeyman named Cael scrapes slag from a cold crucible.

exits.label: Approach the master at the primary casting pit
Seek out the exhausted forge-master by the iron crane
Speak with the scarred master beside the grand hearth

nodes.title: The Casting Shed
nodes.page: Flakes of gray slag hiss as a journeyman named Cael scrapes them from the rim of a cold, soot-blackened crucible under the leaking iron roof of the casting shed. Rainwater drips through rusted joints and pools on the cracked concrete floor where discarded molds lie broken in the shadows. The massive weight of the Clapper pulls at your shoulders, its low, comforting hum offering a stark contrast to the dreary silence of the workshop.

nodes.brief: Beside the deep pit of the grand furnace, an old caster named Tormund stirs gray ash with an iron poker.

exits.label: Approach the primary casting pit with your burden
Walk over to the main furnace crane for inspection

nodes.title: The Grand Furnace Pit
nodes.page: Gray ash billows in a sluggish cloud as an old caster named Tormund stirs the cooling embers of the deep furnace pit with a long iron poker. The brickwork radiates a dry, exhausted heat that barely warms the damp chill creeping in from the river-gates. Biscuit lets out a low, weary snort, echoing the heavy metallic sighs of the cooling machinery around you. You shift the Clapper on your back until it sits true, and its familiar pulse taps your shoulder blades.

nodes.brief: Near the cracked stone wall of the mixing floor, a weigh-master named Sula checks empty bronze scales.

exits.label: Step forward to present your bell-metal at the pit
Make your way toward the main furnace crane

nodes.title: The Mixing Floor
nodes.page: Empty bronze scales swing idly in the damp draft near the cracked stone wall of the mixing floor, where a weigh-master named Sula taps her metal stylus against an unwritten tally board. Silence fills the vast chamber except for condensation dripping from the overhead roof trusses. You pause near the entrance so Biscuit can catch his breath, and the Clapper knocks soft against your padded leather frame.

nodes.brief: Along the soot-stained corridor of the forge-masters' office, a clerk named Orin tallies unpaid municipal warrants.

exits.label: Step past the desk toward the inner vestibule

nodes.title: The Forge-Masters' Office
nodes.page: Yellow candlelight flickers over stacks of unpaid municipal warrants across the soot-stained desk where a clerk named Orin runs a ink-stained finger down a long column of debts. Outside the narrow window, the murky river laps against the stone pilings of the foundry quarter in a monotonous rhythm. You hitch the cradle on your back until the bronze tongue sits quiet against the tension of the room.

nodes.brief: Behind the heavy iron doors of the cool-room, an apprentice named Jory guards the last remaining scrap of bell-metal.

exits.label: Present your cracked bell-metal at the casting pit
Enter the soot-choked vestibule to face the clerk

nodes.title: The Cool-Room Doors
nodes.page: Heavy iron bolts secure the frost-rimmed doors of the cool-room, where an apprentice named Jory stands guard over the final remaining scrap of precious bell-metal. His breath fogs in the freezing air spilling from the unheated storage chamber, smelling faintly of old oil and oxidized copper. Biscuit paws impatiently at the frozen puddles on the flagstones, his harness jingling softly in the dim corridor. You hitch the Clapper higher on your back; the metal tongue ticks against the cold like a slow clock.

nodes.brief: Near the smoking ventilation shaft of the lower foundry, a stoker named Fenn shovels wet slack into a hopper.

exits.label: Speak to the grimy stoker
Slip past the roaring furnace

nodes.title: The Stoker's Hopper
nodes.page: Gray soot billows from the ventilation shaft and scrapes your eyes raw as heat from the lower foundry soaks into your wool coat. Fenn heaves a wooden shovel and flings wet slack into the roaring iron hopper; it lands with a dull thud. He wipes black grease from his forehead with a sleeve, then looks at the bronze Clapper in its padded cradle on your back. Something under the floor shakes, and loose bolts rattle in the masonry.

nodes.brief: Beside the flooded drainage trench of the casting floor, a laborer named Krell pumps stale water out with a wooden bilge-pole.

exits.label: Wait for the laborer to finish
Step around the muddy trench

nodes.title: The Bilge-Pole
nodes.page: Sluggish brown water laps against the slippery stone banks of the casting floor as Krell plants his wooden bilge-pole deep into the drainage trench. With a rhythmic grunt, he heaves his weight against the pole, forcing a foul-smelling stream of runoff toward the sluice gates. The damp chill of the river pierces your boots, contrasting sharply with the dry, baked heat radiating from the brickwork nearby. Krell pauses with calloused hands on the wood and eyes the bundle secured to your shoulders with unconcealed curiosity. You can wait for him to finish his grueling work or step around the muddy trench to seek out the master smiths.

nodes.brief: At the threshold of the primary casting pit, Master Morzan demands to see your cracked bell-metal before opening the gate.

exits.label: Press on and present the fragments

nodes.title: The Primary Pit
nodes.page: Iron chains hang from the soot-blackened rafters above the primary casting pit and throw long, wavering shadows across the stone floor. Master Morzan stands with his arms crossed over a leather apron, his sharp gaze fixed upon you as you approach the boundary of his domain. The immense circular pit yawns open like an ancient grave, smelling powerfully of old charcoal, sulfur, and melted slag. He raises a gloved hand and demands to inspect your cracked bell-metal before the iron gates may swing open. You can present the fragments of Orison for his exacting inspection or turn back into the crowded gloom of the passage.

nodes.brief: Beneath the towering iron crane of the main furnace, an exhausted forge-master named Tormund inspects the heavy bronze Clapper on your back.

exits.label: Press on and explain your journey

nodes.title: The Iron Crane
nodes.page: Above the main furnace the great iron crane groans as it holds suspended crucibles and rusted counterweights. Tormund stands near the base of the massive machinery, rubbing a tired hand across his stubbled jaw as he listens to the faint, persistent humming of the bronze Clapper on your back. The furnace fire roars behind him, casting a dull red glow over his scarred face and grease-stained tunic. He gestures toward the heavy load you carry, demanding to know its exact provenance before he allows the work to proceed. You can explain your long mountain journey to the weary master or challenge his authority with a swift demand for entry.

nodes.brief: Inside the soot-choked vestibule of the foundry, a nervous clerk named Orin blocks your path to check your guild permits.

exits.label: Press on and hand over your papers

nodes.title: The Soot-Choked Vestibule
nodes.page: Yellow tallow lamps flicker weakly through the thick haze inside the foundry vestibule, casting dancing shadows across water-stained stone walls. Orin stands behind a rickety desk piled high with grease-spotted manifests, blocking the inner doorway with an ink-stained ledger in his hands. He peers at you over the rim of a pair of wire-rimmed spectacles, demanding to see your official guild permits before allowing a single further step. The air smells of vinegar-cured ink and damp wool, the sort of damp that clings to municipal paper and clerks' sleeves. You can hand over your travel papers for inspection or attempt to brush past the nervous clerk.

nodes.brief: Beside the glowing brickwork of the grand hearth, a scarred master named Vane weighs the desperate terms of your arrival against the empty tin bins.

exits.label: Press on and offer your heavy bronze

nodes.title: The Grand Hearth
nodes.page: Radiant heat rolls in waves from the grand brick hearth and warms your frozen fingers even as the acrid smell of burning coal catches in your throat. Vane stands beside the glowing masonry, a thick leather glove shielding his scarred forearm as he stares angrily into the empty tin bins. His weathered face tightens into a grimace as he compares the desperate urgency of your arrival against the pitiful lack of metal in the stores. He taps a heavy iron poker against the hearthstone, weighing whether your burden is worth the expenditure of his last precious fuel. The bronze Clapper can go under his inspection; the mountain's need can be pressed as a demand for help at once.

nodes.brief: Beside the murky watergate, you find a shivering clerk named Orris trading dry biscuits for news of the upper snows.

exits.label: Trade high mountain news for the key
Leave the clerk to find the blocked carters
Seek the watchman by the damp charcoal crates

nodes.title: The Water-Gate Clerk
nodes.page:
Muck laps against the green slime of the stone watergate where a shivering clerk named Orris hunkers over a brazier of damp peat. He breaks a dry barley biscuit between blue knuckles, offering half in exchange for any word you carry from the white passes above. Old iron and drowned roots rise from the murky river, and an oily grease slides past the moorings to coat the wooden piles.

You can trade the news of the high snows for his dry crust and a key to the toll-wicket, or turn your back on his shivering trade and seek the blocked carters by the silt-choked quay. Alternatively, the watchman among the charcoal crates might offer a safer route away from the rising water.

nodes.brief: In the drowned alleyway, an old cooper named Jael offers you a rusted iron skiff to cross the grey sluice before the tide turns.

exits.privWhy: the reader carries the frostbite scar that marks them as one who crossed the glacier
exits.label: Follow the hidden ledge along the grey rock
Cross the flooded smithy yard to find the skinner
Pay the grease-stained mechanic inside the winch-house

nodes.title: The Drowned Alley Skiff
nodes.page:
Water laps knee-deep through the narrow lane, turning cobblestones into treacherous stepping-stones where an old cooper named Jael sits patching a rusted iron skiff. He gestures with a tar-brush toward the grey, swollen sluice, offering to pole you across before the tide rolls in from the valley mouth and swallows the lower foundations. The air here tastes of stagnant brine and hot scale, and winter still refuses to lock the mud into ice.

You can step into the leaking iron skiff and trust the cooper's pole, or search the flooded smithy yard where a one-eyed skinner might trade for your mule. Another path leads toward the sagging winch-house, where a mechanic waits to demand a toll.

nodes.brief: Under the dripping eaves of the cooperage, a wary apprentice blocks your path to check if your travel papers bear the mountain seal.

exits.label: Present your travel papers to the watchful apprentice
Turn aside to offer clean rags to the desperate mother
Slip past toward the timber lean-to and the exhausted scribe

nodes.title: The Cooperage Guard
nodes.page:
Drips from the sagging cedar eaves patter on the dirt as a wary apprentice steps from the shadow of the cooperage and plants an ash stave across your path. His eyes flick to the bronze Clapper riding upon your back before dropping to demand the official mountain seal stamped upon your parchment travel papers. Damp air smells of fermented oak shavings and vinegar and clings to the wool of your collar.

You can show your stamped papers to pass the guard toward the salt-crusted crane, or turn away to help the desperate mother with her coughing infant. You might also slip past the timber lean-to where the exhausted scribe struggles with ruined ledgers.

nodes.brief: By the silt-choked quay, a group of restless carters argue over blocked towpaths and the rising level of the lowland drainage canal.

exits.label: Wait for the carters to clear the blocked path
Put your back against the stalled wheel to help
Turn back toward the shelter of the narrow alleys

nodes.title: The Silt-Choked Quay
nodes.page:
Heavy wagons sink to their wooden hubs by the grey water's edge, where three carters shout against the roar of the lowland drainage canal bursting its banks. Mud spatters your greaves as the men heave their shoulders against a stalled axle, their breath pluming white in the chill air while the dark tide rises around the rotting pilings.

You can wait for the teamsters to clear the path, offer your broad shoulders to the strain of the wheel, or turn back toward the narrow alleys before the rising waters cut off your retreat entirely.

nodes.brief: Amidst stacked crates of damp charcoal, a tired watchman warns you that the lower sluice gates are groaning under midnight pressure.

exits.label: Answer the watchman with steady patience
Slip silently past into the charcoal shadows
Toss a small copper coin to buy his silence
Warn him of the groaning sluice gates ahead

nodes.title: The Stacked Crates
nodes.page: Cold moisture drips from the sagging cedar eaves, pattering rhythmically against the dirt floor as a tired watchman steps out from behind towering stacks of damp charcoal. He raises a rusted lantern and throws a jaundiced yellow glow across the bronze strapped to your shoulders while the lower sluice gates groan under midnight pressure nearby.

nodes.brief: Your old glacier scar tingles sharply in the damp air, guiding your frost-trained boots along a hidden ledge above the submerged wharf.

exits.label: Follow the elevated stone ledge above the flood
Scramble down to the slippery timbers of the wharf
Pause to test the crumbling mortar beneath your boots

priv.why: the reader carries the frostbite scar that marks them as one who crossed the glacier

nodes.title: The Hidden Ledge
nodes.page:
Old frostbite aches deep within your left shoulder, the jagged scar from the high glacier tingling sharply in the damp lowland air as it guides your frost-trained boots along a hidden stone ledge. Below you, the dark submerged wharf laps against the stone foundations, and the bronze clapper on your back keeps time with your old mountain injuries.

You can follow the elevated ledge above the flood, scramble down to the slippery timbers of the wharf, or pause to test the stability of the crumbling mortar beneath your boots.

nodes.brief: Near the flooded smithy yard, a one-eyed skinner named Bran offers to trade a coil of hemp for your spare mule harness.

exits.label: Trade your spare harness for the coiled hemp
Question the skinner about the rising water levels
Ignore the offer and press on toward the gates
Check the mule's pack before leaving the yard

nodes.title: The Flooded Smithy
nodes.page:
Murky water laps around the anvil block in the flooded smithy yard, where a one-eyed skinner named Bran gestures with a greasy hand toward a coiled hemp rope. He glances nervously at the mule and the padded cradle on your back, offering to trade his dry cordage for your spare harness before the river swallows the rest of his gear.

You can accept the skinner's trade for the stout hemp, question him about the rising water levels upstream, or ignore his desperate offer and press on toward the lower gates.

nodes.brief: Inside a sagging winch-house, a grease-stained mechanic named Taggart demands a toll before letting you turn the drainage crank.

exits.privWhy: the reader owes the Cable Court a toll-debt and is recognised by its collectors
exits.label: Pay the mechanic's toll from your pouch
Argue guild regulations with the surly mechanic

nodes.title: The Sagging Winch-House
nodes.page:
Thick grease coats the heavy iron levers inside the sagging winch-house, where a scowling mechanic named Taggart plants his boots across the threshold and demands a toll before you touch the drainage crank. The air smells of stale oil and river silt, and the rhythmic clanking of the machinery echoes like a heartbeat through the damp floorboards.

You can pay the mechanic's fee from your dwindling pouch, try to outwit him with a sharp word about guild regulations, or look for another way to reach the drainage controls.

nodes.brief: Past the salt-crusted crane, a desperate mother named Milla begs you for clean rags to wrap her coughing infant against the chill.

exits.label: Search your pack for a clean strip of linen
Offer the mother a warming swallow from your flask

exits.privWhy: the Clapper is bare and chipped, and rings or complains in the fog
exits.label: Listen as the bronze clapper hums against the cold

nodes.title: The Salt-Crusted Crane
nodes.page:
Rust flakes from the iron ribs of the salt-crusted crane as a desperate mother named Milla steps from the drizzle, clutching a coughing infant to her chest while begging you for clean rags against the mountain chill. The wind off the water carries the sharp tang of brine and old iron, chilling your fingers inside your thick woollen mittens.

You can search your pack for a clean strip of linen, offer the mother a warming swallow from your flask, or murmur a quiet apology and walk past her into the fog.

nodes.brief: Within a timber lean-to, an exhausted scribe named Hesketh sorts water-ruined ledgers while grease lamps flicker in the drafty dark.

exits.privWhy: the Clapper is bare and chipped, and rings or complains in the fog
exits.label: Listen as the bronze clapper hums its warning
Help the exhausted scribe salvage his water-ruined ledgers

nodes.title: The Water-Ruined Ledgers
nodes.page:
Flickering grease lamps cast long, dancing shadows across water-ruined ledgers inside a drafty timber lean-to, where an exhausted scribe named Hesketh frantically tries to wipe mud from his ink-stained parchment. Outside, rain ticks on the lean-to while the great water-wheel grinds far off, and the clapper on your back knocks softly into the chill.

You can help the scribe salvage his ruined records, ask him about the road ahead toward the foundry, or leave him to his dismal work and step back out into the rain.

nodes.brief: By the silt-banked fountain, a sharp-tongued fishwife named Nessa accuses you of tracking mountain mud onto her drying nets.

exits.label: Offer a polite apology to the angry fishwife
Step carefully around her drying nets to avoid trouble

nodes.title: The Silt-Banked Fountain
nodes.page:
Murky water overflows the stone basin of the silt-banked fountain, where a sharp-tongued fishwife named Nessa scrubs her wooden tubs and glares fiercely at the mud tracking from your boots onto her drying nets. Gulls wheel overhead in the grey sky, crying out against the rising wind that sweeps up from the lowlands.

You can offer a polite apology to the fishwife, step carefully around her nets to avoid further trouble, or ask her if the lower bridge is still passable.

nodes.brief: Under the creaking arch of the sluice bridge, a nervous boy named Kray drops his bundle of iron spikes into the murky depths.

exits.label: Reach into the murky water to help retrieve the spikes
Offer the boy a word of comfort and hurry across

nodes.title: The Sluice Bridge Arch
nodes.page:
Timbers groan under the weight of the water as you step beneath the creaking arch of the sluice bridge, where a nervous boy named Kray drops his bundle of iron spikes into the murky depths with a dull splash. He looks up at you with wide, frightened eyes, his fingers clutching uselessly at his wet leather apron.

You can reach into the water to help the boy retrieve his spikes, offer him a word of comfort about the rising flood, or hurry across the bridge before the timbers give way.

nodes.brief: In a narrow alley smelling of coal smoke, an old bailiff named Vane blocks your way to inspect the wooden cradle on your back.

exits.label: Allow the bailiff to inspect the wooden cradle
Demand to know his authority for stopping travellers

nodes.title: The Narrow Coal Alley
